dataset_status: Phase 4 reconciled generated explanations with the authorized Phase 8D edits applied
quality_note: AI-generated learning aids. Batch-level AI semantic reviews and a comprehensive structural audit are documented. The entire set has not been independently verified by a human native speaker.
privacy_scope: No Anki note/card IDs, standalone original card example fields, live field snapshots, scheduling values, rollback records, or collection backup packages are included.

records.nuance: それ refers to something near the listener or something already mentioned. Here it points back to the story being discussed. It stands on its own as a pronoun.
records.logic: The shared situation or conversation identifies the thing, so それ can refer to it without repeating its name.
records.meaning: that; that one; the thing just mentioned
records.difference: これ usually points to something near the speaker; それ to something near the listener or already mentioned; あれ to something away from both. その needs a following noun, while それ stands alone.
records.filipino: iyan; ang bagay na iyan; ang nabanggit na iyon

records.nuance: 一（いち） is the basic number one. In 一から始める, it means starting from the first step or the beginning.
records.logic: One is the first point in a numbered sequence, so starting 一から suggests starting at the beginning.
records.meaning: one; in 一から, from the beginning
records.difference: 一（いち） is the basic numeral. 一つ（ひとつ） counts one thing with the general native counting form.
records.filipino: isa; sa pangungusap na ito, mula sa simula

records.nuance: 二（に） gives the number two. With 回, which counts occurrences, 二回 means twice. Here the speaker has met that person twice.
records.logic: 二 supplies the quantity; 回 tells us that the quantity counts occasions rather than objects.
records.meaning: two; 二回 = twice / two times
records.difference: 二（に） is the basic numeral. 二つ（ふたつ） counts two things with the general native counting form.

records.nuance: 三（さん） is the number three. 三人（さんにん） counts three people; here it describes the mother's three children.
records.logic: 三 supplies the number, while 人 identifies the counted group as people.
records.difference: 三（さん） is the basic numeral. 三つ（みっつ） counts three things with the general native counting form.

records.nuance: し is the reading of 四 in established combinations such as 四月（しがつ）, April. よん is the usual basic counting form, but it does not replace し in 四月.
records.logic: 四月 names the fourth month of the calendar, so its meaning is April. Its established reading is しがつ.
records.difference: 四（よん） has the same numerical value and is common in counting. Readings depend on the combination: 四月 is しがつ, while 四回 is よんかい.

records.nuance: これ points to something close to the speaker, physically or in the current context. In これをください, the speaker selects the item they want. It stands alone as a pronoun.
records.logic: The speaker points out an identifiable item, so これ replaces its name.
records.difference: これ stands alone, while この needs a noun: この本 = this book. それ usually points to something near the listener or something already mentioned.

records.nuance: よん is the usual basic counting form of 四. 四回目（よんかいめ） means the fourth time; here it is the speaker's fourth visit to Hawaii.
records.logic: 四 gives the number, 回 counts occurrences, and 目 marks position in the sequence: the fourth occurrence.
records.meaning: four; 四回目 = the fourth time
records.difference: 四（し） has the same value but appears in combinations such as 四月（しがつ）, April. 四回 uses よん, not し.
records.filipino: apat; 四回目 = ikaapat na beses

records.nuance: 五（ご） is the number five. 五人（ごにん） means five people; 五人で describes doing something as a group of five. The Japanese does not specify whether the speaker is one of them; “of us” is the English translation’s interpretation.
records.logic: 五 gives the group size, and 人 specifies that the count is of people.
records.difference: 五（ご） is the basic numeral. 五つ（いつつ） counts five things with the general native counting form.

records.nuance: 六（ろく） is the number six. 六人（ろくにん） counts six people; here it tells us how many children he has.
records.logic: 六 supplies the quantity, and 人 makes it a count of people.
records.difference: 六（ろく） is the basic numeral. 六つ（むっつ） counts six things with the general native counting form.
records.filipino: anim; 六人 = anim na tao

records.nuance: なな is the usual basic counting form of 七. In 七本（ななほん）, 本 counts long, slender objects, including the bananas in this sentence.
records.logic: 七 gives the quantity; 本 tells us which shape-based counter is being used, rather than adding the meaning 'book'.
records.meaning: seven; 七本 = seven long or slender items
records.difference: 七（しち） also means seven. The reading depends on the combination: 七月 is しちがつ, while ななほん is a natural reading of 七本.
records.filipino: pito; sa pangungusap na ito, pitong saging

records.nuance: 八（はち） is the number eight. 八個 counts eight individual items; here the items are apples. In 八個, はちこ and はっこ are both accepted readings; the exact Vocabulary-Kana reading for the target 八 remains はち.
records.logic: 八 gives the number, and 個 counts the apples as individual units.
records.difference: 八（はち） is the basic numeral. 八つ（やっつ） is the general native form for eight things.
records.filipino: walo; sa pangungusap na ito, walong mansanas

records.nuance: きゅう is the usual basic counting form of 九. 九人（きゅうにん） means nine people; here it gives the number of players on one baseball team.
records.logic: 九 supplies the team size, while 人 specifies that the count is of people.
records.difference: 九（く） has the same value but is used in combinations such as 九時（くじ）, nine o'clock. 九人 uses きゅうにん.
records.filipino: siyam; 九人 = siyam na tao

records.kanji_breakdown:
九 = nine
つ = general native counting suffix (not a kanji)
records.nuance: 九つ（ここのつ） counts nine things and can also describe a young child's age. Here 娘は明日九つになります means that the daughter turns nine tomorrow.
records.logic: The native counting form gives a count of nine. In an age context, 九つになる means reaching the age of nine.
records.meaning: nine things; nine years old when used for a child's age
records.difference: 九歳（きゅうさい） explicitly counts years of age. 九つ can express a young child's age without 歳, with the context identifying what is counted.
records.filipino: siyam na bagay; sa pangungusap na ito, siyam na taong gulang

records.nuance: 十（じゅう） is the number ten. In this sentence, the child uses their fingers to count to ten.
records.logic: 十 is the endpoint of this count. It also forms the tens unit in numbers such as 二十（にじゅう）, two tens or twenty.
records.difference: 十（じゅう） is the basic numeral. 十（とお） is the native counting form for ten things; unlike 一つ through 九つ, it has no final つ.

records.nuance: 百（ひゃく） is one hundred and also serves as the hundreds unit in larger numbers. Here 百才 means one hundred years old.
records.logic: 百 supplies the quantity of one hundred. The following age counter 才, also written 歳, identifies that quantity as years of age.
records.difference: 百（ひゃく） is 100, while 千（せん） is 1,000. Some compounds change the sound of 百, as in 三百（さんびゃく）.
records.filipino: isang daan; sa pangungusap na ito, isang daang taong gulang

records.nuance: 千（せん） is one thousand and serves as the thousands unit in larger numbers. 千円（せんえん） means one thousand yen.
records.logic: 千 supplies a group of a thousand; 円 makes that quantity an amount of money in yen.
records.difference: 千（せん） is 1,000, while 万（まん） is 10,000. Some compounds change the sound of 千, as in 三千（さんぜん）.
records.filipino: isang libo; 千円 = isang libong yen

records.nuance: 万（まん） is the ten-thousand unit used in Japanese numbers. 一万（いちまん） or 1万 means ten thousand; here it is the price in yen.
records.logic: Japanese large numbers use groups of ten thousand. One 万 is ten 千, so 1万円 is ten thousand yen.
records.difference: 千（せん） is 1,000; 万（まん） is 10,000. Thus 二万（にまん） means 20,000, not 2,000.
records.filipino: sampung libo; 1万円 = sampung libong yen

records.nuance: 時（とき） can refer to time itself or to a particular time or occasion. In 時の経つのは早い, it refers to the flow of time: time passes quickly.
records.logic: The central idea is time as something that passes or as a point when something happens. This sentence uses the passing-time sense.
records.meaning: time; a time or occasion, depending on context
records.difference: 時間（じかん） often emphasizes an amount or period of time. 時（とき） can point to an occasion or to time generally. 時 read じ is used for clock hours, as in 三時.
records.filipino: oras; panahon; dito, mabilis lumipas ang panahon

records.nuance: する is a general verb for doing an action or activity. Here 宿題をした means 'did homework'. In this use, it is transitive: を marks the activity being done. It is irregular; した is its past form.
records.logic: 宿題 names the activity, and する expresses carrying it out: the task is named first, then the verb says it is done.
records.meaning: do; perform; carry out an activity
records.difference: やる can also mean doing an activity and often sounds more casual. する is a neutral choice. Both have other uses, so they are not interchangeable in every context.
records.filipino: gawin; 宿題をする = gawin ang takdang-aralin

records.nuance: 日（にち） is used as a day suffix in many dates and day counts. In 11日（じゅういちにち）, it identifies the eleventh day of the month, not an eleven-day duration.
records.logic: The number identifies a position on the calendar, and 日 specifies that the position is a day within the month.
records.meaning: day; a suffix used in dates and counts of days
records.difference: 日（ひ） is a standalone word for a day or the sun. にち is used in many compounds. Some dates have special readings, such as 二日（ふつか）, so not every date uses にち.
records.filipino: araw; sa petsang 11日, ika-11 ng buwan

records.nuance: 六日（むいか） can mean six days or the sixth day of a month. In 六日前, it measures a six-day interval before now: six days ago.
records.logic: Six day-units make up the interval. 前 places it before the reference time. Learn むいか as the established reading of the whole word.
records.meaning: six days; the sixth of the month; here 六日前 = six days ago
records.difference: 六日間（むいかかん） explicitly marks a duration of six days. 六日 alone can be a duration or a calendar date, depending on context.
records.filipino: anim na araw; ika-6 ng buwan; 六日前 = anim na araw ang nakalipas

records.nuance: 三日（みっか） can mean three days or the third day of a month. Here 三日かかりました describes the three days needed for the letter to arrive.
records.logic: Three day-units measure the elapsed time. With かかる, the sentence states how much time something takes, so this is a duration.
records.meaning: three days; the third of the month; here, a duration of three days
records.difference: 三日間（みっかかん） makes the three-day duration explicit. 三日 alone can express either a duration or a date.
records.filipino: tatlong araw; ika-3 ng buwan; dito, inabot ng tatlong araw

records.nuance: 五日（いつか） can mean five days or the fifth day of a month. Here 五月五日 is May fifth, so it names a calendar date.
records.logic: The month sets the calendar context, and 五日 identifies its fifth day. Learn いつか as the established reading, rather than combining ご and にち.
records.meaning: five days; the fifth of the month; here, May 5th
records.difference: 五日（いつか） is a specific day count or date. いつか meaning 'someday' refers to an unspecified time; the pronunciation is the same.
records.filipino: limang araw; ika-5 ng buwan; 五月五日 = ika-5 ng Mayo

records.nuance: 八日（ようか） can mean eight days or the eighth day of a month. Here 八日から marks the eighth as the starting date for the trip.
records.logic: 八日 identifies a numbered calendar day, and から makes that date the starting point. The whole word has the established reading ようか.
records.meaning: eight days; the eighth of the month; here, the eighth
records.difference: 八日（ようか） is the eighth or eight days. 四日（よっか） is the fourth or four days. Keep the long よう sound distinct from よっ.
records.filipino: walong araw; ika-8 ng buwan; 八日から = mula sa ika-8 ng buwan

records.nuance: 二日（ふつか） can mean two days or the second day of a month. In 二日待った, it tells us how long the speaker waited: two days.
records.logic: Two day-units measure the waiting interval. The verb's context makes this a duration rather than a date.
records.meaning: two days; the second of the month; here, a duration of two days
records.difference: 二日間（ふつかかん） explicitly marks a two-day duration. 二日 alone can also name the second day of a month.
records.filipino: dalawang araw; ika-2 ng buwan; dito, naghintay ng dalawang araw

records.nuance: 九日（ここのか） can mean nine days or the ninth day of a month. Here 九日に specifies the date when the package will arrive: the ninth.
records.logic: The number identifies a day within the month. The delivery context makes this a calendar date; learn ここのか as the whole-word reading.
records.meaning: nine days; the ninth of the month; here, on the ninth
records.difference: 九日間（ここのかかん） explicitly marks a nine-day duration. 九つ（ここのつ） counts nine things, not days.
records.filipino: siyam na araw; ika-9 ng buwan; dito, sa ika-9

records.nuance: ところ refers to a place or location associated with the situation. After a word referring to a person, it can mean their place. Here 友達のところ is the friend's home or place where the speaker stayed.
records.logic: The person identifies which place is meant, so 友達のところ can name the friend's place without specifying the building.
records.meaning: place; location; someone's place or home in this context
records.difference: 場所（ばしょ） names a location directly. 人のところ is a natural way to refer to someone's place. ところ also has grammatical uses beyond physical places.
records.filipino: lugar; 友達のところ = sa bahay ng kaibigan

records.nuance: 十日（とおか） can mean ten days or the tenth day of a month. In 十日後, it measures an interval ending ten days later; here the speaker will return in ten days.
records.logic: Ten day-units form the interval, and 後 places the return after that interval. Learn とおか as the established reading.
records.meaning: ten days; the tenth of the month; 十日後 = ten days later / in ten days
records.difference: 十日間（とおかかん） explicitly expresses a ten-day duration. 十日後 points to the time after ten days have elapsed.
records.filipino: sampung araw; ika-10 ng buwan; 十日後 = pagkalipas ng sampung araw

records.nuance: 七日（なのか） can mean seven days or the seventh day of a month. In modern Tokyo usage, なのか is the usual reading; なぬか remains in use, especially in Kansai and older texts. Here 先月の七日 names the seventh of last month.
records.logic: The specified month sets the calendar context, and 七日 identifies its seventh day. The complete word has the established reading なのか.
records.meaning: seven days; the seventh of the month; here, the seventh
records.difference: 七日間（なのかかん） makes a seven-day duration explicit. なぬか is another reading of 七日, especially in regional or older usage; retain なのか for this card.
records.filipino: pitong araw; ika-7 ng buwan; dito, noong ika-7 ng nakaraang buwan

records.nuance: 四日（よっか） can mean four days or the fourth day of a month. Here 来月の四日から marks the fourth of next month as the start of the school term.
records.logic: The month identifies the calendar, and 四日 names its fourth day. から marks that date as the starting point.
records.meaning: four days; the fourth of the month; here, the fourth
records.difference: 四日（よっか） has a doubled consonant and means four days or the fourth. 八日（ようか） has a long vowel and means eight days or the eighth.
records.filipino: apat na araw; ika-4 ng buwan; dito, mula sa ika-4 ng susunod na buwan

records.nuance: 月（つき） refers to the moon in this sentence: it looks beautiful tonight. The same word can also mean a month in other contexts.
records.logic: The sky and 今夜 identify the moon sense. Although 月 also appears in calendar words, the complete sentence determines which meaning is intended.
records.meaning: moon; also month in other uses; here, the moon
records.difference: 月（がつ） is the suffix for named months, as in 四月. 月（げつ） occurs in compounds such as 月曜日. This card's standalone reading is つき.
records.filipino: buwan; dito, ang buwan sa langit

records.nuance: 水（みず） is water. In everyday drinking contexts, it usually means cool or room-temperature water. Here 水を一杯 asks for a glass or cup of water.
records.logic: 水 names the substance, and 一杯 counts one containerful. The word itself does not specify the container.
records.difference: お湯（おゆ） is hot water. お水（おみず） is a polite everyday way to say water; 水 also has a broader substance meaning beyond this temperature contrast.
records.filipino: tubig; 水を一杯 = isang basong tubig

records.nuance: 金（かね） means money here. 金がかかる describes something costing money. 金 alone can sound blunt in conversation; お金（おかね） is the more usual neutral everyday wording.
records.logic: In this established money sense, 金 names the funds needed or spent. かかる expresses the cost; the sentence is about an expense.
records.meaning: money; 金がかかる = cost money
records.difference: お金（おかね） refers to the same money with a more courteous everyday tone. 金（きん） means gold in material contexts; it is a different reading and sense.

records.kanji_breakdown:
日 = sun / day
曜 = weekday
日 = day
records.nuance: 日曜日（にちようび） is Sunday. It identifies a day in the weekly cycle. Here は makes Sunday the time topic for the seaside trip.
records.logic: The weekday name is associated with the sun. 曜日 marks a named day of the week; the final 日 is read び in this word.
records.difference: 休日（きゅうじつ） is a day off or holiday, which need not be Sunday. 日曜（にちよう） is the shorter form of 日曜日.

records.kanji_breakdown:
土 = earth / soil
曜 = weekday
日 = day
records.nuance: 土曜日（どようび） is Saturday. Here 土曜日の夜 specifies Saturday night for going to a club. 行きます can describe a plan or a habit, depending on context.
records.logic: The weekday name is associated with Saturn, 土星（どせい）. 土 identifies that weekday, while 曜日 marks the named day of the week.
records.difference: 土曜（どよう） is the shorter form for the same day. 週末（しゅうまつ） means the weekend more broadly.
records.filipino: Sabado; 土曜日の夜 = Sabado ng gabi

records.kanji_breakdown:
金 = gold / metal
曜 = weekday
日 = day
records.nuance: 金曜日（きんようび） is Friday. It names the day of the week; here 金曜日の夜 sets the time for going out with friends.
records.logic: The weekday name is associated with Venus, 金星（きんせい）. 金 identifies this weekday within the fixed 曜日 naming pattern.
records.difference: 金（かね） can mean money, but 金曜日 is the fixed weekday name Friday. 金曜（きんよう） is its shorter form.
records.filipino: Biyernes; 金曜日の夜 = Biyernes ng gabi

records.kanji_breakdown:
月 = moon / month
曜 = weekday
日 = day
records.nuance: 月曜日（げつようび） is Monday. In this invitation, に marks Monday as the proposed meeting day.
records.logic: The weekday name is associated with the moon. 月 identifies Monday within the fixed 曜日 naming pattern, rather than counting a month.
records.difference: 月（つき） can mean the moon or a month, while 月曜日 uses げつ. 月曜（げつよう） is the shorter form for Monday.
records.filipino: Lunes; 月曜日に = sa Lunes

records.kanji_breakdown:
火 = fire
曜 = weekday
日 = day
records.nuance: 火曜日（かようび） is Tuesday. Here it identifies the day when a meeting takes place; に marks that time.
records.logic: The weekday name is associated with Mars, 火星（かせい）. 火 identifies Tuesday within the fixed 曜日 naming pattern.
records.difference: 火曜（かよう） is the shorter form of 火曜日 and names the same day.
records.filipino: Martes; 火曜日に = sa Martes

records.kanji_breakdown:
水 = water
曜 = weekday
日 = day
records.nuance: 水曜日（すいようび） is Wednesday. Here は makes Wednesday the time topic for the speaker's part-time work.
records.logic: The weekday name is associated with Mercury, 水星（すいせい）. 水 identifies Wednesday within the fixed 曜日 naming pattern.
records.difference: 水（みず） is the standalone word for water, while 水曜日 uses すい. 水曜（すいよう） is the shorter form for Wednesday.

records.nuance: 週（しゅう） is a week, either as a calendar period or a seven-day unit. Here その次の週 refers to the week following the one already being discussed.
records.logic: The reference week establishes a position in the calendar sequence. 次 moves to the following week.
records.difference: 週 refers to a week. 曜日（ようび） identifies a day of the week, such as Monday. 一週間（いっしゅうかん） explicitly names a one-week interval.
records.filipino: linggo; その次の週 = ang kasunod na linggo

records.nuance: 年（とし） can refer to a year or to age. In 新しい年が始まりました, it means a new calendar year; it does not describe someone's age.
records.logic: A year is a recurring calendar cycle. 新しい and 始まる present the start of the next cycle.
records.meaning: year; age in other contexts; here, a calendar year
records.difference: 年（ねん） is used in year numbers and counts, such as 一年（いちねん）. This note uses the standalone reading とし.
records.filipino: taon; edad sa ibang gamit; 新しい年 = bagong taon

records.nuance: 分かる（わかる） means understanding something or having it become clear. It is generally intransitive; what is understood commonly takes が or is the topic with は. Here the question asks whether the meaning was understood.
records.logic: The central idea is clarity: when the meaning is understood, it becomes clear. Here, the speaker asks whether the listener understood the question's meaning.
records.meaning: understand; know or realize something as it becomes clear
records.difference: 知る（しる） often means finding out; 知っている describes knowing a fact. 分かる emphasizes understanding or clarity, though their uses can overlap.

records.nuance: そう refers to a manner, situation, or idea already understood from context. In 私もそう思います, it points to the opinion just mentioned: 'I think so too.'
records.logic: The earlier opinion supplies the content, and そう refers back to it instead of repeating the whole idea.
records.meaning: that way; so; in that manner
records.difference: そう commonly refers back to the other person's words or a mentioned idea. こう means 'this way', often with a manner being shown or described by the speaker.
records.filipino: ganoon; 私もそう思います = ganoon din ang iniisip ko

records.nuance: 何（なに） asks for the identity or content of something unknown. In 何を食べたいですか, it asks which food the listener wants to eat.
records.logic: An item is left unspecified, and 何 asks the listener to supply it. を marks it as the object of 食べる.
records.difference: 何 also has the standard reading なん in combinations such as 何ですか and 何時. どれ asks 'which one' from an identifiable set. This card uses なに.
records.filipino: ano; 何を食べたいですか = ano ang gusto mong kainin?

records.nuance: 先（さき） can mean ahead in space or earlier in an order. In お先にどうぞ, it politely lets the other person go or act first: 'Please go ahead.'
records.logic: The other person is given the earlier position in the sequence, so 先に expresses acting before someone else.
records.meaning: ahead; before; first; tip or end in other contexts
records.difference: 前（まえ） often names a position in front or a time before something. 先（さき） often emphasizes being ahead in a sequence or moving beyond a reference point; their meanings can overlap.
records.filipino: una; unahan; お先にどうぞ = mauna ka na po

records.kanji_breakdown:
今 = now / current
年 = year
records.nuance: 今年（ことし） is the current calendar year. Here it gives the time frame for the speaker's wish to travel to Italy.
records.logic: 今 selects the year containing the present time, and 年 supplies the calendar unit. Learn ことし as the established everyday reading of the whole word.
records.difference: 来年（らいねん） is next year, while 去年（きょねん） is last year. 今年 is tied to the year in which the speaker is speaking.

records.nuance: 今（いま） is the present moment or current time. In this sentence, it locates the ongoing studying at the time of speaking.
records.logic: 今 sets the time reference to the present, and 勉強しています describes the activity continuing at that time.
records.difference: 今日（きょう） means today, covering the current day. 今 focuses more closely on the present time, although its scope can widen with context.

records.kanji_breakdown:
今 = now / current
日 = day
records.nuance: 今日（きょう） is today, the calendar day containing the present moment. Here it specifies that the speaker has no work today. きょう is the usual everyday reading for this meaning.
records.logic: The current day is identified as a whole time unit. The spelling expresses that concept, but きょう is learned as the complete word's established reading.
records.difference: 今（いま） means now. 今日 read こんにち is more formal and can also mean 'nowadays'; retain きょう for this everyday sentence.
records.filipino: ngayong araw; sa araw na ito

records.kanji_breakdown:
今 = now / current
週 = week
records.nuance: 今週（こんしゅう） is the current week. Here it places the Japanese test within that calendar week, without specifying the particular day.
records.logic: 今 selects the week containing the present time, and 週 identifies the seven-day calendar unit.
records.difference: 来週（らいしゅう） is next week; 先週（せんしゅう） is last week. 今週 is a calendar reference, while 一週間（いっしゅうかん） can measure a one-week interval.

records.nuance: 来る（くる） is an intransitive verb for movement toward the speaker or a location treated as the reference point. Here he will come after noon, around early afternoon; 昼過ぎ does not specifically mean after eating lunch. It is irregular: the polite form is 来ます（きます）, and the negative is 来ない（こない）.
records.logic: The movement approaches the chosen reference point. The person moving is the subject, rather than an object being acted on.
records.meaning: come; arrive toward the relevant reference point
records.difference: 行く（いく） usually describes going away from the reference point. 来る uses the approaching viewpoint; the choice depends on the situation.
records.filipino: dumating; pumunta rito; dito, darating siya pagkalampas ng tanghali

records.kanji_breakdown:
来 = come / next
年 = year
records.nuance: 来年（らいねん） means the calendar year after the present one. Here it sets when the speaker suggests traveling together.
records.logic: The reference point is this year; 来年 names the next calendar year in that sequence. Learn the compound reading らいねん as a whole.
records.difference: 今年（ことし） is this year; 来年（らいねん） is the following calendar year.
records.filipino: sa susunod na taon; sa susunod na taon, sabay tayong maglakbay

records.nuance: 行く（いく） describes going to another place, generally viewed as movement away from the speaker's or current reference point. It can also describe visiting or attending a place. The polite nonpast 行きます can describe habits or future plans, depending on context.
records.logic: 行く describes movement to a destination. 図書館に identifies that destination. The nonpast form alone does not determine whether the visit is habitual or planned.
records.difference: 行く（いく） views movement toward a destination; 来る（くる） views it as movement toward the speaker or another reference point.
records.filipino: pumunta; pumupunta sa aklatan tuwing Linggo

records.nuance: 帰る（かえる） is to return to a home or other place treated as one’s base. 家に帰ろう is a suggestion: “Let’s go home.”
records.logic: The destination is presented as the place one is returning to, rather than simply any place one is going.
records.meaning: return; go home; go back to one’s base
records.difference: 行く（いく） simply describes going to a destination; 帰る（かえる） emphasizes returning to one’s home or base.

records.nuance: 大きい（おおきい） describes something large in size. Here it describes the building the speaker points out. Before a noun, 大きな is also possible.
records.logic: The adjective marks the building as large relative to the context; the question asks what that building is.
records.difference: 小さい（ちいさい） means small. 大きい and 小さい are い-adjectives; 大きな and 小さな can also modify nouns directly.

records.nuance: 小さい（ちいさい） describes small physical size. Here it describes the flowers that are blooming, not their number.
records.logic: The adjective applies to each flower’s size; 花が咲いています says that the flowers are blooming.
records.difference: 大きい（おおきい） means large. 小さい／小さな and 大きい／大きな can both appear before nouns.

records.nuance: 少ない（すくない） describes an amount or number that is low. 今年は雨が少ない means this year has had little rain.
records.logic: The amount of rain is presented as below what the context expects or compares it with; 少ない evaluates quantity, not the size of raindrops.
records.difference: 多い（おおい） means many or much. 少ない describes a low amount; 少し（すこし） often means a small amount or degree, as in 少し疲れました.
records.filipino: kaunti; kaunti ang ulan ngayong taon

records.nuance: 少し（すこし） softens the degree: the speaker is somewhat tired, not necessarily very tired. It can also mean a small quantity or a short time in other contexts.
records.logic: 少し limits the degree of 疲れました; it answers “how tired?” rather than counting objects.
records.meaning: a little; slightly; a short while in other contexts
records.difference: 少ない（すくない） describes a low count or amount; 少し（すこし） can modify a state or action to indicate a small degree or amount.

records.nuance: 多い（おおい） describes a high number or amount. The sentence says Kyoto has many temples; it does not mean the temples themselves are large.
records.logic: お寺が多い evaluates the number of temples in Kyoto, with が marking what is numerous.
records.difference: 少ない（すくない） means few or little. 多い describes a high number or amount, not large physical size.

records.nuance: 上げる（あげる） means to raise or put something up. Here 荷物をあみだなに上げた means he placed the luggage on the overhead rack; を marks what he moved.
records.logic: The luggage is moved to a higher supporting place. In this sentence 上げる is transitive: the person acts on the luggage.
records.meaning: raise; lift; put up / place on a higher level
records.difference: 上がる（あがる） describes something rising or going up; 上げる（あげる） describes someone raising or putting something up.
records.filipino: itaas; inilagay niya sa lagayan sa itaas ang mga bagahe

records.nuance: 上（うえ） means above or upward. In 上を向いて, it describes the direction to face or look.
records.logic: The head or gaze is oriented toward a higher direction; を marks the direction followed by 向く.
records.difference: 下（した） is below or underneath; 上（うえ） points to the higher side or an upward direction.

records.nuance: 下（した） means below or underneath. 机の下にあった locates the wallet beneath the desk.
records.logic: The desk serves as the reference point; the wallet is in the space on its lower side.
records.difference: 上（うえ） is above or on the upper side; 下（した） is below or on the lower side.
records.filipino: ilalim; nasa ilalim ng mesa ang pitaka

records.nuance: 右（みぎ） is the right-hand side relative to a person or direction of orientation. Here it specifies which pocket holds the handkerchief.
records.logic: Right and left distinguish the two sides of the same orientation. The Japanese does not state who owns the pocket; the deck English supplies “my.”
records.difference: 左（ひだり） is the opposite side from 右（みぎ） when using the same orientation.
records.filipino: kanan; nasa kanang bulsa ang panyo (the English translation specifies “my” pocket)

records.nuance: 左（ひだり） is the left-hand side relative to the direction one faces. そこを左に曲がってください asks the listener to turn left at that point.
records.logic: The place そこ is the turning point; 左に gives the direction of the turn.
records.difference: 右（みぎ） is the opposite side from 左（ひだり） when using the same orientation.

records.nuance: 方（ほう） can mean a direction or side. In 私の方, it means “my direction / toward me,” which is what he looked toward.
records.logic: 私 identifies the reference side; 方 presents that person as a direction or side rather than naming a physical compass point.
records.meaning: direction; side; in 私の方, my direction / toward me
records.difference: 方（ほう） means direction or side here. 方（かた） can be a polite way to refer to a person; retain this card’s reading ほう.
records.filipino: direksyon; sa aking direksyon; tumingin siya sa akin

records.nuance: 人（ひと） means a person. In 優しい人, it refers to someone kind or gentle; the adjective supplies the positive quality.
records.logic: 優しい describes the person rather than changing the meaning of 人 itself.
records.meaning: person; here, a kind / gentle person
records.difference: 人（ひと） is the ordinary word for a person. 方（かた） can refer politely to a person, while 方（ほう） means a direction or side.

records.kanji_breakdown: どう = how; what (in opinion questions)
records.nuance: どう（どう） asks how something is or what someone thinks of it. あなたはどう思いますか asks for the listener’s opinion: “What do you think?”
records.logic: どう leaves the manner, evaluation, or opinion open for the listener to provide.
records.meaning: how; what do you think? in an opinion question
records.difference: どう asks for an evaluation or manner; 何（なに／なん） asks what thing or content is meant.
records.filipino: ano sa palagay mo?; ano ang tingin mo?

records.nuance: 入れる（いれる） is transitive: someone puts an item inside a container. Here 手帳 is put into the bag; かばんに marks where it goes.
records.logic: The speaker describes an agent moving an object across the bag’s boundary into its inside.
records.difference: 入る（はいる） is intransitive: a person or thing enters. 入れる（いれる） means someone puts an item in.
records.filipino: ilagay sa loob; ipinasok niya sa bag ang planner

records.nuance: 入る（はいる） describes a person or thing entering a place. Here 中に入ってください invites the listener to come inside because it is cold.
records.logic: The person moves across the boundary into the inside area; the sentence does not say someone else puts them there.
records.difference: 入る（はいる） describes entering; 入れる（いれる） describes someone putting an object inside. Their readings and transitivity differ.
records.filipino: pumasok; pumasok po kayo sa loob

records.nuance: 出る（でる） means to leave or come out. 今朝は早く家を出ました says the speaker left home early this morning. Here を marks the place left, not an object being taken.
records.logic: The person moves from inside the house to outside it. 出る focuses on the person’s departure.
records.difference: 出る（でる） describes a person or thing going out; 出す（だす） describes someone taking or bringing an object out.
records.filipino: umalis; umalis ako nang maaga sa bahay kaninang umaga

records.kanji_breakdown: できる = be able to; can do
records.nuance: できる（できる） expresses ability or competence. With a language plus が, as in イタリア語ができます, it means she can use or speak Italian; it does not specify her proficiency level.
records.logic: The ability is associated with Italian as the skill area. Here が marks the language skill she has.
records.meaning: be able to; can do; know / be able to use a language
records.difference: できる describes ability in a language broadly. 分かる（わかる） focuses on understanding it; 話せる（はなせる） specifically says one can speak it.
records.filipino: marunong gumamit o magsalita ng Italyano; kaya niyang mag-Italyano

records.nuance: 出す（だす） is transitive: someone takes or brings an object out of somewhere. Here he removes the textbook from his bag; から marks its source.
records.logic: The person causes the textbook to move from inside the bag to outside it; the object is marked with を.
records.meaning: take out; bring out; send out in other contexts
records.difference: 出る（でる） is intransitive, as when a person leaves. 出す（だす） is transitive, as when someone takes an object out.
records.filipino: ilabas; inilabas niya sa bag ang aklat

records.nuance: 本（ほん） means a book here. 一冊 is the counter form used for one book; the counter clarifies quantity, not the reading of 本.
records.logic: 本 names the item bought; 一冊 counts one bound volume.
records.difference: 本 is the book itself; 冊（さつ） is the counter used when counting books and other bound volumes.
records.filipino: aklat; bumili ako ng isang aklat

records.nuance: 休む（やすむ） means to rest or be absent from work or school. 会社を休みます means taking the day off from work; を marks the workplace one is absent from here.
records.logic: The person intentionally pauses their usual work attendance. 明日 sets the day off as tomorrow.
records.meaning: rest; take time off; be absent from work / school
records.difference: 休む can mean taking time away from work or resting generally. 休憩する（きゅうけいする） more specifically means take a break.
records.filipino: magpahinga; hindi papasok sa trabaho bukas

records.nuance: 体（からだ） means the body and can also refer to physical health. 体が丈夫だ describes a robust, healthy constitution; the deck translation “physically strong” is close, though the Japanese also suggests sound health.
records.logic: 丈夫 describes the body as resilient or in good condition, rather than saying the person is strong in every possible sense.
records.meaning: body; physical health / constitution in context
records.difference: 体（からだ） is the everyday word for body. 身体（しんたい） is a more formal or technical term for the body.
records.filipino: katawan; malusog at malakas ang pangangatawan

records.nuance: 目（め） means eye. 青い目をしています is the Japanese expression for having blue eyes; English naturally uses the plural “eyes.”
records.logic: 青い describes the eye colour, and 目をしています describes the person’s visible eye appearance.
records.meaning: eye; eyes in 青い目をしています
records.difference: 目（め） is an eye generally; 瞳（ひとみ） more specifically refers to the pupil or the visible colored part of the eye.
records.filipino: mata; asul ang mga mata niya

records.nuance: どこ asks for a place. Here it asks where the book was put; the Japanese leaves the person who put it there unstated, while English supplies “you.”
records.logic: The place remains unknown, and どこ asks the listener to identify it. に marks the place where the book was put.
records.difference: どこ asks where. どちら can also ask which direction or place and often sounds more polite.
records.filipino: saan; saan inilagay ang librong iyon?

records.nuance: 口（くち） means the mouth. 口を大きく開けてください asks someone to open their mouth wide; 大きく describes how wide.
records.logic: The mouth is the part being opened; を marks it as the object of 開ける.
records.difference: 口（くち） is the mouth or an opening; 唇（くちびる） means the lips specifically.
records.filipino: bibig; ibuka nang malaki ang bibig, pakiusap

records.nuance: 耳（みみ） is the ear. Here 耳がよく聞こえません means her hearing is not very good; よく聞こえる is about hearing well.
records.logic: The sentence describes how well sound can be heard, not a problem with the ear’s visible shape.
records.difference: 耳（みみ） is the body part; 聞こえる（きこえる） describes sound being audible or a person being able to hear it.

records.kanji_breakdown:
上 = up / above
手 = hand
records.nuance: 上手（じょうず） means skillful or good at something. Here the younger sister sings well. The English “can sing” conveys ability but does not fully express the Japanese praise of her skill.
records.logic: Learn 上手 as a complete word meaning skillful; it is not a claim that skill comes literally from an “upper hand.” In 歌が上手, が marks the skill.
records.difference: 下手（へた） means unskilled or not good at something. 上手 is a な-adjective/noun, as in 上手な歌手.
records.filipino: mahusay; mahusay kumanta ang nakababata kong kapatid na babae

records.nuance: 手（て） means hand. Here raising a hand signals that the person understood; 手を上げる is to raise one’s hand.
records.logic: The hand is lifted upward as a visible signal. を marks the hand being raised.
records.difference: 手（て） is the hand; 腕（うで） usually means the arm and can also refer to someone’s skill.
records.filipino: kamay; itaas ang kamay kung naunawaan mo

records.nuance: 足（あし） can mean leg or foot. With 長い here, it means legs: he has long legs.
records.logic: Length describes the lower limbs in this sentence, rather than the soles of the feet.
records.difference: 足（あし） can refer to the whole lower limb; 脚（あし） more specifically writes “leg” in many contexts.
records.filipino: binti; mahahaba ang mga binti niya

records.nuance: 男（おとこ） means a male person or man. 男の人 refers to the man who started speaking to the group.
records.logic: The compound 男の人 identifies the person’s gender; the sentence then says he spoke to 私たち.
records.difference: 男の人 is an ordinary way to say man; 男性（だんせい） is more formal or neutral in descriptions and forms.

records.nuance: 女（おんな） means woman or female. In 若い女の人, 若い describes her as young; 女 alone does not mean “young girl.”
records.logic: 女の人 identifies a female person, and 若い adds her age description.
records.difference: 女の人 is common everyday wording for a woman; 女性（じょせい） is more formal or neutral.
records.filipino: babae; bata pa ang babaeng tindera

records.kanji_breakdown:
子 = child
供 = attend / accompany in other uses
records.nuance: 子供（こども） means child or children. Here the English uses “Kids”; the Japanese noun does not itself specify a plural, and the sentence says they were noisy on the train.
records.logic: Treat 子供 as the established word for a child or children, rather than translating it as a literal sum of the individual characters.
records.difference: 子供 is the everyday word for a child or children. 児童（じどう） is more formal and often used in school or administrative contexts.
records.filipino: bata; maingay ang mga bata sa tren

records.nuance: あげる（あげる） means to give something to the listener or another person. この本、あなたにあげます means “I’ll give you this book.” The recipient is marked with に; the giver is understood from context.
records.logic: あげる presents the transfer from the giver toward the recipient. In contrast, くれる presents it as coming toward the speaker or someone the speaker treats as close; how that relationship is framed depends on context.
records.meaning: give; hand over to another person
records.difference: あげる gives from the giver’s viewpoint. くれる（くれる） describes someone giving to the speaker or the speaker’s in-group. This note is kana-only; do not confuse giving あげる with 上げる “raise.”
records.filipino: ibigay; ibibigay ko sa iyo ang aklat na ito

records.kanji_breakdown:
大 = very / great
好 = like / fondness
records.nuance: 大好き（だいすき） means to like or love something very much. 犬が大好き expresses strong affection for dogs; it need not be romantic love.
records.logic: 大 intensifies 好き. The complete expression is a な-adjective; が marks the thing the speaker likes.
records.difference: 好き（すき） means like or fond of; 大好き（だいすき） expresses a stronger degree.
records.filipino: gustong-gusto ko ang mga aso; mahal na mahal ko ang mga aso

records.nuance: 私（わたし） is a first-person pronoun. 私が行きましょう offers or proposes that the speaker go; it is not just an abstract “I.”
records.logic: 私 identifies who will go. が marks the speaker as the person volunteering or taking the turn.
records.difference: 私 is widely usable and often polite or neutral. 僕（ぼく） is more casual and commonly used by male speakers; speakers’ choices vary.
records.filipino: ako; ako na po ang pupunta

records.kanji_breakdown:
友 = friend
達 = people / group marker in some uses
records.nuance: 友達（ともだち） means friend(s). In 私には友達がたくさんいます, it means the speaker has many friends. The word itself can refer to a friend or friends.
records.logic: たくさん gives the number as many; Japanese does not need a separate plural ending on 友達 here.
records.difference: 友達 is a friend or companion. 知り合い（しりあい） means an acquaintance, someone known but not necessarily a friend.

records.nuance: 家（うち） often means one’s home or household. 家に遊びに来てください is a friendly invitation to come visit the speaker at home. The card’s reading is うち.
records.logic: 家 is the destination, and 遊びに来る means come over socially for a visit.
records.meaning: home; house; household, depending on context
records.difference: 家（うち） often presents a home as one’s own household; 家（いえ） often refers more directly to a house or dwelling. Retain うち for this card.
records.filipino: bahay namin; pumasyal kayo sa bahay namin

records.nuance: 気（き）が小さい is an idiom meaning timid or easily worried about small things. Here 意外に says that this trait is unexpected.
records.logic: The phrase describes a cautious, timid temperament; it does not say that a person’s mind or spirit is physically small.
records.meaning: spirit; temperament; in 気が小さい, timid
records.difference: 気が小さい means timid or small-hearted; 大胆（だいたん） means bold or daring.
records.filipino: loob; mahina ang loob niya, nang di-inaasahan

records.kanji_breakdown:
天 = sky / heaven
気 = air / atmosphere
records.nuance: 天気（てんき） means weather. いい天気 describes pleasant weather today, rather than the day itself being “good.”
records.logic: The compound refers to atmospheric conditions; the context judges them pleasant.
records.difference: 天気 is everyday weather. 天候（てんこう） is a more formal word for weather conditions.

records.nuance: 晴れる（はれる） means the weather clears or becomes sunny. 明日は晴れるといいですね expresses a hope that tomorrow will be fine.
records.logic: The sky or weather changes to a clear state; といいですね adds the speaker’s wish.
records.difference: 晴れる is the verb “clear up / become sunny”; 晴れ（はれ） is the noun “fine / sunny weather.”

records.nuance: 開ける（あける） is transitive: someone opens something that is shut. 窓を開けてください is a polite request to open the window.
records.logic: The person causes the window to change from closed to open; を marks the window as the object.
records.difference: 開ける（あける） describes someone opening something; 開く（あく） describes something opening. 開く（ひらく） is also used for opening or unfolding books and pages.
records.filipino: buksan; buksan po ninyo ang bintana

records.nuance: 開く（ひらく） means open or spread out. Here 32ページを開いてください means open the textbook to page 32. Keep this card’s reading ひらく.
records.logic: The book is opened at a specified page; 32ページ identifies the place to open it to.
records.difference: 開く（ひらく） is used for opening a book or spreading something out. 開ける（あける） is common for someone opening a window or door; 開く can also be read あく with a different intransitive use.
records.filipino: buksan; buksan po ninyo ang aklat sa pahina 32

records.nuance: 閉じる（とじる） means close something open. Here the request is to close the textbooks; てください makes it polite.
records.logic: The textbooks are the things being brought to a closed state, marked with を.
records.difference: 閉じる is common for books, eyes, and similar things; 閉める（しめる） is common for shutting a door or window. Some uses overlap.
records.filipino: isara; pakisara ang mga aklat-aralin ninyo

records.nuance: 閉める（しめる） is transitive: someone shuts a door or window. ちゃんと adds “properly,” while よ makes this a direct casual request.
records.logic: The door is the object being moved to a shut state; を marks it.
records.difference: 閉める（しめる） means someone shuts something. 閉まる（しまる） describes a door or shop becoming or being closed.
records.filipino: isara; isara mo nang maayos ang pinto

records.nuance: 閉まる（しまる） is intransitive: a door shuts or a shop’s business ends. Here 閉まっていました describes the shop as already closed at a past reference time.
records.logic: The sentence focuses on the shop’s closed state and does not name anyone who closed it.
records.meaning: close; shut; be closed; a shop close for business
records.difference: 閉める（しめる） is what someone does to shut a door or shop. 閉まる（しまる） describes the resulting closed state or the shop ending business.
records.filipino: sarado na noon ang tindahan; nagsara na ang tindahan

records.nuance: 聞く（きく） means listen to in this sentence. 聞いています describes the ongoing activity of listening to the radio.
records.logic: The person directs attention to the radio’s broadcast; を marks what she is listening to.
records.meaning: listen; hear; ask in other contexts
records.difference: 聞く（きく） can describe intentionally listening. 聞こえる（きこえる） means sound is audible or can be heard, without necessarily focusing on it.

records.kanji_breakdown:
時 = time / hour
間 = interval / span
records.nuance: 時間（じかん） can mean a time span or available time. 今は時間がありません means the speaker has no time right now.
records.logic: 今 sets the current situation; 時間 refers to the time the speaker has available.
records.difference: 時間（じかん） often means a span or available time; 時刻（じこく） means the clock time or point when something happens.

records.nuance: 高い describes a high position or level. Depending on what it describes, it can mean tall/high, expensive, high-pitched, or high in degree; with a building it means tall.
records.logic: The comparison set is buildings in this town, and 一番 selects the greatest height.
records.meaning: high; tall; expensive in other contexts
records.difference: 高い（たかい） means tall or high; 低い（ひくい） means low or short in height.
records.filipino: mataas; ito ang pinakamataas na gusali sa bayang ito

records.kanji_breakdown: くれる = give to me / someone on my side
records.nuance: Frames an action or gift as coming to the speaker or the speaker’s in-group. Here a friend gave the speaker a birthday present.
records.logic: The giver is marked by が; the recipient is understood from context. くれる frames the giving from the recipient’s side.
records.meaning: to give (to me or someone on my side)
records.difference: あげる describes giving from the giver’s side; くれる describes someone giving to the speaker or the speaker’s side.
records.filipino: Ibinigay sa akin ng kaibigan ko ang regalo para sa kaarawan ko.

records.nuance: Describes a low price or cost. Here the clothes are very inexpensive; it does not mean “safe.”
records.logic: The adjective evaluates how much money an item costs; whether “cheap” sounds positive or negative depends on context.
records.difference: 安い means low-priced; 易しい（やさしい） means easy.
records.filipino: mura; mura ang mga damit na ito

records.nuance: Can refer to space in front of something or an earlier time or position. 店の前 means in front of the shop here.
records.logic: The shop is the reference point; 前 locates the meeting place at its front.
records.difference: 前（まえ） means front/before; 後ろ（うしろ） means behind.

records.nuance: あと marks what follows something in time or order. 仕事の後 means after work here.
records.logic: Work is the reference event; 後 places the movie later than that event.
records.difference: 後（あと） means after; 前（まえ） means before. 後 also has other readings, including うしろ and ご.

records.nuance: Names the morning period. 気持ちのいい朝 describes a pleasant or refreshing morning.
records.logic: 気持ちのいい describes how the morning feels; 朝 identifies the time of day.
records.difference: 朝（あさ） is morning; 昼（ひる） is daytime/noon, and 夜（よる） is night.

records.nuance: Broadly refers to daytime around noon and can mean lunchtime when context supports it. Here 昼のドラマ means a daytime drama, not necessarily something watched over lunch.
records.logic: It marks the drama’s daytime slot; 毎日 says the speaker watches it every day.
records.difference: 昼（ひる） means daytime/noon; 昼食（ちゅうしょく） specifically means lunch/the midday meal.

records.nuance: Refers to this evening or tonight. The question asks when tonight’s party starts.
records.logic: 今 anchors the evening to today; the question asks the party’s start time.
records.difference: 今晩（こんばん） and 今夜（こんや） are close alternatives and often overlap.

records.nuance: The nighttime period after evening, often extending through the dark hours. 昨日の夜 means last night.
records.logic: 昨日 places the night in the past; 家にいました says the speaker stayed home then.
records.difference: 夜（よる） is night; 夕方（ゆうがた） is evening around sunset.

records.nuance: The ordinary verb for eating food. Here the speaker ate Thai curry yesterday.
records.logic: The food marked by を is what was eaten; 食べました is polite past.
records.difference: 食べる means eat; 飲む（のむ） means drink.

records.nuance: Means drink. With お酒 it refers to drinking alcohol; ～ています describes the speaker as drinking with a friend now or around the present.
records.logic: お酒 marks what is consumed; 友達と marks the companion.
records.meaning: to drink; to have a drink
records.difference: 飲む means drink; 食べる（たべる） means eat.
records.filipino: uminom ng alak; umiinom ng alak kasama ang kaibigan

records.nuance: Can mean cooked rice or a meal. Here it contrasts with bread as a preferred staple.
records.logic: より…が好きだ states preference; the bread contrast supports the rice sense, though ご飯 can also mean meal.
records.difference: ご飯（ごはん） can mean rice or a meal; 食事（しょくじ） means meal more generally.

records.nuance: Covers seeing and intentionally looking at something. Here the speaker likes looking at pictures.
records.logic: 絵を見る is the activity nominalized by の and marked as what the speaker likes.
records.meaning: to see; look at; watch (by context)
records.difference: 見る（みる） means see/look; 見える（みえる） means be visible or come into view.

records.nuance: Means to show something by making it available to see. The request asks someone to show the photo.
records.logic: 写真を marks what is shown; ～てください makes a polite request. Japanese leaves the recipient unstated.
records.difference: 見せる（みせる） is transitive “show”; 見える（みえる） is “be visible.”

records.nuance: Asks for an increase in degree, amount, or extent. Here it means come closer than the listener is now.
records.logic: もっと modifies 近く, increasing closeness; 来てください is a polite request.
records.difference: もっと means more/further; もう can mean already or one more, depending on context.

records.kanji_breakdown: 見 = see; find by looking (word cue)
records.nuance: Means to find or discover something sought or previously unknown. The speaker found a new job.
records.logic: 新しい仕事 is the object found; the past form reports a successful result.
records.difference: 見つける（みつける） is transitive “find”; 見つかる（みつかる） is “be found/turn up.”

records.nuance: Describes something visible or within sight, without emphasizing deliberate looking. Mt. Fuji is clearly visible from here.
records.logic: ここから marks the viewpoint; よく emphasizes visibility from that position.
records.meaning: to be visible; can be seen
records.difference: 見える（みえる） means be visible; 見る（みる） means actively look/see.

records.nuance: Means speak or talk. With a person marked by と, it means speak with that person; here by phone with the speaker’s mother.
records.logic: 電話で gives the means and 母と identifies the conversation partner.
records.meaning: to speak; talk; tell (depending on object)
records.difference: 話す（はなす） means speak/talk; 話し合う（はなしあう） means discuss together.

records.nuance: Means to read written material. ～ています can describe an activity in progress or a continuing habit; this sentence permits either.
records.logic: 雑誌を marks the material read; the progressive form does not by itself force only a “right now” interpretation.
records.difference: 読む（よむ） means read; 読み上げる（よみあげる） means read aloud.

records.nuance: Means to write. Here the speaker wrote a letter to him.
records.logic: 手紙 is what is written (を); 彼に marks the recipient.
records.difference: 書く（かく） means write; 描く（かく） means draw/depict, with the same reading but a different kanji and meaning.
records.filipino: sumulat ng liham para sa kaniya

records.nuance: Points to a place near the listener or already established in conversation. The request is to sit there.
records.logic: に marks the location; its exact referent depends on shared context.
records.difference: そこ often points to a listener-side/known place; あそこ often points to a more distant or shared place.

records.nuance: Means meet someone. また会いましょう is a friendly suggestion to meet again.
records.logic: また means again; ～ましょう presents a proposal that includes the speaker.
records.difference: 会う（あう） means meet; 合う（あう） means fit, match, or agree.

records.kanji_breakdown: 仕 = serve/do (character cue); 事 = matter, thing
records.nuance: Means work or a job: duties someone does or their employment. Here work is described as busy in March.
records.logic: The whole word refers to work as an activity or occupation; these are character cues, not a historical derivation.
records.difference: 仕事 is work/job; 職業（しょくぎょう） specifically means occupation/profession.

records.nuance: An electric railway train. The sentence says the speaker commutes to school by train.
records.logic: The characters are useful cues to the modern compound, not a complete etymological account.
records.difference: 電車 is a train; 汽車 often refers to a steam train, with regional variation in broader usage.
records.filipino: sumasakay ako ng tren papasok sa paaralan

records.nuance: A railway station. The question asks where the station is.
records.logic: The word names the rail stop/place being sought; どこ asks its location.
records.difference: 駅 is a railway station; 停留所（ていりゅうじょ） is a stop for buses or trams.

records.nuance: With reading やめる, means stop, quit, or discontinue an action. Here it asks someone to stop talking.
records.logic: 話すの nominalizes the action; を marks what should cease, and ください makes a request.
records.difference: 止める（やめる） means discontinue an action; 止める（とめる） often means cause movement/progress to stop. The note’s exact reading is やめる.

records.nuance: ここ points to a place near the speaker or currently in focus. Here it locates the book.
records.logic: に marks where something exists; 本があります says a book is present at that location.
records.difference: ここ is here/this place; そこ is there/that place near the listener or already mentioned.

records.nuance: 歩く means to walk on foot. The sentence invites the listener to walk to the station together.
records.logic: まで marks the destination limit; ～ましょう makes a suggestion including the speaker.
records.difference: 歩く means walk; 行く（いく） means go and does not specify walking.
records.filipino: maglakad; maglakad tayo papunta sa istasyon

records.nuance: 近い describes a short distance or closeness. The station is near the speaker’s current place.
records.logic: ここから sets the starting viewpoint; 近い evaluates distance from it.
records.difference: 近い means near; 遠い（とおい） means far.

records.nuance: 長い describes great length or duration. Here it describes her hair.
records.logic: 髪 is the thing whose physical length is being described; とても intensifies the adjective.
records.difference: 長い means long; 高い（たかい） means high/tall or expensive by context.

records.nuance: 短い describes limited physical length or duration. Here it describes his legs.
records.logic: 足 is being evaluated for length; the sentence says his legs are short.
records.difference: 短い means short; 長い（ながい） means long.
records.filipino: maikli; maikli ang mga binti niya

records.nuance: 広い describes a place or area as spacious. The house is very spacious; deck “big” is a loose English equivalent.
records.logic: The house has ample space, so 広い focuses on room/area rather than height or overall size alone.
records.difference: 広い means spacious/wide; 大きい（おおきい） means large in overall size.

records.nuance: もらう describes receiving something, with the giver commonly marked by から or に. Here she is the source of the present.
records.logic: プレゼントを is what was received; 彼女から marks where it came from.
records.difference: もらう views the event from the receiver’s side; あげる views giving from the giver’s side.
records.filipino: tumanggap; nakatanggap ako ng regalo mula sa kaniya

records.kanji_breakdown: 全 = whole; 部 = part/section (character cues)
records.nuance: 全部 means all of something, the complete amount or set. The speaker politely requests all of the items being discussed.
records.logic: It gathers the relevant items into one complete set; それ refers to those items in context.
records.difference: 全部 refers to the whole set; みんな commonly refers to all people, though it can be used more broadly.

records.nuance: 国 means a country or nation. について introduces the topic the speaker will talk about.
records.logic: 少し limits the amount of what will be said; お話しましょう is a polite proposal to speak.
records.difference: 国 is country/nation; 故郷（ふるさと） means one’s hometown or homeland.

records.nuance: 白い describes a white color. Here it describes the whiteness of his teeth.
records.logic: 歯 identifies what has the color; the adjective predicates a visible quality.
records.difference: 白い means white; 黒い（くろい） means black.
records.filipino: maputi; maputi ang mga ngipin niya

records.nuance: 赤い describes the color red. The rose bought was red.
records.logic: It modifies バラ and identifies which rose by its color.
records.difference: 赤い means red; 白い（しろい） means white.

records.nuance: 米（こめ） refers to rice grain, usually uncooked rice. お米 uses the polite prefix お before 米; the sentence says Japanese people love rice.
records.logic: The particle が marks rice as what is loved; this contrasts the grain term 米 with cooked rice ご飯.
records.difference: 米（こめ） is rice grain; ご飯（ごはん） is cooked rice or a meal.
records.filipino: bigas; mahal na mahal ng mga Hapon ang bigas

records.nuance: まだ means still or not yet, depending on the sentence polarity. With 終わっていません it means the homework is not finished yet.
records.logic: まだ sets the state as continuing up to now; the negative いません says completion has not occurred.
records.difference: まだ…ない means not yet; もう can mean already, or no longer with a negative.
records.filipino: hindi pa; hindi ko pa natatapos ang takdang-aralin

records.nuance: ある expresses existence or presence of inanimate things. Here many documents are on the desk.
records.logic: 机の上に gives the location; 書類が marks the documents that exist there.
records.difference: ある is used for inanimate things; いる is used for people and animals.
records.filipino: may maraming dokumento sa ibabaw ng mesa ko

records.nuance: ない expresses nonexistence or absence. Here there is nothing at this place.
records.logic: 何も with a negative means nothing; ここには sets the location where nothing exists.
records.difference: ない means absent/not exist; ある means exist/be present.

records.nuance: とても intensifies an adjective or adverb. It emphasizes how interesting the book is.
records.logic: It modifies おもしろい, raising the degree of the described quality.
records.difference: とても is a neutral/common intensifier; すごく is more conversational and can sound stronger.

records.nuance: 作る means to make or prepare something. Here the speaker is making breakfast now.
records.logic: 朝ご飯 is what is being prepared; ～ています and 今 indicate an activity in progress now.
records.difference: 作る means make/create; 料理する（りょうりする） specifically means cook/prepare food.
records.filipino: maghanda; naghahanda ako ng almusal ngayon

records.nuance: 使う means to use something for a purpose. The sentence politely asks the listener to use this computer.
records.logic: このパソコンを marks the item being used; ～てください makes a request.
records.difference: 使う means use; 利用する（りようする） is a more formal term for use/utilization.
records.filipino: gamitin; pakigamit ang computer na ito

records.nuance: 消す means to make something disappear or turn off. With 電気 it means turn off the lights/electricity.
records.logic: 昼間 sets the time; 電気を marks what is turned off.
records.difference: 消す is transitive “turn off”; 消える（きえる） is intransitive “go out/turn off.”

records.nuance: 売る means to sell something. The sentence says he sold the house.
records.logic: 家を is the item sold; past form 売った reports the completed sale.
records.difference: 売る is sell; 買う（かう） is buy.

records.nuance: 春 is the spring season. 今年の春 means this spring of the current year.
records.logic: 今年 anchors the season to this year; 暖かい describes the weather as warm.
records.difference: 春（はる） is spring; 夏（なつ） is summer.

records.nuance: 夏 is the summer season. The speaker says they love summer very much.
records.logic: が marks summer as the thing liked; 大好き expresses strong liking.
records.difference: 夏（なつ） is summer; 冬（ふゆ） is winter.

records.nuance: 冬 is the winter season. The sentence describes Canadian winters as very cold.
records.logic: カナダの links the winter to Canada; とても intensifies 寒い.
records.difference: 冬（ふゆ） is winter; 夏（なつ） is summer.
records.filipino: taglamig; napakalamig ng taglamig sa Canada

records.nuance: みんな means everyone or everybody. In this sentence it is the group who will receive sweets.
records.logic: に marks the recipients; あげましょう proposes that the speaker and listener give sweets to everyone.
records.difference: みんな refers to everyone; 全部（ぜんぶ） refers to all of a set of things.
records.filipino: lahat; bigyan natin ng kendi ang lahat

records.nuance: 暑い describes hot weather or air temperature. The sentence says it is very hot today.
records.logic: 今日 anchors the weather to today; とても intensifies the heat.
records.difference: 暑い（あつい） is hot weather; 熱い（あつい） is hot to the touch or feverishly warm.

records.nuance: 熱い describes something hot to the touch or hot in temperature. Here it describes the soup, so it is too hot to drink comfortably.
records.logic: スープ is the thing whose temperature is described; とても intensifies the heat.
records.meaning: hot (to the touch; temperature of an object)
records.difference: 熱い（あつい） is hot to the touch; 暑い（あつい） is hot weather/air.
records.filipino: mainit; mainit ang sabaw na ito

records.nuance: 新しい describes something new or recently acquired/created. The sentence says his car is new.
records.logic: The adjective assigns newness to the car; it does not specify whether the car is brand-new or simply newer than expected.
records.difference: 新しい means new; 古い（ふるい） means old.

records.nuance: 古い describes something old or long-existing. Here it describes the speaker’s car preference.
records.logic: 車 is the item evaluated as old; 好きです expresses preference, not that the car is broken.
records.difference: 古い means old; 新しい（あたらしい） means new.
records.filipino: luma; gusto ko ang mga lumang kotse

records.nuance: 良い means good. It is read いい in this sentence and describes her as a good friend.
records.logic: 友達 is the person’s role/relationship; 良い evaluates the relationship positively.
records.difference: 良い（いい） is commonly read いい; よい is a more formal or careful reading. 悪い（わるい） means bad.

records.nuance: 悪い means bad or harmful. With 体に it means harmful to the body/health; smoking is unhealthy.
records.logic: 体に marks what is affected, so this is a health consequence rather than a moral judgment.
records.difference: 体に悪い means bad for health; 体にいい means good for health.
records.filipino: masama sa kalusugan; masama sa katawan ang paninigarilyo

records.nuance: 思う means to think, believe, or feel an opinion. そう思います means “I think so” or “I feel the same way.”
records.logic: そう points back to the idea just mentioned; も adds that the speaker shares that view too.
records.difference: 思う expresses a thought/opinion; 考える（かんがえる） often emphasizes considering or reasoning something through.
records.filipino: sa tingin ko rin; ganoon din ang iniisip ko

records.nuance: いつも describes something that happens regularly or is usual. Here she is consistently energetic/cheerful.
records.logic: It modifies 元気だ and presents the state as her usual one.
records.difference: いつも means always/usually; ときどき（時々） means sometimes.

records.nuance: 忘れる means to forget or fail to remember something. In the request, 約束を忘れないで means do not forget the promise.
records.logic: 約束 is the thing remembered; ないでください politely asks the listener to avoid forgetting.
records.difference: 忘れる is forget; 覚える（おぼえる） is remember/learn.
records.filipino: kalimutan; huwag mong kalimutan ang pangako

records.nuance: 住む means to live or reside in a place. Here he lives near his company/office.
records.logic: 会社の近くに marks the location of residence; ～ている describes his continuing living situation.
records.difference: 住む means reside; 暮らす（くらす） often emphasizes how one lives or daily life.
records.filipino: manirahan; nakatira siya malapit sa opisina niya

records.kanji_breakdown: 名 = name; reputation; 前 = before (character cues)
records.nuance: 名前 means a person’s name. The polite request asks the listener to tell their name.
records.logic: 名前 is the information requested; 教えてください is a polite request to tell/share it.
records.difference: 名前 is a name; 名字（みょうじ） is a family name/surname.
records.filipino: pangalan; sabihin mo sa akin ang pangalan mo

records.nuance: いつ asks about the time an event happens. Here it asks when she will come.
records.logic: 来ますか asks about a future or scheduled arrival; いつ leaves the specific time open.
records.difference: いつ asks when; どこ asks where.

records.nuance: 飲み物 is something to drink, a beverage. The speaker wants some kind of drink.
records.logic: The compound names a thing for drinking; 何か makes it “something.”
records.difference: 飲み物 is a beverage; 食べ物（たべもの） is food to eat.
records.filipino: inumin; gusto ko sana ng maiinom

records.kanji_breakdown: 気 = feeling/mind; 持 = hold (character cues)
records.nuance: 気持ち refers to a feeling, emotion, or state of mind. Here the speaker cannot understand his feelings.
records.logic: The word refers to someone’s inner emotional state; が marks what the speaker does not understand.
records.difference: 気持ち is a feeling/emotional state; 気分（きぶん） often refers to one’s mood or physical feeling at a particular time.
records.filipino: damdamin; hindi ko maintindihan ang damdamin niya

records.nuance: 生きる means to be alive or live one’s life. 一生懸命 emphasizes everyone’s effort in living.
records.logic: 皆 identifies the people; 一生懸命 modifies how they live, expressing earnest effort rather than a literal translation.
records.difference: 生きる means live/be alive; 生活する（せいかつする） means carry on daily life.
records.filipino: mabuhay; nagsisikap silang mamuhay nang buong makakaya

records.kanji_breakdown: どちら = which one; which direction
records.nuance: どちら politely asks which of two options. The sentence asks whether the listener prefers meat or fish.
records.logic: 肉と魚 set up the alternatives; どちらが好き asks which one is preferred.
records.difference: どちら is a polite form used to choose between options; どれ usually selects from three or more items.
records.filipino: alin; alin ang mas gusto mo, karne o isda?

records.kanji_breakdown: 先 = ahead; previous; 生 = life (character cues)
records.nuance: 先生 is the usual respectful title for a teacher and certain professionals. The speaker wants to become a Japanese-language teacher.
records.logic: 日本語の identifies what the person teaches; になる means become.
records.difference: 先生 is a respectful title; 教師（きょうし） is a more formal term for the occupation teacher.
records.filipino: guro; nais kong maging guro ng wikang Hapon

records.kanji_breakdown: 大 = large; great; 学 = study
records.nuance: 大学 means a university or college. Here the speaker wants to go to university and study more.
records.logic: に marks the destination of 行く; もっと modifies studying as “more.”
records.difference: 大学 means university/college; 高校（こうこう） means high school.
records.filipino: unibersidad; gusto kong pumasok sa unibersidad at mag-aral pa

records.kanji_breakdown: 学 = study; 生 = learner/life (character cues)
records.nuance: 学生 is a student, especially someone enrolled in an educational institution. 真面目な describes him as earnest/serious in attitude.
records.logic: The noun identifies his status; 真面目 describes his manner as a student.
records.difference: 学生 means student; 生徒（せいと） is commonly used for school pupils, especially below university.
records.filipino: estudyante; masipag at seryoso siyang estudyante

records.kanji_breakdown: 大 = university-level; 学 = study; 生 = student (character cues)
records.nuance: 大学生 means a university student. Here the speaker says her older sister is a university student.
records.logic: 大学 specifies the institution level; 生 here is part of the word for a student.
records.difference: 大学生 is a university student; 高校生（こうこうせい） is a high-school student.
records.filipino: estudyante sa unibersidad; estudyante sa unibersidad ang ate ko

records.kanji_breakdown: 高 = high; 校 = school; 生 = student (character cues)
records.nuance: 高校生 is a high-school student. The sentence says the speaker’s younger brother is in high school.
records.logic: 高校 specifies high school; 生 indicates the person’s student status in this compound.
records.difference: 高校生 is a high-school student; 大学生（だいがくせい） is a university student.
records.filipino: estudyante sa high school; high-school student ang nakababatang kapatid kong lalaki

records.kanji_breakdown: 勉 = make effort; 強 = strong (character cues)
records.nuance: 勉強 means study or learning. In this sentence, the speaker is studying Japanese.
records.logic: 日本語を marks the subject being studied; ～ています presents the activity as ongoing or current.
records.difference: 勉強する means study; 習う（ならう） means learn from instruction/practice, often with a teacher.
records.filipino: mag-aral; nag-aaral ako ng wikang Hapon

records.nuance: 強い describes strength or intensity. With 風 it means the wind is strong today.
records.logic: 風 is the phenomenon whose force is described; 今日 anchors the weather to today.
records.difference: 強い means strong; 弱い（よわい） means weak.

records.kanji_breakdown: どれ = which one; what one
records.nuance: どれ asks which item from a group of three or more. この中で sets the group, and the speaker asks which item is liked.
records.logic: この中で means among these; が marks the selected preference.
records.difference: どれ is used for selecting an item from several; どちら often selects between two and is more polite.
records.filipino: alin; alin dito ang gusto mo?

records.nuance: 弱い means weak. With 体 it describes a constitution/body that is somewhat frail or not robust.
records.logic: 体が identifies the aspect that is weak; 少し softens the statement.
records.difference: 体が弱い describes a weak constitution; 強い（つよい） is strong.
records.filipino: mahina ang pangangatawan; medyo mahina ang pangangatawan ng batang iyon

records.nuance: 数 means number or count of items. The sentence says the number of glasses is insufficient.
records.logic: グラスの数 identifies the count being evaluated; 足りません means it is not enough.
records.difference: 数 is a count/number of things; 番号（ばんごう） is an identifying number or numeral label.
records.filipino: bilang; kulang ang bilang ng baso

records.nuance: 勝つ means to win a contest, game, or competition. Here the Yankees won today’s game.
records.logic: ヤンキースが marks the team that won; the past form reports the result.
records.difference: 勝つ means win; 負ける（まける） means lose.

records.nuance: 負ける means to lose or be defeated. Here the speaker’s team lost that match.
records.logic: その試合で sets the match in which the loss occurred; the team is the one that lost.
records.difference: 負ける means lose; 勝つ（かつ） means win.
records.filipino: matalo; natalo ang koponan namin sa laban na iyon

records.nuance: 要る means be needed or required. In this sentence, a reservation is unnecessary.
records.logic: 予約は is the topic; the negative polite form 要りません says it is not needed.
records.difference: 要る（いる） means be needed; いる（居る） means exist/be present for people or animals.

records.nuance: ドア is a door. ドアを開けてください asks the listener to open it.
records.logic: を marks the door as the object of 開ける; ください makes a polite request.
records.difference: ドア is a door; 戸（と） is a native Japanese word for a door or sliding panel.

records.nuance: 払う means to pay money owed or due. Here the speaker offers to pay.
records.logic: 私が emphasizes the speaker as the one who will pay; ～ましょう offers or proposes the action.
records.difference: 払う means pay; 支払う（しはらう） is a more formal/common compound for making a payment.

records.nuance: 乗る means to get on or ride a vehicle. 駅から asks the listener to take a taxi from the station.
records.logic: タクシーに marks the vehicle boarded; に is used with this verb for the vehicle.
records.difference: 乗る means board/ride; 降りる（おりる） means get off.
records.filipino: sumakay; sumakay ka ng taksi mula sa istasyon

records.nuance: 立つ means to stand or take a standing position. Here he stood on stage.
records.logic: ステージに marks the place where he stood; the past form describes the completed event.
records.difference: 立つ means stand; 座る（すわる） means sit.

records.nuance: 次 means the next one or what follows. Here it introduces the next meeting time.
records.logic: 次は marks the next occasion/topic; いつ asks when to meet.
records.difference: 次 means next; 最後（さいご） means last/final.
records.filipino: susunod; kailan tayo magkikita sa susunod?

records.nuance: 早い means early when describing time. The sentence says it is still too early to go to school.
records.logic: まだ reinforces that the appropriate time has not arrived; 学校へ行くには sets the activity for which it is early.
records.difference: 早い（はやい） means early; 速い（はやい） means fast in speed.
records.filipino: maaga; masyado pang maaga para pumasok sa paaralan

records.nuance: 始める means to start something. The request is to begin the test.
records.logic: テストを marks what someone should start; を fits the transitive “start [something]” pattern.
records.difference: 始める is transitive “start something”; 始まる（はじまる） is intransitive “something begins.”

records.nuance: 始まる means an event or process begins. Here a new job has started.
records.logic: 新しい仕事が is what began; が marks the event as subject, with no agent starting it specified.
records.difference: 始まる is intransitive “begin”; 始める（はじめる） is transitive “start something.”
records.filipino: magsimula; nagsimula na ang bago kong trabaho

records.nuance: 終わる means to end or finish. The conference ends at four o’clock.
records.logic: 会議 is the event that ends; に marks the ending time.
records.difference: 終わる is intransitive “end”; 終える（おえる） is transitive “finish something.”
records.filipino: matapos; matatapos ang kumperensiya nang alas-kuwatro

records.nuance: 終わり is the end or finishing point. 夏休みももう終わりだ says summer vacation is already over/at its end.
records.logic: もう indicates the expected endpoint has arrived; だ states that vacation is at its end.
records.difference: 終わり is the end; 始まり（はじまり） is the beginning.
records.filipino: katapusan; tapos na rin ang bakasyon sa tag-init

records.nuance: テーブル is a table, usually a piece of furniture in this context. The sentence says the speaker bought a new one.
records.logic: 新しい modifies テーブル; を marks it as what was bought.
records.difference: テーブル is a table; 机（つくえ） often means a desk or work table.
records.filipino: mesa; bumili ako ng bagong mesa

records.nuance: 紙 means paper as a material or sheet. The speaker asks whether paper and a pencil are available.
records.logic: 紙と鉛筆 names two items; ありますか asks whether they are present/available.
records.difference: 紙 is paper; 神（かみ） means deity/god and is a homophone with a different kanji.
records.filipino: papel; may papel at lapis ba kayo?

records.nuance: 楽しむ means to enjoy or take pleasure in an experience. Here the speaker wants to enjoy time alone today.
records.logic: 一人の時間 is the experience enjoyed; ～たい expresses the speaker’s desire.
records.difference: 楽しむ means enjoy an activity/experience; 楽しい（たのしい） describes something as enjoyable.
records.filipino: mag-enjoy; gusto kong namnamin ang oras na mag-isa ngayon

records.nuance: 楽しい describes something or someone as enjoyable, pleasant, or fun. Here he is a very enjoyable person to be with; “fun to be with” is natural English.
records.logic: 人 is what is described; とても intensifies the positive impression.
records.difference: 楽しい describes something enjoyable; 楽しむ（たのしむ） means actively enjoy it.

records.nuance: 歌う means to sing. The sentence says the group sang loudly.
records.logic: 大きな声で describes the volume/way they sang; 私たちは identifies the singers.
records.difference: 歌う means sing; 演奏する（えんそうする） means perform/play music on an instrument.

records.nuance: 色 means color or hue. The speaker compliments the sweater’s lovely color.
records.logic: すてきな modifies 色; の links the color to the sweater.
records.difference: 色 is color; 模様（もよう） is a pattern/design.
records.filipino: kulay; ang ganda ng kulay ng sweater mo

records.nuance: すぐ means immediately or very soon. 行きます indicates the speaker will go without much delay.
records.logic: It modifies 行きます, emphasizing how soon the action will happen.
