records.difference: すぐ means right away/soon; もうすぐ specifically means very soon/almost.

records.nuance: ゲーム is a game; ビデオゲーム specifies a video game. The sentence says they played one.
records.logic: 私たちは identifies the players; をした is the common expression for playing a game.
records.difference: ゲーム is a game; 試合（しあい） is a match or sporting contest.
records.filipino: laro; naglaro kami ng video game

records.kanji_breakdown: 直 = return to proper condition; fix (character cue)
records.nuance: 直る means to return to a good or working condition; for a machine, it can mean be repaired/fixed. The air conditioner is not fixed yet.
records.logic: クーラー is the thing whose condition should improve; まだ…ません means it has not happened yet. The agent doing repairs is not stated.
records.meaning: to be fixed/repaired; return to working order
records.difference: 直る is intransitive “be fixed”; 直す（なおす） is transitive “fix something.”
records.filipino: maayos; hindi pa naaayos ang aircon

records.nuance: 曲がる means to bend or turn. Here it instructs the listener to turn left at that place.
records.logic: そこ marks the location; 左に gives the direction of the turn; ください makes it a polite instruction.
records.difference: 曲がる is intransitive “turn/bend”; 曲げる（まげる） is transitive “bend something.”

records.nuance: 同じ means the same or alike. The sentence says his Japanese level is about the same as mine.
records.logic: 私と sets the comparison; 位（くらい） softens it to “about/approximately the same level.”
records.difference: 同じ means same; 似ている（にている） means similar, not necessarily identical.
records.filipino: pareho; halos kapareho ng antas ko sa wikang Hapon

records.nuance: 違う means differ or be incorrect. With 答え, it means the answer is wrong/does not match.
records.logic: 答えが identifies what is different or incorrect; polite です states the judgment.
records.meaning: to differ; be different; be wrong (by context)
records.difference: 違う means differ/be wrong; 間違える（まちがえる） means make a mistake or get something wrong.

records.kanji_breakdown: 図 = diagram; 書 = writing; 館 = building (character cues)
records.nuance: 図書館 is a library. The speaker borrowed a cookbook there; で marks the place where the borrowing occurred.
records.logic: 料理の本 is what was borrowed; を marks the book, and 図書館で gives the source/place.
records.difference: 図書館 is a library; 本屋（ほんや） is a bookstore.
records.filipino: aklatan; humiram ako ng aklat-pangluto sa aklatan

records.nuance: 泊まる means to stay overnight somewhere, usually as a guest. The speaker plans to stay at this hotel tonight/today.
records.logic: ホテルに marks the lodging place; Japanese 今日は does not specify a time of day, but staying at a hotel normally means overnight.
records.difference: 泊まる means stay overnight; 止まる（とまる） means stop moving, with the same reading.
records.filipino: manuluyan; dito ako tutuloy sa hotel ngayong gabi

records.nuance: 遊ぶ means to play or spend leisure time. Here the children are playing in the park.
records.logic: 公園で gives where they are playing; ～ている presents the activity as underway.
records.meaning: to play; spend time for fun
records.difference: 遊ぶ means play/have leisure; 運動する（うんどうする） means exercise.
records.filipino: maglaro; naglalaro sa parke ang mga bata

records.kanji_breakdown: どうして = why; for what reason
records.nuance: どうして asks for a reason. Here it asks why the listener is crying.
records.logic: It requests the cause of the crying; the casual の at the end invites an explanation.
records.difference: どうして asks why; どうやって asks how to do something.

records.nuance: 服 means clothes or clothing. Here it is the new clothing the speaker bought yesterday.
records.logic: 新しい modifies the clothes; を marks them as what was bought.
records.difference: 服 means clothing; 着物（きもの） can mean traditional Japanese clothing and is narrower in many contexts.
records.filipino: damit; bumili ako ng bagong damit kahapon

records.kanji_breakdown: 父 = father; お = respectful/polite prefix
records.nuance: お父さん is a respectful or familiar way to say “father/dad,” and can also be used when addressing or referring to someone else’s father. The sentence says he is a company employee.
records.logic: The honorific お marks respectful/familiar usage; the sentence itself does not specify whether this is the speaker’s or another person’s father.
records.difference: お父さん is respectful/familiar; 父（ちち） is the usual humble term for one’s own father when speaking to others.
records.filipino: ama; empleyado sa kompanya ang tatay niya

records.nuance: 父 is the humble way to refer to one’s own father when speaking to other people. The speaker says they love their father.
records.logic: 私は sets the speaker as topic; 父が identifies the loved family member.
records.difference: 父（ちち） is used for one’s own father in outside conversation; お父さん（おとうさん） is a respectful/familiar form or address.
records.filipino: ama; mahal na mahal ko ang aking ama

records.kanji_breakdown: 母 = mother; お = respectful/polite prefix
records.nuance: お母さん is a respectful or familiar word for “mother/mom,” and can refer to someone else’s mother. Here the listener is asked to pass regards to their mother.
records.logic: に marks the recipient of the message; よろしくお伝えください is a polite request to convey regards.
records.difference: お母さん is respectful/familiar; 母（はは） is the usual humble term for one’s own mother when speaking to others.
records.filipino: ina; pakisabi ng pagbati ko sa iyong ina

records.nuance: 母 is the humble way to refer to one’s own mother when speaking to other people. Here the speaker talked with their mother yesterday.
records.logic: 母と marks her as the conversation partner; 昨日 places the conversation yesterday.
records.difference: 母（はは） is for one’s own mother in outside conversation; お母さん（おかあさん） is respectful/familiar or used in direct address.
records.filipino: ina; nakipag-usap ako sa aking ina kahapon

records.nuance: 親 means a parent or parents. 親の愛 means parental love; the sentence expresses gratitude for it.
records.logic: の links parent(s) to love; ありがたい conveys grateful appreciation.
records.difference: 親 refers to a parent/parents; 両親（りょうしん） explicitly means both parents.
records.filipino: magulang; nagpapasalamat tayo sa pagmamahal ng mga magulang

records.kanji_breakdown: 姉 = older sister; お = respectful/polite prefix
records.nuance: お姉さん is a polite/respectful way to refer to an older sister, often someone else’s. Here the speaker met the listener’s older sister.
records.logic: あなたのお identifies the addressee’s sister; 昨日 marks when they met.
records.difference: お姉さん is respectful/familiar; 姉（あね） is the usual humble term for one’s own older sister when speaking to others.
records.filipino: ate; nakilala ko kahapon ang ate mo

records.nuance: 妹 means younger sister, usually one’s own when speaking to others. The speaker says she is an elementary-school student.
records.logic: 私の identifies the speaker’s sister; 小学生です gives her school level.
records.difference: 妹 is younger sister; 姉（あね） is older sister.
records.filipino: nakababatang kapatid na babae; elementary pupil ang nakababata kong kapatid na babae

records.nuance: おなか is the stomach/belly in everyday speech. In おなかが空きました, the set phrase means “I’m hungry.”
records.logic: Literally it describes the stomach becoming empty, but the natural meaning is hunger.
records.meaning: stomach; hungry (in the expression おなかが空く)
records.difference: おなかが空く means get hungry; おなかがいっぱい means be full.

records.nuance: 弟 means one’s younger brother. The sentence says he likes baseball.
records.logic: 弟 is the topic; 野球が好き marks baseball as what he likes.
records.difference: 弟 is younger brother; 兄（あに） is older brother.
records.filipino: nakababatang kapatid na lalaki; mahilig sa baseball ang nakababata kong kapatid na lalaki

records.nuance: 娘 means daughter. Here the speaker says their daughter is in the United States.
records.logic: 私の identifies the speaker’s daughter; にいます states her location.
records.difference: 娘（むすめ） means daughter; 息子（むすこ） means son.
records.filipino: anak na babae; nasa Estados Unidos ang anak kong babae

records.nuance: 若い describes someone or something as young in age or at an early stage. The sentence says he is still young.
records.logic: まだ emphasizes that youth continues at present; です makes the statement polite.
records.difference: 若い means young; 幼い（おさない） often means very young/childlike.

records.kanji_breakdown: 彼 = that; she (character cue); 女 = woman
records.nuance: 彼女 means “she/her” when referring to a woman; it can also mean “girlfriend.” Here the sentence predicates that she is an office worker, so the pronoun sense is intended.
records.logic: 彼女は introduces the person as topic; OLです gives her occupation.
records.difference: 彼女 means she/her in this sentence; with relationship context it can mean girlfriend. 彼（かれ） means he/him or boyfriend.

records.nuance: 彼 means “he/him” or “that man,” and can mean boyfriend in a relationship context. Here he is the speaker’s supervisor.
records.logic: 彼は introduces the person as topic; 私の上司です identifies him as the speaker’s boss/supervisor.
records.difference: 彼 means he/him here; 彼女（かのじょ） means she/her. The deck’s “senior” is broader than 上司, which specifically means supervisor/boss.

records.nuance: ミーティング is a meeting, often a work or group meeting. It began at 9 a.m.
records.logic: 朝9時から marks the starting time; が始まった says the meeting began.
records.difference: ミーティング is a meeting; 会議（かいぎ） is a meeting/conference and often sounds more formal.
records.filipino: pulong; nagsimula ang pulong nang alas-nuwebe ng umaga

records.kanji_breakdown: 自 = self; 分 = part (character cues)
records.nuance: 自分 means oneself; in this instruction it means do your homework on your own/by yourself.
records.logic: で marks how the action is done; 自分 identifies the person themself as doing it.
records.difference: 自分で means by oneself; 一人で means alone, emphasizing being without others.
records.filipino: sarili; ikaw mismo ang gumawa ng takdang-aralin mo

records.kanji_breakdown: 主人 = master/householder; ご = respectful prefix
records.nuance: ご主人 is a respectful way to refer to someone else’s husband. The question politely asks whether he is well.
records.logic: ご adds honorific politeness; は marks the husband as topic, and お元気ですか asks about his health/well-being.
records.difference: ご主人 is respectful and can mean someone else’s husband; 夫（おっと） is a neutral term for one’s own husband when speaking to others.
records.filipino: asawa; mabuti ba ang kalagayan ng asawa mo?

records.nuance: 別 means different, separate, or another. 別の本 means a different/additional book.
records.logic: の links 別 to 本; も adds “also/another” to the prior request.
records.difference: 別の本 means another/different book; 同じ本（おなじほん） means the same book.
records.filipino: iba; pakipakita rin ang ibang libro

records.nuance: 酒 means alcoholic drink in general; it can mean sake specifically in some contexts. Here 酒に強い means she tolerates alcohol well.
records.logic: に marks what she is strong against; 強い describes her ability to handle alcohol.
records.difference: 酒 may mean alcohol generally; 日本酒（にほんしゅ） specifically identifies Japanese rice wine/sake.
records.filipino: alak; matibay siya uminom ng alak

records.kanji_breakdown: つける = turn on; attach (kana verb)
records.nuance: つける has several meanings, including turn on a light or device. With 電気を, it means switch on the light/electricity.
records.logic: 電気 is what is switched on; を marks the affected item and ください makes a request.
records.difference: つける means turn on in this context; 消す（けす） means turn off.

records.nuance: 飛ぶ means to fly or move through the air. A bird is flying in the sentence.
records.logic: 鳥が identifies the bird as the subject; ～ています presents the flight as ongoing.
records.difference: 飛ぶ means fly; 飛ばす（とばす） means make something fly/send it flying.

records.kanji_breakdown: 飛 = fly; 行 = go; 機 = machine (character cues)
records.nuance: 飛行機 means airplane. Here the son likes toy airplanes.
records.logic: 飛行機の modifies おもちゃ; the whole phrase names toys shaped like airplanes, not actual flights.
records.difference: 飛行機 means airplane; 空港（くうこう） means airport.
records.filipino: eroplano; mahilig sa laruang eroplano ang anak ko

records.kanji_breakdown: 願 = wish; request; お = polite prefix
records.nuance: お願い means a request or favor; it is also used in polite expressions asking someone for something. Here the speaker says they have a favor to ask.
records.logic: があります presents the favor/request as something the speaker has; the actual request follows or is understood.
records.difference: お願い is a request/favor; 頼み（たのみ） is a request/ask in a less honorific form.

records.kanji_breakdown: 日 = day; 記 = record (character cues)
records.nuance: 日記 is a diary or journal. 日記を付ける is the expression “keep/write a diary.”
records.logic: 毎日 sets the frequency; を付けています describes the ongoing habit of keeping a diary.
records.difference: 日記 is a diary; 記録（きろく） is a record more generally.
records.filipino: talaarawan; araw-araw akong nagsusulat sa talaarawan

records.nuance: 首 means the neck. The sentence says a giraffe’s neck is long.
records.logic: きりんの identifies whose neck; 長い describes its length.
records.difference: 首 means neck; 頭（あたま） means head.
records.filipino: leeg; mahaba ang leeg ng giraffe

records.nuance: 頭 means head. In 頭が痛い, it refers to the head hurting, i.e. a headache.
records.logic: 今朝から sets when the pain began and continues from; が marks the painful body part.
records.meaning: head; in 頭が痛い, headache/head hurts
records.difference: 頭が痛い means the head hurts; 頭痛（ずつう） is the noun “headache.”
records.filipino: ulo; masakit ang ulo ko mula kaninang umaga

records.nuance: 顔 means face. The sentence says he wiped his face with a towel.
records.logic: タオルで gives the means; 顔を is the part wiped; 拭きました is polite past of wipe.
records.difference: 顔 means face; 頭（あたま） means head.
records.filipino: mukha; pinunasan niya ng tuwalya ang mukha niya

records.nuance: あれ points to something away from both speaker and listener, or otherwise distant in the shared context. The question asks what that thing is.
records.logic: は marks the pointed-at item as topic; 何 asks its identity.
records.difference: あれ points to something away from both; それ often points near the listener or to something already mentioned.

records.nuance: 探す means to look for or search for something. He was looking for the post office.
records.logic: 郵便局を is the target sought; ～ていました presents the search as ongoing in the past.
records.difference: 探す means actively look for; 見つける（みつける） means find what was being sought.

records.nuance: 落ちる means to fall or drop. The proverb 猿も木から落ちる says even monkeys fall from trees, meaning even experts make mistakes.
records.logic: も means “even”; から marks the tree as the place from which one falls.
records.difference: 落ちる is intransitive “fall”; 落とす（おとす） is transitive “drop something.”

records.kanji_breakdown: 手 = hand; 洗 = wash; お = polite prefix
records.nuance: お手洗い is a polite term for a restroom/toilet. The literal hand-washing association makes it a discreet expression.
records.logic: お marks polite usage; the whole compound conventionally names the restroom, not just hand washing.
records.difference: お手洗い is polite; トイレ is a common direct loanword for toilet/restroom.

records.nuance: 冷たい describes something cold to the touch or at a low temperature. Here it modifies a drink the speaker asks for.
records.logic: 飲み物 is the item requested; をください is a polite request for it.
records.difference: 冷たい is cold to the touch; 寒い（さむい） is cold weather or feeling cold.
records.filipino: malamig; pakiabot po ng malamig na inumin

records.nuance: 曇る means become cloudy or overcast. The forecast says it will probably cloud over from around midday tomorrow.
records.logic: 明日は marks tomorrow; 昼頃から means from around noon; でしょう expresses a prediction/probability.
records.difference: 曇る means become cloudy; 曇り（くもり） is cloudiness/overcast weather.
records.filipino: magiging maulap; malamang na magiging maulap bandang tanghali bukas

records.nuance: 神 means a god or deity. The sentence says he believes in God/a god; Japanese does not specify a particular religion.
records.logic: 神を is what he believes in; 信じている describes his continuing belief.
records.difference: 神 can mean a deity/god; 神様（かみさま） is a respectful form. 紙（かみ） means paper.
records.filipino: diyos; naniniwala siya sa isang diyos

records.nuance: まずい means bad-tasting when describing food. It can also mean bad or troublesome in other contexts; here it criticizes the food.
records.logic: 料理は sets the food as topic; the adjective gives a negative evaluation.
records.difference: まずい means bad-tasting; おいしい（美味しい） means tasty/delicious.
records.filipino: hindi masarap; hindi masarap ang pagkain dito

records.nuance: この辺 means this area or around here. The sentence says he lives somewhere in the nearby vicinity.
records.logic: この modifies 辺; に marks the location where he lives.
records.difference: この辺 means around here; 近く（ちかく） means nearby/close by.

records.nuance: 緑 means green or greenery. With たくさんあります in a town, it refers to abundant plants/green spaces.
records.logic: この町には sets the town as location; 緑が marks what is plentiful.
records.difference: 緑 means green/greenery; 草（くさ） specifically means grass.
records.filipino: luntiang halaman; maraming luntiang lugar sa bayang ito

records.nuance: 易しい means easy or simple. Here it describes a problem as fairly easy.
records.logic: この問題は is the topic; かなり intensifies the evaluation to “quite/pretty.”
records.difference: 易しい（やさしい） means easy; 優しい（やさしい） means kind/gentle, the same reading with another kanji.
records.filipino: madali; medyo madali ang problemang ito

records.kanji_breakdown: 留 = stay; remain; 学 = study; 生 = student (character cues)
records.nuance: 留学生 is a student studying abroad. It can refer to an international student, often one studying in a country other than their home country.
records.logic: The compound describes studying while abroad; the sentence simply identifies him as a 留学生.
records.difference: 留学生 means a student studying abroad; 外国人学生（がいこくじんがくせい） specifically means a foreign student, which can overlap but is not identical.

records.nuance: 戻る means return to a previous place or state. The speaker says they are going back to the office now.
records.logic: 会社に marks the return destination; 今 places the action at the present/near future.
records.difference: 戻る means return to a prior place/state; 帰る（かえる） means go home or return to one’s base.

records.nuance: 起こす means to wake someone up or cause someone to rise. The speaker asks someone to wake them at six tomorrow; the object is omitted but understood.
records.logic: 明日、6時に gives the requested time; ～てください asks the listener to do it. Japanese leaves the person being woken unstated.
records.meaning: to wake someone; cause to get up
records.difference: 起こす is transitive “wake someone”; 起きる（おきる） is intransitive “wake up/get up.”

records.nuance: 寝る means to sleep or go to bed. もう寝よう suggests it is time to go to bed now.
records.logic: もう indicates “now/already”; volitional ～よう invites the speaker and listener to do it.
records.difference: 寝る means sleep/go to bed; 起きる（おきる） means wake up/get up.

records.nuance: 甘い describes a sweet taste. The strawberry tastes sweet.
records.logic: この identifies this strawberry; the adjective describes its taste.
records.difference: 甘い means sweet; 辛い（からい） means spicy.
records.filipino: matamis; matamis ang strawberry na ito

records.nuance: こっち is a casual form of こちら. Here it means come here/toward me or this place.
records.logic: に marks the destination; 来てください asks the listener to come.
records.difference: こっち is casual “here/this way”; こちら is more polite.

records.nuance: 辛い means spicy or hot-tasting. With もの it means spicy food/things; he likes them.
records.logic: もの generalizes to spicy food; が好き marks it as what he likes.
records.difference: 辛い（からい） means spicy; 熱い（あつい） means hot in temperature.
records.filipino: maanghang; mahilig siya sa maanghang na pagkain

records.nuance: 誰 asks which person. 誰と asks who the listener would like to meet.
records.logic: と marks the potential meeting partner; 会ってみたい expresses wanting to try meeting/see how it is.
records.difference: 誰に asks to whom; 誰と asks with whom.
records.filipino: sino; sino ang gusto mong makilala balang araw?

records.nuance: 愛する expresses deep love or affection. Here the speaker says they love their family.
records.logic: 家族を marks the people loved; ～ています describes an ongoing feeling/state.
records.difference: 愛する is love deeply; 好き（すき） means like/be fond of, often less intense.

records.nuance: 酸っぱい describes a sharp sour taste. The sentence says these grapes taste sour.
records.logic: このぶどう identifies the fruit; the adjective describes its flavor.
records.difference: 酸っぱい means sour; 甘い（あまい） means sweet.
records.filipino: maasim; maasim ang ubas na ito

records.nuance: 呼ぶ means call or summon someone. Here it means call the waiter over.
records.logic: ウェイターを marks who is called; ～ましょう proposes doing it together.
records.difference: 呼ぶ means call someone over; 電話する（でんわする） means make a phone call.

records.nuance: 胸 means chest. With 痛みがあります, it indicates a slight chest pain.
records.logic: 胸に marks where the pain is; 少し softens the degree.
records.difference: 胸 means chest; 背中（せなか） means back.
records.filipino: dibdib; medyo masakit ang dibdib ko

records.kanji_breakdown: 片 = one side/part; 仮 = provisional; 名 = name (character cues)
records.nuance: 片仮名 is katakana, one of the Japanese syllabaries. The request is to write the name using katakana.
records.logic: で marks the writing system/manner; 書いてください requests that the name be written that way.
records.difference: 片仮名 means katakana; 平仮名（ひらがな） means hiragana.
records.filipino: katakana; isulat ang pangalan sa katakana

records.nuance: 悲しい describes sadness or sorrow. Here it describes the movie’s emotional effect.
records.logic: その映画は sets the movie as topic; past 悲しかった says it was sad.
records.difference: 悲しい means sad; 寂しい（さびしい） means lonely or lonesome.

records.kanji_breakdown: あそこ = over there; that place
records.nuance: あそこ points to a place away from both speaker and listener. Here a bus stop is located over there.
records.logic: に marks the location where the bus stop exists; あります states its presence.
records.difference: あそこ means over there; ここ means here near the speaker.
records.filipino: doon; may hintuan ng bus doon

records.kanji_breakdown: 手 = hand; help (character cue); 伝 = convey/assist (character cue)
records.nuance: 手伝う means help someone with a task. 私が手伝いましょう offers the speaker’s help.
records.logic: 私が emphasizes the speaker as the helper; ～ましょう makes an offer/proposal.
records.difference: 手伝う means help with a task; 助ける（たすける） often means help/rescue someone from difficulty.
records.filipino: tutulungan kita; ako na ang tutulong

records.nuance: 浴びる means to bathe in or have something poured over oneself. In シャワーを浴びる it means take a shower.
records.logic: シャワーを is the thing received; 朝 sets when the speaker showers.
records.difference: シャワーを浴びる means take a shower; 入浴する（にゅうよくする） means bathe/soak in a bath.
records.filipino: maligo sa shower; naliligo ako tuwing umaga

records.nuance: 渇く means become thirsty or dry. のどが渇く is the common expression for being thirsty.
records.logic: のど is the body part that feels dry; past 渇きました conveys the resulting state of thirst.
records.difference: のどが渇く means be thirsty; 乾く（かわく） means become dry, as clothes or ground do.

records.nuance: 髪の毛 means the hair on one’s head. 伸びたね says it has grown/looks longer.
records.logic: が marks the hair as what grew; ね invites agreement or shared observation.
records.difference: 髪の毛 means head hair; 毛（け） can mean hair/fur more generally.
records.filipino: buhok; humaba ang buhok mo, ano?

records.nuance: おいしい describes food or drink as tasty. Here it compliments the cake as delicious.
records.logic: このケーキ identifies the food; ね seeks friendly agreement.
records.difference: おいしい means tasty; まずい means bad-tasting.
records.filipino: masarap; masarap ang cake na ito, ano?

records.nuance: 腕 means an arm; it can also mean skill or ability in other contexts. Here 太い describes his arms as thick/muscular.
records.logic: 彼の identifies whose arms; 太い describes their physical build.
records.difference: 腕 means arm here; 手（て） is hand. The deck “big arms” paraphrases thick/muscular arms.
records.filipino: braso; malaki ang mga braso niya

records.nuance: 僕 is an informal first-person pronoun traditionally associated with male speakers, often used by boys and men. The sentence means “I am a student.”
records.logic: 僕は marks the speaker as topic; 学生です gives their status.
records.difference: 僕 is often masculine/informal; 私（わたし） is more broadly usable and usually more neutral/polite.

records.nuance: だめ means no good, unacceptable, or hopeless depending on context. Here だめな男 is a strongly negative judgment of a man.
records.logic: な links the adjective-like だめ to 男; the sentence makes a critical evaluation.
records.difference: だめ means no good; 悪い（わるい） means bad and is more general.
records.filipino: walang kwenta; wala siyang silbi bilang lalaki

records.nuance: きれい can mean beautiful or clean. Describing 彼女 as とてもきれいだ means she is very beautiful.
records.logic: 彼女は is the person described; とても intensifies the compliment.
records.difference: きれい means beautiful here; 美しい（うつくしい） is a more formal/literary “beautiful.”

records.nuance: 嬉しい describes the speaker’s happiness or gladness about an event. 彼に会えて嬉しかった means they were glad they got to meet him.
records.logic: 会えて is the potential/fortunate form of meet, giving the reason for the feeling; past 嬉しかった reports that reaction.
records.difference: 嬉しい is glad about something; 楽しい（たのしい） describes an enjoyable experience.

records.nuance: 七 is the number seven. Here it counts the members of the group.
records.logic: 全部で means in total; 七人 counts seven people, using the 人 counter.
records.difference: 七 can be read しち or なな; this note’s reading is しち. 七月 is しちがつ, while some compounds prefer なな for clarity.
records.filipino: pito; pito lahat ang miyembro ng grupo

records.nuance: 九 is the number nine. In 九月 it is read くがつ, meaning September.
records.logic: 月 is the month counter; the established calendar reading is くがつ.
records.difference: 九 is commonly read きゅう or く; 九月 is くがつ. Preserve this note’s く.
records.filipino: siyam; plano kong pumunta sa Setyembre

records.nuance: 億 is the unit one hundred million. 65億人 means 6.5 billion people.
records.logic: 65 multiplied by 100 million gives 6.5 billion; 人 counts people.
records.difference: 億 is 100 million; 万（まん） is 10,000.
records.filipino: bilyon; 6.5 bilyon ang populasyon ng mundo

records.nuance: 寺 means a Buddhist temple. The sentence says there is an old temple over there.
records.logic: あそこに marks its location; 古い modifies the temple; お is a polite prefix before 寺 in お寺.
records.difference: 寺（てら） means Buddhist temple; 神社（じんじゃ） is a Shinto shrine.
records.filipino: templong Budista; may lumang templo roon

records.nuance: ドル is the dollar currency unit. The sentence says these clothes cost 300 dollars.
records.logic: 300 modifies ドル as the price; しました here expresses the cost.
records.difference: ドル is a dollar; 円（えん） is the Japanese yen.
records.filipino: dolyar; nagkakahalaga ng 300 dolyar ang mga damit na ito

records.nuance: 日 can mean sun, day, or daylight. In 夏は日が長い it refers to daylight duration: summer days are long.
records.logic: 夏は sets summer as topic; 日が長い describes the span of daylight as long.
records.difference: 日が長い means the days/daylight are long; 日光（にっこう） means sunlight.

records.nuance: 火 means fire. 火を消して tells someone to put the fire out.
records.logic: を marks fire as what should be extinguished; 消して is a casual request/command.
records.difference: 火 means fire; 火事（かじ） means a fire/disastrous conflagration.

records.nuance: 木 means a tree or wood. Here it is a tree that fell because of a typhoon.
records.logic: 台風で gives the cause; が marks the tree that fell.
records.difference: 木 means tree/wood; 森（もり） means forest.
records.filipino: puno; bumagsak ang puno dahil sa bagyo

records.nuance: 金（きん） means gold. The sentence describes a gold necklace she is wearing; the same kanji has other readings and meanings.
records.logic: 金の modifies ネックレス to specify its material/color; しています describes wearing it.
records.difference: 金（きん） is gold; 銀（ぎん） is silver. 金 can also be read かね for money or きん／こん in other words.
records.filipino: ginto; may suot siyang kuwintas na ginto

records.nuance: システム is a system or organized set of parts. 全てのシステムが停止した says all systems stopped/shut down.
records.logic: 全ての applies to the complete set; 停止した reports the systems stopped operating.
records.difference: システム is a system; 機械（きかい） is a machine.
records.filipino: sistema; huminto ang lahat ng sistema

records.nuance: 分（ぶん） means a portion or share. This cake is the portion intended for the listener.
records.logic: あなたの分 is the share assigned to you; です identifies this cake as that portion.
records.difference: 分（ぶん） is a share/portion here; 分ける（わける） is to divide/share something.
records.filipino: parte; para sa iyo ang bahaging ito ng cake

records.nuance: 分ける means divide or distribute something among people. Here everyone shared the sweets.
records.logic: お菓子を is what is divided; みんなで marks the group doing it together; past 分けました reports completion.
records.difference: 分ける is transitive “divide/share something”; 分かれる（わかれる） means split/separate into parts.
records.filipino: ipamahagi; pinaghati-hatian namin ang mga kendi

records.nuance: コンピュータ is a computer. The sentence says the speaker bought a new computer.
records.logic: 新しい modifies the computer; を marks it as what was bought.
records.difference: コンピュータ means computer; パソコン usually means a personal computer.
records.filipino: computer; bumili ako ng bagong computer

records.nuance: 何 asks what something is. In 質問は何ですか, it asks what the question is.
records.logic: 質問は sets “question” as topic; 何 asks for its content or identity.
records.difference: 何 is read なん here; it is also commonly read なに in other contexts.

records.kanji_breakdown: 先 = previous; ahead; 週 = week
records.nuance: 先週 means last week. The sentence says the speaker went to the sea/beach last week.
records.logic: 先 modifies 週 to mean the preceding week; は marks the time as topic.
records.difference: 先週 is last week; 来週（らいしゅう） is next week.
records.filipino: noong nakaraang linggo; pumunta ako sa tabing-dagat noong nakaraang linggo

records.nuance: 今まで means until now or up to this point. The question asks where the listener has been until now.
records.logic: 今 marks the present reference point; まで marks the endpoint of the time span.
records.difference: 今まで means until now; これまで is a similar expression, often a little more formal.
records.filipino: hanggang ngayon; nasaan ka hanggang ngayon?

records.nuance: 来月 means next month. The speaker will become a university student starting then.
records.logic: から marks the starting point; 大学生になります describes the change in status.
records.difference: 来月 means next month; 先月（せんげつ） means last month.
records.filipino: sa susunod na buwan; magiging estudyante ako sa unibersidad simula sa susunod na buwan

records.nuance: ロボット is a robot. The sentence says he is doing research on robots.
records.logic: ロボットの研究 is research about robots; をしています describes his ongoing research activity.
records.difference: ロボット means robot; 機械（きかい） means machine more generally.
records.filipino: robot; nagsasaliksik siya tungkol sa mga robot

records.nuance: 行き（ゆき） after a place name indicates a train or other service bound for that destination. 東京行き means Tokyo-bound.
records.logic: 東京 modifies 行き; the train is identified by its destination.
records.meaning: bound for; going to (as a route/service label)
records.difference: 東京行き means bound for Tokyo; 東京から means from Tokyo. 行き can also be read いき in other usages.
records.filipino: papuntang Tokyo; sumakay ako sa tren na papuntang Tokyo

records.nuance: 帰り means the return trip or way home/back. 仕事の帰りに means on the way home from work.
records.logic: 仕事の links the return trip to work; に marks when the beer was drunk.
records.meaning: return trip; way back; on the way home
records.difference: 帰り is the way back; 行き（ゆき） is the outbound/bound-for trip.
records.filipino: pauwi; uminom ako ng beer pauwi mula sa trabaho

records.nuance: 大きさ means size or dimensions. The speaker asks for an envelope of this size.
records.logic: この modifies 大きさ; の links the size to the envelope; 欲しい expresses wanting one.
records.difference: 大きさ is size; 大きい（おおきい） is the adjective “big.”
records.filipino: laki; gusto ko ng sobreng ganito kalaki

records.nuance: 中 means inside or the interior. The wallet is inside the drawer.
records.logic: 引き出しの中 identifies the drawer’s interior; に marks the location where the wallet exists.
records.difference: 中（なか） means inside; 外（そと） means outside. It can also mean middle depending on context.
records.filipino: loob; nasa loob ng drawer ang pitaka ko

records.nuance: パソコン is a personal computer (PC). The sentence says he owns two PCs.
records.logic: 2台 counts machines/computers; を持っています means he has/owns them.
records.difference: パソコン is a personal computer; コンピュータ can mean computers more generally.
records.filipino: personal computer; mayroon siyang dalawang personal computer

records.nuance: 多く means many or a large number/amount. 多くの人 means many people.
records.logic: 毎年 marks recurrence each year; 多くの modifies 人, who travel abroad.
records.difference: 多くの人 means many people; 少ない（すくない） means few.
records.filipino: marami; maraming tao ang naglalakbay sa ibang bansa bawat taon

records.nuance: プログラム can mean a program, schedule, or printed event guide. At reception, it refers to a program handout the visitor received.
records.logic: 受付で marks where it was received; 受け取った reports getting it.
records.difference: プログラム is a program/event guide; 予定表（よていひょう） is a schedule/list of plans.
records.filipino: programa; nakuha ko ang programa sa reception

records.nuance: 下り（くだり） train refers to the route’s downbound/outbound direction, often away from a central hub; it does not simply mean physically downhill.
records.logic: 下り modifies 電車; 発車します says the train will depart soon.
records.difference: 下り（くだり） is downbound; 上り（のぼり） is the corresponding upbound direction. The reference direction depends on the railway route.
records.filipino: papalabas na tren; malapit nang umalis ang tren na biyaheng palabas

records.nuance: 方（かた） is a polite way to refer to a person. 次の方 means the next person in line; どうぞ invites them forward.
records.logic: 次の modifies the person as next; どうぞ is a courteous prompt.
records.difference: 方（かた） means person politely here; 方（ほう） can mean direction or side.
records.filipino: susunod na po; maaari na ang susunod

records.nuance: テレビ means television or TV as a device/program medium. The speaker says they do not watch much TV.
records.logic: あまり with a negative means not much/not often; を marks TV as what is watched.
records.difference: テレビ is television; 映画（えいが） means a movie/film.
records.filipino: telebisyon; hindi ako masyadong nanonood ng TV

records.nuance: 外 means outside or outdoors. 外は暑いよ says it is hot outside.
records.logic: は sets outside as topic; 暑い describes the weather, and よ adds an informing/emphatic tone.
records.difference: 外 means outside; 中（なか） means inside.

records.nuance: 休み means a rest, break, holiday, or day off. Here it means the speaker has no work on Thursday.
records.logic: 木曜日は sets Thursday as topic; 仕事が休み is a common way to say work is off/a day off.
records.difference: 休み is a day off/rest; 休む（やすむ） is to rest or take time off.
records.filipino: day off; walang pasok sa trabaho tuwing Huwebes

records.nuance: ソフト is short for software in this context. The sentence says this software can be used to study Japanese.
records.logic: このソフトで marks the tool used; ことができます expresses ability/possibility.
records.difference: ソフト means software here; ハードウェア means hardware. In other contexts ソフト can mean soft or soft-serve.
records.filipino: software; maaari kang mag-aral ng Hapon gamit ang software na ito

records.nuance: 入り口 means entrance or entryway. The sentence says the entrance is over there.
records.logic: The compound names the opening through which one enters; は marks it as the topic.
records.difference: 入り口 is entrance; 出口（でぐち） is exit.
records.filipino: pasukan; naroon sa banda roon ang pasukan

records.nuance: 左手 means the left hand. The sentence says she writes using her left hand, i.e. she is left-handed.
records.logic: で marks the hand used as the means; 字を書く means write characters.
records.difference: 左手（ひだりて） means left hand; 右手（みぎて） means right hand.
records.filipino: kaliwang kamay; nagsusulat siya gamit ang kaliwang kamay

records.nuance: これら refers to several things near the speaker or already in focus. Here it refers to the issues they will discuss today.
records.logic: これらの modifies 問題; について marks the topic, and 話し合います means discuss together.
records.difference: これら refers to these items; それら often refers to those items away from the speaker or previously mentioned.
records.filipino: mga ito; pag-uusapan natin ngayon ang mga isyung ito

records.nuance: 山 means a mountain. The sentence describes the mountain air as clean/fresh.
records.logic: 山の links the air to the mountain; きれい describes its quality.
records.difference: 山 is a mountain; 丘（おか） is a hill.
records.filipino: bundok; malinis ang hangin sa bundok

records.nuance: 川 means a river or stream. 小さな describes it as small; the speaker crossed it.
records.logic: を marks the river as the route crossed; 渡りました reports completing the crossing.
records.difference: 川 means river/stream; 橋（はし） means bridge, the structure used to cross one.
records.filipino: ilog; tumawid ako sa maliit na ilog

records.nuance: いずれ means someday, eventually, or at some point in the future. Here it expresses a vague future occasion to meet again.
records.logic: また means again; いずれ leaves when the next meeting will happen unspecified.
records.difference: いずれ is a somewhat formal “sometime/eventually”; いつか is a common “someday.”
records.filipino: balang araw; magkita tayong muli balang araw

records.nuance: 空（そら） means the sky. 空が真っ青 describes the sky as a vivid blue.
records.logic: が marks the sky as what is blue; 真っ青 intensifies the color.
records.difference: 空（そら） means sky; 空（から／くう） can mean empty or void in other words.
records.filipino: langit; matingkad na bughaw ang langit

records.kanji_breakdown: あまり = not very (with negative); too much (other contexts)
records.nuance: あまり with a negative means not very or not much. The beer is not very good.
records.logic: あまり modifies 美味しくありません; the negative form makes this a softened negative evaluation.
records.difference: あまり…ない means not very/not much; とても means very.
records.filipino: hindi gaanong masarap; hindi gaanong masarap ang beer na ito

records.nuance: 毎日 means every day. The sentence says they take a walk daily.
records.logic: 毎日 sets the repeated frequency; 散歩をします describes the regular activity.
records.difference: 毎日 is every day; 毎週（まいしゅう） is every week.

records.nuance: 毎年 means every year. The sentence says the salary goes up each year.
records.logic: 毎年 sets the recurring time; 給料が上がる says salary rises.
records.difference: 毎年 can be read まいねん or まいとし; preserve this note’s まいねん. 今年（ことし） means this year.
records.filipino: taun-taon; tumataas ang suweldo ko bawat taon

records.nuance: 毎週 means every week. The speaker calls their mother weekly.
records.logic: 母に marks the person called; 毎週 gives the frequency of the call.
records.difference: 毎週 is every week; 毎日（まいにち） is every day.
records.filipino: linggu-linggo; tinatawagan ko ang nanay ko linggu-linggo

records.kanji_breakdown: 田 = rice field (word cue); んぼ is kana
records.nuance: 田んぼ is a rice paddy or rice field. The sentence says many rice fields are in this area.
records.logic: この辺は sets the vicinity as topic; がたくさんあります states that many fields are present.
records.difference: 田んぼ is a rice paddy; 畑（はたけ） is a field for crops other than rice.
records.filipino: palayan; maraming palayan sa paligid na ito

records.nuance: 花 means flower. The sentence says beautiful flowers bloomed.
records.logic: きれいな modifies 花; 咲きました means bloomed/flowered.
records.difference: 花 means flower; 木（き） means tree.

records.kanji_breakdown: サービス = service; customer service
records.nuance: サービス means service or customer care. Here この店はサービスがいい praises the service at the store.
records.logic: 店 is the topic; サービスがいい evaluates how good the customer service is.
records.difference: サービス means service here; 無料（むりょう） means free of charge.
records.filipino: serbisyo; maganda ang serbisyo sa tindahang ito

records.nuance: 男の子 means a boy or male child. The boys are playing soccer.
records.logic: たち marks a group of boys; が identifies them as the players.
records.difference: 男の子 means boy; 女の子（おんなのこ） means girl.
records.filipino: mga batang lalaki; naglalaro ng soccer ang mga batang lalaki

records.kanji_breakdown: 私 = I; たち = plural/group marker
records.nuance: 私たち means we/us, referring to the speaker and at least one other person. The sentence says they will marry next month.
records.logic: 私たち is the subject/topic; 来月 sets when 結婚します will happen.
records.difference: 私たち means we; 私（わたし） means I/me.
records.filipino: kami; ikakasal kami sa susunod na buwan

records.nuance: グループ is a group. Here a group of students came to the shop.
records.logic: 学生の modifies グループ; が marks the group as the subject that came.
records.difference: グループ is a group; 集団（しゅうだん） is a more formal/general collective.
records.filipino: grupo; dumating sa tindahan ang grupo ng mga estudyante

records.nuance: 家（いえ） means a house or home as a building/place. The speaker identifies this place as their house.
records.logic: ここが sets “here” as the subject being identified; 私の家 is my house.
records.difference: 家（いえ） often means house/building; 家（うち） often means one’s home/household, though meanings overlap.

records.nuance: ホテル is a hotel. The sentence says the speaker just arrived there.
records.logic: に marks the destination; 今 marks the arrival as just now/recent.
records.difference: ホテル is a hotel; 旅館（りょかん） is a traditional Japanese inn.
records.filipino: hotel; kararating ko lang sa hotel

records.nuance: 雪 means snow. 雪が降りました says snow fell/it snowed at Christmas.
records.logic: クリスマスに gives the time; 雪が降る is the ordinary expression for snow falling.
records.difference: 雪 means snow; 雨（あめ） means rain.
records.filipino: niyebe; umulan ng niyebe noong Pasko

records.kanji_breakdown: 青 = blue; green in some conventional categories
records.nuance: 青い means blue and can cover some colors called green in conventional Japanese expressions. Here it describes the sea as very blue.
records.logic: ここの海 is the sea here; とても intensifies the color.
records.difference: 青い means blue; 緑（みどり） is green, though 青 can appear in conventional green-light expressions.

records.kanji_breakdown: 青 = blue; green in some conventional categories
records.nuance: 青 means the color blue; it can also be used in established expressions for some things English calls green. Here it is the speaker’s favorite color.
records.logic: 好きな色は sets the topic as favorite color; 青です identifies it.
records.difference: 青 means blue; 緑（みどり） means green. Traffic lights are still conventionally called 青信号（あおしんごう）.
records.filipino: asul; asul ang paborito kong kulay

records.nuance: 晴れ is clear/sunny weather. 明日の天気は晴れです is a forecast that tomorrow will be sunny/clear.
records.logic: 明日の天気 sets tomorrow’s weather as topic; 晴れ is the forecast condition.
records.difference: 晴れ is clear/sunny weather; 晴れる（はれる） means the weather clears/becomes sunny.

records.kanji_breakdown: やはり = as expected; after all; still
records.nuance: やはり indicates that something happened as expected or confirms a prior impression. Here he was late after all/as expected.
records.logic: 彼は遅刻しました is the event; やはり marks it as consistent with expectation.
records.difference: やはり is a slightly formal form of やっぱり; both often mean as expected/after all.
records.filipino: gaya ng inaasahan; nahuli pa rin siya, gaya ng inaasahan

records.nuance: 暗い means dark or dim. It describes the eastern sky as dark.
records.logic: 東の空 is the sky in the east; です makes the observation polite.
records.difference: 暗い means dark; 明るい（あかるい） means bright/light.
records.filipino: madilim; madilim ang langit sa silangan

records.nuance: 東 means east. 東の空 is the sky in the east, which the sentence says is dark.
records.logic: の links direction to the sky; 東 specifies its location.
records.difference: 東 is east; 西（にし） is west.
records.filipino: silangan; madilim ang langit sa silangan

records.nuance: 西 means west. The sentence says the sun sets in the west.
records.logic: に marks the direction/location where the sun sets.
records.difference: 西 is west; 東（ひがし） is east.
records.filipino: kanluran; lumulubog ang araw sa kanluran

records.kanji_breakdown: つまり = in short; that is
records.nuance: つまり draws a conclusion or restates a point as “so” or “in other words.” Here the speaker concludes that the other person knows nothing.
records.logic: The sentence summarizes what the speaker has inferred; つまり signals that conclusion.
records.difference: つまり summarizes or draws a conclusion; 要するに（ようするに） is a similar “in short.”
records.filipino: sa madaling salita; kung gayon, wala ka palang alam

records.nuance: 北 means north. Russia is located north of Japan in the sentence.
records.logic: 日本の北 gives the reference point and direction; にあります states location.
records.difference: 北 is north; 南（みなみ） is south.
records.filipino: hilaga; nasa hilaga ng Japan ang Russia

records.nuance: ビル is a building, commonly a multistory office or commercial building. Here the speaker’s company is on its eighth floor.
records.logic: あのビルの8階 identifies the floor where the company is located; the sentence uses this as a location complement without に.
records.difference: ビル means a building; 建物（たてもの） is a general word for a building.
records.filipino: gusaling iyon; nasa ikawalong palapag ng gusaling iyon ang opisina ng kompanya ko

records.nuance: 聞こえる means a sound reaches the ear or is audible, often without emphasizing deliberate listening. The TV sound can be heard from the next room.
records.logic: 隣の部屋から marks where the sound comes from; 音が聞こえる describes it as audible.
records.meaning: to be audible; can be heard
records.difference: 聞こえる means be audible; 聞く（きく） means actively listen or ask.
records.filipino: marinig; naririnig ang tunog ng TV mula sa katabing kuwarto

records.kanji_breakdown: 人 = person; 間 = interval/space (character cues)
records.nuance: 人間 means a human being or humankind. 人間の心 means the human mind/heart is complex.
records.logic: 人間の links the human species to 心; 複雑 describes that inner life as complex.
records.difference: 人間 means a human being; 人（ひと） means a person/persons more generally.
records.filipino: tao; masalimuot ang isip ng tao

records.nuance: かつて refers to an earlier time in the past. Here it recalls the period when the speaker was a student.
records.logic: 私が学生だった頃 identifies that past period; かつて marks it as formerly/once.
records.difference: かつて means once/formerly; いずれ（いずれ） means someday/eventually.
records.filipino: noong panahong estudyante pa ako; noong ako ay estudyante pa

records.nuance: 高さ is the height of something. Here it gives Mt. Fuji’s elevation as 3,776 meters.
records.logic: 富士山の identifies what is measured; the number and meters state the height.
records.difference: 高さ is height as a measured property; 高い（たかい） is the adjective high/tall.
records.filipino: taas; 3,776 metro ang taas ng Mt. Fuji

records.nuance: 初めて means for the first time. The speaker says this is their first time coming to Tokyo.
records.logic: 東京に来るの nominalizes coming to Tokyo; 初めて evaluates that experience as new.
records.difference: 初めて means for the first time; 最初（さいしょ） means the beginning/first in a sequence.
records.filipino: sa unang pagkakataon; unang beses ko itong pagpunta sa Tokyo

records.nuance: スポーツ means sports or a sport. The Japanese asks whether the listener does/practices any sports; it does not ask “which sport.”
records.logic: 何か means any/some; スポーツをしています asks whether they participate in a sport.
records.difference: スポーツをする means do/play a sport; 試合（しあい） means a match/game.
records.filipino: isport; may nilalaro ka bang isport?

records.kanji_breakdown: なぜ = why; for what reason
records.nuance: なぜ asks the reason for something. Here it asks why the person did not come.
records.logic: 来なかった is negative past; casual の invites an explanation.
records.difference: なぜ asks why; いつ asks when. なぜ is often more direct/formal than どうして.

records.nuance: 牛 means a cow or cattle. Here one cow is eating grass.
records.logic: が marks the cow as subject; 草を食べています describes its ongoing action.
records.difference: 牛（うし） means cow/cattle; 牛肉（ぎゅうにく） means beef.
records.filipino: baka; kumakain ng damo ang baka

records.nuance: 半分 means one half or half of something. The speaker gave a friend half of the sweets.
records.logic: お菓子を is what was divided; 友達に marks the recipient; 半分 gives the amount.
records.difference: 半分 is half; 全部（ぜんぶ） is all/the whole amount.
records.filipino: kalahati; ibinigay ko sa kaibigan ko ang kalahati ng mga kendi

records.nuance: 昼休み is the midday break or lunch break. The speaker went to the park during that break.
records.logic: に marks when the outing happened; 公園に行った gives the activity.
records.difference: 昼休み is a lunch/midday break; 休み時間（やすみじかん） is a break period more generally.
records.filipino: tanghaling pahinga; pumunta ako sa parke noong lunch break

records.nuance: 毎晩 means every evening or every night. The sentence says the older sister writes in her diary nightly.
records.logic: 毎晩 sets the repeated time; 日記を書いています describes her continuing habit.
records.difference: 毎晩 is every evening/night; 毎朝（まいあさ） is every morning.
records.filipino: gabi-gabi; nagsusulat sa talaarawan ang ate ko gabi-gabi

records.nuance: やっと means finally, often after waiting, effort, or delay. Here the work has at last finished.
records.logic: 仕事が終わりました is the completed event; やっと conveys relief or that it took a while.
records.difference: やっと emphasizes reaching an outcome after difficulty/wait; ついに（ついに） means finally/eventually, often more neutral or dramatic.
records.filipino: sa wakas; sa wakas natapos ko ang trabaho

records.nuance: ニュース means news or a news broadcast. The sentence asks whether the listener watched the evening news.
records.logic: 夜の specifies the evening broadcast; を見ましたか asks whether they watched/saw it.
records.difference: ニュース is news; 新聞（しんぶん） is a newspaper.
records.filipino: balitang panggabi; napanood mo ba ang balitang panggabi?

records.nuance: 話 can mean a conversation, subject, or story. Here あなたの話 is the story/things the listener told, and it is interesting.
records.logic: あなたの links the talk/story to the listener; 面白い evaluates it.
records.difference: 話（はなし） means story/talk; 話す（はなす） is the verb speak/tell.

records.nuance: ビデオ means video; in ビデオに撮る it refers to recording something on video. The speaker recorded the program.
records.logic: その番組 is the program recorded; ビデオに撮った is the recording expression.
records.difference: ビデオに撮る means record on video; 録画する（ろくがする） is a general verb for video-record.
records.filipino: video; ni-record ko sa video ang palabas na iyon

records.kanji_breakdown: 英 = England/English; 語 = language (character cues)
records.nuance: 英語 means the English language. It can refer to the language being used (英語を話す) or to English as a school subject; context determines which.
records.logic: 英語が is the language one can speak; 話せますか is the potential form of speak in a question.
records.difference: 英語 means English; 日本語（にほんご） means Japanese.
records.filipino: Ingles; marunong ka bang magsalita ng Ingles?

records.kanji_breakdown: ローマ = Rome/Roman; 字 = letter/script
records.nuance: ローマ字 means Roman letters or the Roman alphabet as used to write Japanese/other words. The request asks for the name to be written in Roman letters.
records.logic: で marks the writing system/manner; 名前を書いてください is a polite request.
records.difference: ローマ字 is Roman-letter writing; カタカナ is a Japanese syllabary.
records.filipino: mga titik Romano; pakisulat ang pangalan gamit ang mga titik Romano

records.nuance: 字 means a written character or handwriting. Here the request is to write the characters larger.
records.logic: もっと大きく modifies how to write; 字を書いてください asks the listener to write characters.
records.difference: 字 means written character/handwriting; 文字（もじ） is a more explicit word for written characters/text.
records.filipino: sulat; pakisulat nang mas malaki ang mga letra

records.kanji_breakdown: マンション = apartment/condominium building (Japan usage)
records.nuance: In Japanese, マンション usually means a multi-unit apartment or condominium building, not a large detached mansion. He lives in one.
records.logic: に marks the residence location; 住んでいます describes where he lives.
records.difference: マンション in Japanese is an apartment/condominium building; English “mansion” is a large luxury house.
records.filipino: condominium; nakatira siya sa isang apartment building

records.nuance: ガス means gas, such as a household gas supply. Here the gas supply stopped because of an earthquake.
records.logic: 地震で gives the cause; ガスが止まった describes the supply as stopping, without naming an agent.
records.difference: ガス is gas; 電気（でんき） is electricity.
records.filipino: gas; naputol ang suplay ng gas dahil sa lindol

records.kanji_breakdown: 会 = meet; 社 = company/shrine (character cues)
records.nuance: 会社 means a company or business. With 勤めています it means he works for a small company.
records.logic: 小さな modifies company; に勤める is the pattern for being employed at/with an organization.
records.difference: 会社 is a company; 会社員（かいしゃいん） is a company employee.
records.filipino: kompanya; nagtatrabaho siya sa isang maliit na kompanya

records.kanji_breakdown: サラリーマン = salaried company employee
records.nuance: サラリーマン traditionally refers to a salaried company employee, often a male office worker. In this sentence it describes the father’s occupation.
records.logic: 父は sets father as topic; サラリーマンです identifies his work role.
records.difference: サラリーマン is a salaried company worker; 会社員（かいしゃいん） is a more neutral/general company employee term.
records.filipino: empleyado sa kompanya; empleyado sa kompanya ang tatay ko

records.kanji_breakdown: 電 = electricity; 話 = talk (character cues)
records.nuance: 電話 means a telephone or phone call. あとで電話します means the speaker will call later.
records.logic: 電話する is the expression for making a call; the person called is understood from context.
records.difference: 電話 is a phone/call; 電話番号（でんわばんごう） is a phone number.

records.nuance: バス is a bus. バスで行こう suggests going by bus together.
records.logic: で marks the means of transport; 行こう is a casual proposal including the speaker.
records.difference: バス is a bus; 電車（でんしゃ） is a train.

records.nuance: 通り means a street or road. This street is lively/busy.
records.logic: この identifies the street; にぎやか describes its lively atmosphere.
records.difference: 通り is a street; 道（みち） is a general word for a road/path.

records.nuance: クラス means a class/group of students. The sentence says each class at this school has 30 students.
records.logic: 1クラス30人 is a compact count expression: 30 people per class.
records.difference: クラス is a class; 授業（じゅぎょう） is a lesson/class session.
records.filipino: klase; may 30 estudyante sa bawat klase sa paaralang ito

records.nuance: トラック means a truck. The question asks whether the listener can drive one.
records.logic: を marks the vehicle driven; 運転できますか asks about ability.
records.difference: トラック means truck; 車（くるま） is a car/vehicle more generally.
records.filipino: trak; marunong ka bang magmaneho ng trak?

records.nuance: 他 means other or additional things. In その他, it means the remaining/other category.
records.logic: その他は contrasts 留学生 from Asia with those from other regions; は marks that category.
records.difference: 他（た） in その他 means other; 別（べつ） means different/separate.
records.filipino: iba pa; ang natitirang 30 porsiyento ay mula sa ibang rehiyon

records.nuance: パーティー is a party or social gathering. 開きます means the speaker will host/hold one at home tomorrow.
records.logic: うちで marks the location; を開く is a common way to hold a party/event.
records.difference: パーティー is a party; 会議（かいぎ） is a meeting/conference.
records.filipino: party; magdaraos ako ng party bukas sa bahay

records.nuance: 止める（とめる） means to stop something or make it stop. 車を止めて asks someone to stop the car.
records.logic: 車を marks the object whose movement should stop; て-form is a casual request/command.
records.difference: 止める（とめる） is transitive “stop something”; 止まる（とまる） is “come to a stop.”

records.nuance: 止まる（とまる） means come to a stop or cease. The train stopped because of an accident.
records.logic: 電車が is what stopped; 事故で gives the cause.
records.meaning: to stop; come to a stop; cease
records.difference: 止まる（とまる） is intransitive “stop”; 止める（とめる） is transitive “stop something.”
records.filipino: huminto; huminto ang tren dahil sa aksidente

records.nuance: 渡る means cross from one side to another. The group walked across a bridge.
records.logic: 橋を marks the route crossed; 歩いて says they did so on foot.
records.difference: 渡る means cross; 渡す（わたす） means hand/pass something across or to someone.
records.filipino: tumawid; naglakad kami patawid sa tulay

records.nuance: ガラス means glass as a material. The sentence says the speaker bought a crystal-glass vase.
records.logic: クリスタルガラスの modifies 花瓶 by material; を買いました reports buying it.
records.difference: ガラス is glass material; コップ is a drinking glass/cup.
records.filipino: salamin; bumili ako ng plorera na yari sa kristal na salamin

records.nuance: コース means a course of study or a route, depending on context. 日本語コース is a Japanese-language course the speaker is taking.
records.logic: 日本語 modifies コース; を取っています means be enrolled in/take it.
records.difference: コース is a course here; 授業（じゅぎょう） is a class/lesson session.
records.filipino: kurso; kumukuha ako ng kurso sa wikang Hapon

records.nuance: 長さ means length as a measurable dimension. The cable is one meter long.
records.logic: このケーブルの identifies what is measured; 1メートル states the length.
records.difference: 長さ is length; 長い（ながい） is the adjective long.
records.filipino: haba; isang metro ang haba ng kable na ito

records.nuance: アパート means an apartment or apartment building. The sentence says he lives in one.
records.logic: に marks the residence; 住んでいます describes where he lives.
records.difference: アパート and マンション both refer to multi-unit housing in Japan; usage distinctions can depend on building type and market convention.

records.kanji_breakdown: 広 = wide; broad; 広さ = area/extent
records.nuance: 広さ means the size or floor area of a place. The question asks how large the house is.
records.logic: その家の identifies the property measured; どれぐらい asks to what extent/degree.
records.difference: 広さ is area/extent; 広い（ひろい） means wide or spacious.
records.filipino: lawak; gaano kalawak ang bahay na iyon?

records.nuance: 全く can mean entirely or really in affirmative sentences, but with a negative it means not at all. Here the speaker does not understand at all.
records.logic: 全く modifies 分かりません; the negative predicate gives the “not at all” reading.
records.difference: 全く分からない means not understand at all; よく分からない means not understand well/clearly.
records.filipino: hindi talaga; wala talaga akong naiintindihan

records.kanji_breakdown: レコード = record; vinyl record
records.nuance: レコード means a record, often a vinyl record. かけました means the speaker played/put on a jazz record.
records.logic: ジャズの modifies the record; レコードをかける is the expression for playing one.
records.difference: レコード is a record here; 録音（ろくおん） means an audio recording/recording process.
records.filipino: plaka; nagpatugtog ako ng jazz record

records.nuance: カメラ means a camera. 壊れた says it broke or stopped working.
records.logic: が marks the camera as the thing that broke; past 壊れた reports the change of state.
records.difference: カメラ is camera; 写真（しゃしん） is a photograph.

records.kanji_breakdown: 世 = world/generation; 界 = boundary/realm (character cues)
records.nuance: 世界 means the world. 世界旅行 means a trip around the world.
records.logic: 世界 modifies 旅行 to indicate travel around/in many parts of the world; したい expresses desire.
records.difference: 世界 means world; 地球（ちきゅう） means Earth as a planet.
records.filipino: mundo; gusto kong maglakbay sa buong mundo

records.nuance: 白 is the color white. The sentence says white is the color of snow.
records.logic: 白は is the topic; 雪の色 identifies it as the color of snow.
records.difference: 白（しろ） is the color white; 白い（しろい） is the adjective white.
records.filipino: puti; puti ang kulay ng niyebe

records.nuance: テープ means tape; in テープに録音する it refers to an audio tape/recording medium. She recorded the conversation onto tape.
records.logic: その会話 is what was recorded; に marks the medium; 録音した means recorded audio.
records.difference: テープ means tape/medium; 録音（ろくおん） is the act/result of recording.
records.filipino: tape; ni-record niya sa tape ang usapan

records.nuance: 黒い is the adjective black. The sentence says she is wearing a black dress.
records.logic: 黒い modifies ドレス; を着ています means is wearing.
records.difference: 黒い is the adjective black; 黒（くろ） is the noun/color black.
records.filipino: itim; nakasuot siya ng itim na bestida

records.nuance: 黒 is the color black. The question asks whether a black ballpoint pen is available.
records.logic: 黒の modifies ボールペン by color; ありますか asks whether one is available.
records.difference: 黒（くろ） is the noun black; 黒い（くろい） is the adjective black.
records.filipino: itim; may itim na ballpen ba kayo?

records.nuance: 赤 is the color red. The traffic light changed to red.
records.logic: 信号が marks the traffic signal; 赤に変わる means change to red.
records.difference: 赤（あか） is the noun red; 赤い（あかい） is the adjective red.
records.filipino: pula; nagpalit sa pula ang ilaw-trapiko

records.nuance: 銀行 means a bank as a financial institution. The sentence says it is open until three o’clock.
records.logic: 銀行は sets the bank as topic; まで marks the closing limit/time.
records.difference: 銀行 is a financial bank; 銀行員（ぎんこういん） means bank employee.
records.filipino: bangko; bukas ang bangko hanggang alas-tres

records.nuance: 銀 means silver. Here it modifies メダル; he won a silver medal.
records.logic: 銀の modifies the medal by material/color; を取った reports receiving/winning it.
records.difference: 銀 means silver; 金（きん） means gold.
records.filipino: pilak; nakakuha siya ng medalyang pilak

records.nuance: ページ means a page in a book or document. The request is to open to page 32.
records.logic: 32 modifies the page number; を開いてください asks the listener to open the material there.
records.difference: ページ is a page; 本（ほん） is a book.

records.nuance: 肉 means meat or flesh. Here it is the food that has finished cooking.
records.logic: 肉が marks what is cooked; 焼けました says it has cooked/been grilled through.
records.difference: 肉 means meat; 魚（さかな） means fish.

records.nuance: 魚 means fish. 肉と魚 sets meat and fish as the two choices.
records.logic: と joins the alternatives; どちらが好き asks which one is preferred.
records.difference: 魚（さかな） is fish; 肉（にく） is meat.
records.filipino: isda; alin ang mas gusto mo, karne o isda?

records.nuance: グラフ is a graph or chart. Here he turned sales figures into a chart.
records.logic: 売上を marks the data represented; グラフにする means make it into a graph/chart.
records.difference: グラフ is a graph/chart; 表（ひょう） is a table.
records.filipino: grap; ginawa niyang grap ang datos ng benta

records.kanji_breakdown: 屋 = shop; store; たばこ = tobacco
records.nuance: たばこ屋 is a tobacco shop. The speaker bought a lighter there.
records.logic: で marks where the purchase happened; ライターを買った is the purchased item/action.
records.difference: たばこ屋 sells tobacco products; コンビニ is a convenience store.
records.filipino: tindahan ng tabako; bumili ako ng lighter sa tindahan ng tabako

records.nuance: ポスト commonly means a mailbox/postbox in Japan. The speaker put a letter into one.
records.logic: 手紙を is the item posted; ポストに marks where it was put.
records.difference: ポスト is a mailbox here; 郵便局（ゆうびんきょく） is a post office.
records.filipino: kahon ng sulat; inilagay ko ang liham sa kahon ng sulat

records.nuance: 茶 means tea. The sentence says they drink tea every day; お茶 is the common polite/familiar form used in the sentence.
records.logic: 毎日 sets frequency; お茶を飲みます describes drinking tea.
records.difference: 茶（ちゃ） means tea; お茶（おちゃ） is the common polite/familiar form.
records.filipino: tsaa; umiinom kami ng tsaa araw-araw

records.kanji_breakdown: 茶 = tea; お = polite/familiar prefix
records.nuance: お茶 is the common polite/familiar word for tea. お茶を入れる means prepare/serve tea, usually by steeping it.
records.logic: を marks the tea being prepared; ～ましょうか offers to do it.
records.meaning: tea; prepare tea (in お茶を入れる)
records.difference: お茶 is tea; 紅茶（こうちゃ） specifically means black tea.
records.filipino: tsaa; ipaghahanda ko ba kayo ng tsaa?

records.nuance: テスト means a test or exam. The polite request is to begin it.
records.logic: を marks the test as what should be started; 始めてください requests the action.
records.difference: テスト is a test; 試験（しけん） is a more formal word for examination.

records.kanji_breakdown: 未 = not yet; 来 = come (character cues)
records.nuance: 未来 means the future. The sentence says no one can know what the future holds.
records.logic: 誰にも with a negative means nobody; 分からない says it cannot be known/understood.
records.difference: 未来 means the future; 将来（しょうらい） often means one’s future/prospects or a coming time.

records.nuance: 無くなる means become gone, run out, or cease to be available. With money, it means the speaker has run out of money.
records.logic: もう indicates already; お金が is what became gone; polite past marks the result.
records.meaning: to run out; be used up; disappear
records.difference: 無くなる is intransitive “run out/be gone”; 無くす（なくす） is transitive “lose/use up something.”
records.filipino: maubos; naubos na ang pera ko

records.nuance: ゴルフ is golf. 始めました means the older brother started playing it.
records.logic: 兄は marks the person; ゴルフを始める is to begin playing golf.
records.difference: ゴルフ is golf; テニス is tennis.
records.filipino: golf; nagsimulang maglaro ng golf ang kuya ko

records.nuance: 消しゴム is an eraser, traditionally a rubber eraser. The speaker asks to borrow one.
records.logic: を marks the item lent; 貸してください asks the listener to lend it.
records.difference: 消しゴム is an eraser; 鉛筆（えんぴつ） is a pencil.
records.filipino: pambura; maaari ko bang hiramin ang pambura mo?

records.nuance: ラジオ means radio as a device or broadcast medium. The sentence says she is listening to the radio.
records.logic: を聞いています is the ordinary expression for listening to a broadcast.
records.difference: ラジオ is radio; テレビ（テレビ） is television.

records.nuance: 売れる means be sold or sell well; it can describe how successfully a product sells. Here air conditioners sold well that summer.
records.logic: クーラーが is the product selling; よく means well/in large numbers; 今年の夏 sets the season.
records.meaning: to sell; be in demand; sell well
records.difference: 売れる is intransitive “sell/be sold”; 売る（うる） is transitive “sell something.”
records.filipino: mabenta; maraming nabentang aircon noong tag-init na iyon

records.nuance: タクシー is a taxi. The polite request is to call one over.
records.logic: を marks the taxi as what should be summoned; 呼んでください requests the action.
records.difference: タクシー is a taxi; バス（バス） is a bus.

records.nuance: ゆっくり means slowly or at an unhurried pace. もっとゆっくり asks the listener to speak even more slowly.
records.logic: もっと increases the degree; 話してください is a polite request to speak.
records.difference: ゆっくり means slowly/unhurriedly; 速く（はやく） means quickly.
records.filipino: dahan-dahan; magsalita ka nang mas dahan-dahan

records.nuance: レストラン is a restaurant. The speaker ate Indian food there.
records.logic: で marks where the meal was eaten; インド料理を is the food eaten.
records.difference: レストラン is a restaurant; 食堂（しょくどう） is a dining hall/cafeteria.
records.filipino: restawran; kumain ako ng pagkaing Indian sa restawran

records.nuance: カード means a card. With 支払いは…カードでお願いします it refers to a payment card, likely a credit/debit card.
records.logic: で marks the payment method; お願いします is a polite request/preference.
records.difference: カード is a card; 現金（げんきん） means cash.
records.filipino: card; pakigamit ang card para sa bayad

records.nuance: 熱 means heat or fever. 熱が出ました means the speaker developed a fever last night.
records.logic: 昨日の夜 sets when it occurred; 熱が出る is the common expression for getting a fever.
records.difference: 熱（ねつ） is fever/heat; 熱い（あつい） means hot to the touch.

records.kanji_breakdown: アルバイト = part-time job; casual work
records.nuance: アルバイト means part-time or casual work; it can also refer to the job itself. The older brother works part-time.
records.logic: アルバイトをしています means have/do part-time work.
records.difference: アルバイト is part-time work; 正社員（せいしゃいん） is a regular full-time employee.
records.filipino: part-time na trabaho; nagtatrabaho nang part-time ang kuya ko

records.nuance: 暖まる means become warm, especially a room or air. The room has not warmed up yet.
records.logic: まだ with negative marks that the expected warm state has not arrived; 部屋が is what warms.
records.difference: 暖まる is intransitive “become warm”; 暖める（あたためる） is transitive “warm something.”
records.filipino: uminam; hindi pa umiinit ang kuwarto

records.nuance: コピー means a copy or photocopy. At the meeting, the speaker distributed copies of a document.
records.logic: 書類のコピー is copies of the document; を配った means distributed them.
records.difference: コピー is a copy; 原本（げんぽん） is the original document.
records.filipino: kopya; namahagi ako ng mga kopya ng dokumento sa pulong

records.nuance: 風 means wind. 風が強い says the wind is strong today.
records.logic: 今日は sets the weather for today; が marks wind as what is strong.
records.difference: 風 means wind; 雨（あめ） means rain.

records.kanji_breakdown: ぶつかる = collide; bump into
records.nuance: ぶつかる means collide with or bump into something. Here the car hit a telephone pole.
records.logic: 車が is the thing that collided; 電柱に marks what it struck.
records.difference: ぶつかる is intransitive “collide”; ぶつける is transitive “hit something.”
records.filipino: bumangga; bumangga ang kotse sa poste ng kuryente

records.kanji_breakdown: フィルム = film; photographic film
records.nuance: フィルム means film; with 旅行に…買った, it likely means photographic film bought for the trip.
records.logic: たくさん modifies the amount bought; 旅行のために gives the purpose.
records.difference: フィルム can mean photographic film; 映画（えいが） means a movie/film as a work.
records.filipino: pelikula para sa kamera; bumili ako ng maraming film para sa biyahe

records.nuance: 良い（よい） means good. Here it means positive/strong points, the only parts he emphasized.
records.logic: 良いところ is the positive aspects; だけ limits what he emphasized to those points.
records.difference: 良い may be read よい or いい; preserve this note’s よい. 悪い（わるい） means bad.
records.filipino: mabuti; idiniin lamang niya ang magagandang punto

records.nuance: デパート means a department store. The speaker bought shoes there.
records.logic: で marks the shop where the purchase occurred; 靴を買った gives the purchase.
records.difference: デパート is a department store; 店（みせ） is a store/shop generally.
records.filipino: department store; bumili ako ng sapatos sa department store

records.nuance: 知らせる means tell or inform someone of information. The speaker informed everyone of the meeting date.
records.logic: 皆に marks the recipients; 会議の日にち is the information conveyed.
records.difference: 知らせる means inform; 知る（しる） means know.
records.filipino: ipaalam; ipinaalam ko sa lahat ang petsa ng pulong

records.nuance: ベッド means a bed. The sentence says he is sleeping in bed.
records.logic: で marks the place/activity setting; 寝ています describes sleeping.
records.difference: ベッド is a bed; 布団（ふとん） is a Japanese-style bedding/futon.

records.nuance: 可 means allowed/acceptable in labels and short notices. 学生可 means students are eligible/allowed; here it says students may apply for the part-time job.
records.logic: 学生 is the group; 可 marks eligibility. ですね seeks confirmation.
records.difference: 可 means allowed/acceptable; 不可（ふか） means not allowed/not acceptable.
records.filipino: puwede; puwedeng mag-apply ang mga estudyante sa part-time na trabahong ito

records.nuance: ノート means a notebook or written notes. In ノートを開いてください, it means open your notebook.
records.logic: を marks what should be opened; ください makes a polite request.
records.difference: ノート is a notebook here; ノートパソコン means laptop computer.

records.nuance: ワイン is wine. 少し飲みました says the speaker drank a little.
records.logic: を marks what was drunk; 少し limits the amount.
records.difference: ワイン is wine; ビール（ビール） is beer.
records.filipino: alak; uminom ako ng kaunting wine

records.nuance: トイレ means a toilet/restroom. Here the question asks whether the listener cleaned it.
records.logic: を marks the toilet as what was cleaned; 掃除しましたか asks about completed cleaning.
records.difference: トイレ is toilet/restroom; お手洗い（おてあらい） is a more polite term.
records.filipino: palikuran; nilinis mo ba ang palikuran?

records.kanji_breakdown: 朝 = morning; ご飯 = cooked rice/meal
records.nuance: 朝ご飯 means breakfast. The sentence says the speaker ate breakfast at seven.
records.logic: 七時に gives the time; を食べました states eating the meal.
records.difference: 朝ご飯 is breakfast; 昼ご飯（ひるごはん） is lunch.
records.filipino: almusal; kumain ako ng almusal nang alas-siyete

records.kanji_breakdown: 買 = buy; 物 = thing (character cues)
records.nuance: 買い物 means shopping or a purchase. 母は買い物に出かけています means mother has gone out shopping/is out shopping.
records.logic: に出かける means go out for an activity; ～ています can describe the resulting state of being away.
records.difference: 買い物 means shopping; 買う（かう） means buy something.
records.filipino: pamimili; umalis ang nanay ko para mamili

records.nuance: キャンプ means camping or a camp. Here the speaker went camping with a friend.
records.logic: 友達と marks the companion; キャンプに行った means went camping.
records.difference: キャンプ is camping; 登山（とざん） is mountain climbing.
records.filipino: camping; nag-camping ako kasama ang kaibigan

records.nuance: 物 means a thing or object. The sentence says there are many things in her house.
records.logic: 彼女の家には sets her house as location/topic; 物がたくさんあります states many things are there.
records.difference: 物 is a thing/object; 事（こと） usually refers to a matter, event, or abstract thing.
records.filipino: bagay; maraming gamit sa bahay niya

records.nuance: プラスチック means plastic as a material. このカップはプラスチックです means this cup is plastic/made of plastic.
records.logic: The material follows the topic cup as a predicate; Japanese often omits “made of.”
records.difference: プラスチック is plastic material; ガラス（ガラス） is glass.
records.filipino: plastik; yari sa plastik ang tasang ito

records.nuance: 忘れ物 is an item someone has forgotten or left behind. The speaker left something at school.
records.logic: 学校に marks where it was left; 忘れ物をしました is a common way to say one forgot/left something behind.
records.difference: 忘れ物 is an item left behind; 落とし物（おとしもの） is something dropped/lost.
records.filipino: naiwang gamit; may naiwan akong gamit sa paaralan

records.nuance: 重さ means weight. The request is to weigh this luggage and tell/check the result.
records.logic: この荷物の identifies what is weighed; を計ってください requests measuring its weight.
records.difference: 重さ is weight; 重い（おもい） is heavy.
records.filipino: bigat; pakisukat ang bigat ng bagahe na ito

records.kanji_breakdown: カラー = color; collar (loanword; context decides)
records.nuance: カラー means color in カラーコピー. The question asks the price for one color copy.
records.logic: カラー modifies コピー to mean color printing; 一枚 counts one sheet/copy; 幾ら asks the price.
records.difference: カラー means color here; 白黒（しろくろ） means black-and-white. It can also mean collar in other contexts.
records.filipino: may kulay; magkano ang isang colored copy?

records.nuance: ピアノ is a piano. ピアノを習う means take lessons/learn to play piano.
records.logic: 昔 places the learning in the past; 習っていました describes an ongoing past period of lessons.
records.difference: ピアノ is a piano; 楽器（がっき） means musical instrument generally.
records.filipino: piano; dati akong nag-aaral tumugtog ng piano

records.nuance: スキー means skiing or skis. スキーに行く is the common expression for going skiing.
records.logic: 冬は sets winter as the recurring time; よく indicates often.
records.difference: スキーに行く means go skiing; スケート means skating.
records.filipino: mag-ski; madalas kaming mag-ski tuwing taglamig

records.kanji_breakdown: 生 = be born; come into being
records.nuance: 生まれる means be born. Here a baby boy was born to the speaker’s older sister and her husband.
records.logic: 姉夫婦に marks the parents; 男の子が marks the baby born.
records.meaning: to be born; come into existence
records.difference: 生まれる is intransitive “be born”; 生む（うむ） is transitive “give birth to.”
records.filipino: ipanganak; nagkaanak ng lalaki ang ate ko at ang asawa niya

records.nuance: プール means a swimming pool. Here the speaker went to the pool during summer vacation.
records.logic: 夏休みに marks when; プールに行った describes going there.
records.difference: プール means pool; 海（うみ） means sea.
records.filipino: swimming pool; pumunta ako sa swimming pool noong bakasyon sa tag-init

records.kanji_breakdown: ホーム = platform (railway); home in other contexts
records.nuance: ホーム in a railway station means a train platform. Here a train will arrive at this platform soon.
records.logic: このホームに marks the platform; 電車が来ます says a train will come/arrive.
records.difference: ホーム means platform in railway context; 駅（えき） means station.
records.filipino: plataporma; paparating na ang tren sa platapormang ito

records.kanji_breakdown: エレベーター = elevator; lift
records.nuance: エレベーター means an elevator/lift. The suggestion is to go down using it.
records.logic: で marks the means; 下に降りましょう suggests descending together.
records.difference: エレベーター is an elevator; 階段（かいだん） is stairs.
records.filipino: elevator; bumaba na tayo gamit ang elevator

records.kanji_breakdown: 中 = middle; 学 = study; 生 = student (character cues)
records.nuance: 中学生 is a junior-high/middle-school student. The sentence says the speaker’s son is at this school level.
records.logic: 息子は sets the son as topic; 中学生です identifies his student stage.
records.difference: 中学生 is middle school; 小学生（しょうがくせい） is elementary school and 高校生（こうこうせい） is high school.
records.filipino: estudyante sa junior high; junior high school student ang anak kong lalaki

records.nuance: メモ means a memo or written note. メモを取る means write down/take notes.
records.logic: を取る is the conventional verb combination; ください makes it a polite request.
records.difference: メモ is a short written note; ノート（ノート） is a notebook or notes.

records.kanji_breakdown: 小 = small; 学 = study; 校 = school (character cues)
records.nuance: 小学校 is an elementary school. The sentence says one is near the speaker’s house.
records.logic: 家の近くに marks the location; あります states the school is there.
