records.difference: 小学校 is elementary school; 中学校（ちゅうがっこう） is middle/junior high school.
records.filipino: elementary school; may elementary school malapit sa bahay ko

records.kanji_breakdown: 中 = middle; 学 = study; 校 = school (character cues)
records.nuance: 中学校 is a middle/junior-high school. The sentence says the son’s school is five minutes from home.
records.logic: 家から marks the starting point for distance/time; 5分 gives travel time/distance.
records.difference: 中学校 is junior high/middle school; 中学生（ちゅうがくせい） is its student.
records.filipino: junior high school; limang minuto ang layo ng paaralan ng anak ko sa bahay

records.kanji_breakdown: びっくりする = be startled; be surprised
records.nuance: びっくりする means be startled or surprised. The speaker was startled by a loud/big sound.
records.logic: 大きな音に marks the trigger; past びっくりしました reports the reaction.
records.difference: びっくりする is be startled/surprised; 驚く（おどろく） means be surprised, often a little more formal.
records.filipino: magulat; nagulat ako sa malakas na tunog

records.nuance: 強さ means strength or intensity. Here it refers to how strong the wind was.
records.logic: 風の identifies what is measured; 驚きました says the speaker was surprised by that force.
records.difference: 強さ is strength/intensity; 強い（つよい） is the adjective strong.
records.filipino: lakas; nagulat ako sa lakas ng hangin

records.nuance: おもちゃ means a toy. Here it is a toy car the baby is playing with.
records.logic: 自動車のおもちゃ is a toy shaped like a car; で marks the toy as what the baby plays with.
records.difference: おもちゃ is a toy; 自動車（じどうしゃ） is a car/automobile.
records.filipino: laruan; naglalaro ang sanggol ng laruang kotse

records.nuance: グラム is a gram, a unit of mass. The speaker requests 200 grams of ground meat.
records.logic: 200 modifies the quantity; ひき肉 is the product requested.
records.difference: グラム is a metric unit of mass; キログラム is 1,000 grams.
records.filipino: gramo; pabili po ng 200 gramo ng giniling na karne

records.nuance: コーヒー is coffee. The speaker drinks it every morning.
records.logic: 毎朝 gives the repeated time; を飲みます describes the habitual action.
records.difference: コーヒー is coffee; お茶（おちゃ） is tea.
records.filipino: kape; umiinom ako ng kape tuwing umaga

records.nuance: テント means a tent. テントを張る means pitch/set up a tent; the group did it together.
records.logic: みんなで means everyone together; を張りました is the conventional verb for pitching a tent.
records.difference: テント is a tent; キャンプ is camping.
records.filipino: tolda; nagtayo kaming lahat ng tolda

records.nuance: 回る means go around, revolve, or make a circuit. The moon goes around/orbits Earth.
records.logic: 地球のまわりを gives the path around Earth; ～ています describes its ongoing orbit.
records.difference: 回る means go around/orbit; 回転する（かいてんする） means rotate/spin around an axis.
records.filipino: umikot sa paligid; umiikot ang buwan sa paligid ng Daigdig

records.nuance: ボート is a boat, often a small recreational boat. The speaker rode/boarded one on the pond.
records.logic: 池で marks where; ボートに乗りました means got on/rode a boat.
records.difference: ボート is a small boat; 船（ふね） is a general ship/boat.
records.filipino: bangka; sumakay ako sa bangka sa lawa

records.nuance: ボール is a ball. The sentence says he threw it.
records.logic: を marks the ball as the object thrown; 投げた is past of throw.
records.difference: ボール is a ball; 球（たま） is a native word for a ball/sphere.

records.nuance: オートバイ means motorcycle. 乗っている says he is riding one or regularly rides it.
records.logic: に乗る is the pattern for boarding/riding a vehicle; ～ている can mean ongoing action or habitual state.
records.difference: オートバイ is a motorcycle; 自転車（じてんしゃ） is a bicycle.

records.nuance: あなた means you. In this sentence, the speaker says they will give the book to the listener.
records.logic: あなたに marks the recipient; あげます is giving from the speaker’s side to someone else.
records.difference: あなた means you, but Japanese often omits it or uses a name/title instead; 君（きみ） is another, more familiar form.
records.filipino: ikaw; ibibigay ko sa iyo ang librong ito

records.nuance: スイッチ means a switch. スイッチを入れる means turn the device on using its switch.
records.logic: カーラジオの identifies the switch; を入れた is the common “switch on” expression.
records.difference: スイッチを入れる means turn on; スイッチを切る means switch off.
records.filipino: switch; binuksan niya ang switch ng radyo sa kotse

records.nuance: 必ず means certainly, without fail, or always. With a seat-belt instruction it stresses that one must wear it every time.
records.logic: 必ず modifies 着けてください, making the instruction emphatic and obligatory.
records.difference: 必ず emphasizes certainty/requirement; いつも means habitually/always.
records.filipino: palagi; siguraduhin mong ikabit ang seat belt

records.nuance: プレゼント is a present or gift. The sentence says the speaker received a gift on their birthday; Japanese does not specify the number, while the deck English uses “some presents.”
records.logic: 誕生日に gives the occasion; をもらいました marks receiving a gift.
records.difference: プレゼント is a gift; 贈り物（おくりもの） is another word for a present/gift.
records.filipino: regalo; nakatanggap ako ng regalo noong kaarawan ko

records.nuance: いつでも means anytime or whenever. The invitation asks the listener to come to the speaker’s home whenever convenient.
records.logic: うちに marks destination; ください is a polite invitation/request.
records.difference: いつでも means any time; いつか means someday at an unspecified future time.
records.filipino: kahit kailan; puwede kang pumunta sa bahay ko kahit kailan

records.kanji_breakdown: 引 = subtract; 算 = calculate (character cues)
records.nuance: 引き算 means subtraction. The daughter is learning it at school.
records.logic: 学校で gives where she learns; 習っている describes current instruction/learning.
records.difference: 引き算 is subtraction; 足し算（たしざん） is addition.
records.filipino: pagbabawas; pinag-aaralan ng anak kong babae ang pagbabawas sa paaralan

records.nuance: テニス is tennis. よくしています means they often play/do it.
records.logic: 彼らは identifies the players; よく marks frequency.
records.difference: テニス is tennis; ゴルフ is golf.
records.filipino: tennis; madalas silang maglaro ng tennis

records.kanji_breakdown: こちら = this way; here; this side (polite)
records.nuance: こちら politely indicates this way or this place. In reception context, it directs visitors to the reception desk.
records.logic: 受付はこちら means reception is this way/here; です is a polite identification.
records.difference: こちら is polite; こっち is a casual equivalent. It can also be a polite “I/we” or “this one” in other contexts.
records.filipino: dito; dito po ang reception desk

records.nuance: ボタン means a button. The sentence politely instructs someone to press it.
records.logic: を marks the button as the object; 押してください makes a polite request.
records.difference: ボタン is a button; スイッチ is a switch.

records.nuance: 急に means suddenly or unexpectedly. Here the speaker suddenly remembered an errand/obligation.
records.logic: 用事を思い出した is what occurred; 急に modifies the suddenness of remembering.
records.difference: 急に means suddenly; 必ず（かならず） means certainly/without fail.
records.filipino: bigla; bigla kong naalala na may kailangan pala akong gawin

records.nuance: 急 means sudden/urgent, and in 急な坂道 it means steep. The sentence says the speaker went up a steep slope.
records.logic: 急な modifies 坂道; 上った means went/climbed up it.
records.difference: 急な坂 means a steep slope; 急に means suddenly. The exact meaning depends on what it modifies.
records.filipino: matarik; umakyat ako sa matarik na daan

records.nuance: ドラマ means a drama or dramatic series. Here ドラマを見る means watch TV dramas.
records.logic: を見るのが好き expresses liking the activity of watching dramas.
records.difference: ドラマ is a drama/series; 映画（えいが） is a film/movie.
records.filipino: drama; gusto kong manood ng mga drama sa TV

records.nuance: ビザ is a visa, an official permission to enter or stay in a country. The Japanese sentence says someone has a student visa; it omits the subject, while the deck English specifies “he.”
records.logic: 学生 modifies the type of visa; を持っています means possess/hold.
records.difference: ビザ is a visa; パスポート is a passport.

records.nuance: ポケット means a pocket. The Japanese says a wallet was put away in a pocket, with the agent omitted; the deck English supplies “I.”
records.logic: ポケットに marks the destination; しまった means put away/stowed.
records.difference: ポケット means a pocket; 財布（さいふ） means wallet.

records.nuance: ぶどう means grapes or a grape. The speaker likes grapes.
records.logic: が marks the liked food; 好きです expresses liking.
records.difference: ぶどう is grape/grapes; いちご means strawberry.

records.nuance: クリスマス means Christmas. The sentence says the speaker eats cake at Christmas.
records.logic: には marks the occasion; ケーキを食べます states the customary activity.
records.difference: クリスマス is Christmas; 誕生日（たんじょうび） is a birthday.

records.nuance: ネクタイ means a necktie. The sentence says a tie was given as a present on Father’s Day; the recipient is not stated in Japanese.
records.logic: 父の日に marks the occasion; ネクタイをプレゼントした means gave a tie as a gift.
records.difference: ネクタイ is a necktie; シャツ is a shirt.
records.filipino: nagbigay ng necktie bilang regalo noong Father’s Day

records.nuance: バイオリン means violin. 習っています indicates she is learning/studying it, likely through lessons or practice.
records.logic: を marks the instrument studied; ～ています describes an ongoing learning activity.
records.difference: バイオリン is a violin; ピアノ is a piano.
records.filipino: biyolin; nag-aaral siyang tumugtog ng biyolin

records.nuance: パスポート means passport. 見つからない means it cannot be found; the speaker cannot locate it.
records.logic: が marks the passport as the thing not found; negative potential/intransitive form leaves the searcher unstated.
records.difference: パスポート is a passport; ビザ is a visa.

records.kanji_breakdown: 上 = upper; 着 = clothing (character cues)
records.nuance: 上着 means an outer garment or jacket worn over other clothes. The speaker took it off because it was hot.
records.logic: 暑いので gives the reason; 脱ぎました means removed the garment.
records.difference: 上着 is outerwear; シャツ（シャツ） is a shirt worn underneath/in place of a jacket.

records.nuance: 着せる means put clothes on someone or dress someone. The speaker dressed their daughter in a cute dress.
records.logic: 娘に marks the person dressed; ドレスを is the clothing put on her.
records.meaning: to dress someone; put clothing on someone
records.difference: 着せる is transitive “dress someone”; 着る（きる） is “wear (clothes oneself).”
records.filipino: sinuotan ng cute na bestida ang anak kong babae

records.nuance: バッグ means a bag or handbag. The speaker has a black bag.
records.logic: 黒い modifies バッグ; を持っています means have/carry.
records.difference: バッグ is a bag; 財布（さいふ） is a wallet.

records.nuance: 立てる means set something upright or stand it up. Here candles were placed upright in the cake.
records.logic: ろうそくを is the object set upright; ケーキに marks where they were placed.
records.meaning: to stand/set up; erect; place upright
records.difference: 立てる is transitive “stand something up”; 立つ（たつ） is intransitive “stand.”
records.filipino: itirik; itinirik niya ang mga kandila sa cake

records.nuance: ゴム means rubber or elastic. Here it has stretched and lost its tension.
records.logic: が marks the rubber/elastic; 伸びてしまった indicates an unwanted change/result.
records.difference: ゴム means rubber/elastic; プラスチック means plastic.

records.nuance: ギター means guitar. 得意 means she is good/skilled at playing it.
records.logic: ギターが得意 is the pattern for being good at an activity/skill; instrument playing is implied.
records.difference: ギター is guitar; バイオリン is violin.
records.filipino: gitara; mahusay siyang tumugtog ng gitara

records.nuance: セーター means sweater. The sentence says this sweater is wool.
records.logic: この identifies the sweater; ウールだ states its material.
records.difference: セーター is a sweater; シャツ is a shirt.
records.filipino: sweater; gawa sa lana ang sweater na ito

records.nuance: 移す means move or transfer something from one place to another. The desk was moved near the window.
records.logic: 机を marks the moved object; 窓のそばに gives its new location.
records.difference: 移す is transitive “move/transfer something”; 移る（うつる） is intransitive “move/transfer.”
records.filipino: inilipat ang mesa malapit sa bintana

records.nuance: 動き means movement or a move/action. Here it refers to the opponent’s movements in a game or contest.
records.logic: 相手の modifies movement; まず…見ましょう proposes watching it first.
records.difference: 動き is movement/action; 動く（うごく） is to move.
records.filipino: galaw; panoorin muna natin ang galaw ng kalaban

records.nuance: カーテン means a curtain. The speaker opened the curtains in the morning.
records.logic: 朝 marks when; を開けた means opened them.
records.difference: カーテン is a curtain; 窓（まど） is a window.

records.nuance: シャツ means a shirt. The sentence says this shirt needs ironing.
records.logic: この identifies the shirt; アイロンが必要 means ironing is necessary.
records.difference: シャツ is a shirt; セーター is a sweater.
records.filipino: kamiseta; kailangang plantsahin ang kamisetang ito

records.nuance: 始めに means at the beginning or first. The sentence says soup is served first.
records.logic: 始めに modifies the serving order; スープが出ます describes what is brought/served.
records.difference: 始めに means first/at the beginning; 初めて（はじめて） means for the first time.

records.nuance: ナイフ means a knife. The speaker cut their hand with one.
records.logic: ナイフで marks the instrument; 手を切った describes the injury/action.
records.difference: ナイフ is a knife; 包丁（ほうちょう） is a kitchen knife.
records.filipino: nahiwa ang kamay gamit ang kutsilyo

records.nuance: バイク commonly means motorcycle in Japanese. The older brother loves motorcycles.
records.logic: バイクが大好き marks the thing he loves.
records.difference: バイク means motorcycle in this context; オートバイ is a fuller synonym. In some contexts バイク can refer to a bicycle.
records.filipino: motorsiklo; gustong-gusto ng kuya ko ang motorsiklo

records.kanji_breakdown: いつか = someday; at some time
records.nuance: いつか means someday or at some unspecified future time. The speaker wants to go to Africa someday.
records.logic: いつか sets an indefinite future time; 行きたい expresses desire.
records.difference: いつか means someday; いつでも means anytime/whenever.
records.filipino: balang araw; gusto kong pumunta sa Africa balang araw

records.kanji_breakdown: オレンジ = orange (fruit or color)
records.nuance: オレンジ can mean an orange fruit or the color orange. With が好きです and no color noun, this sentence naturally means the speaker likes oranges as fruit.
records.logic: が marks what is liked; context favors the edible fruit sense.
records.difference: オレンジ means orange fruit here; みかん is a common Japanese citrus fruit.
records.filipino: kahel; gusto ko ang mga kahel

records.kanji_breakdown: さっき = just now; a little while ago
records.nuance: さっき refers to a short time earlier. さっきの話 means the conversation/topic from a little while ago.
records.logic: の話 makes the earlier time modify the conversation; 続けましょう proposes continuing it.
records.meaning: just now; a little while ago
records.difference: さっき is a short time ago; 昔（むかし） means long ago/in the past.
records.filipino: kanina; ituloy natin ang napag-usapan natin kanina

records.kanji_breakdown: テキスト = text; written material
records.nuance: テキスト means text or written material. The sentence asks someone to read it; the Japanese does not specify that it must be a textbook.
records.logic: It names the written content being read, whether a passage, document, or study text.
records.difference: テキスト is the written material; 本（ほん） is a book, which may contain text.

records.nuance: 歌（うた） usually means a song or singing. In literary contexts, it can also refer to Japanese poetry, especially waka. Here その歌 refers to a particular song.
records.logic: 歌 centers on verbal artistic expression through singing or poetic form. Depending on context, it can refer to a song, singing, or traditional poetry.
records.meaning: song; singing; poem in literary contexts
records.difference: 歌 is a song; 音楽（おんがく） is music more broadly.

records.nuance: りんご is an apple. 一つ asks for one; Japanese nouns here do not mark plural, so the English “apples” is not a plural form in Japanese.
records.logic: The quantity comes from 一つ, while りんご names the fruit.
records.difference: りんご is the fruit; みかん is a different fruit, a mandarin orange.

records.kanji_breakdown: 面 = face / surface; 白 = white (character cues only)
records.nuance: 面白い describes something that holds interest or is amusing. With 本 and 全然…なかった, it means the book was not interesting at all; which shade depends on context.
records.logic: This established word describes a response of interest or amusement, not a literal combination of “face” and “white.”
records.difference: 面白い describes the thing as interesting or amusing; 楽しい describes an enjoyable experience or how someone feels.

records.nuance: アルバム is an album. The sentence says the speaker saw his album, but does not tell us whether it is a music release or a photo album.
records.logic: The loanword names a collected set of recordings or photographs; the surrounding context decides which kind.
records.difference: アルバム is a collected album; 写真（しゃしん） is a photograph.
records.filipino: album; koleksiyon ng mga larawan o kanta

records.kanji_breakdown: 真 = true / complete; 中 = middle
records.nuance: 真ん中 means the middle or center. Here a person is standing in the middle of the road.
records.logic: 中 supplies the idea of middle; 真ん中 is the established word for the central position, rather than a historical literal formula.
records.difference: 真ん中 is the central position; 周り（まわり） means the surrounding area.

records.nuance: 真っ白 means pure white or completely white. The snow has made everything outside look white.
records.logic: The prefix 真っ intensifies 白 to describe an uninterrupted or vivid white appearance.
records.difference: 真っ白 means completely white; 白っぽい（しろっぽい） means whitish, not fully white.

records.nuance: スカート means a skirt. あまり with the negative はかない means she does not wear skirts very often.
records.logic: The negative frequency expression limits how often she wears this type of clothing; it does not mean she never wears one.
records.difference: スカート is a skirt; ズボン is trousers.

records.nuance: 真っ暗 means pitch-dark or completely dark. The sentence simply describes the outside as having almost no light.
records.logic: The prefix 真っ intensifies 暗い to express a strongly dark condition.
records.difference: 真っ暗 means pitch-dark; 薄暗い（うすぐらい） means dim or somewhat dark.
records.filipino: dilim na dilim; madilim na madilim

records.nuance: ペン means a pen. 貸してください politely asks the listener to lend it to the speaker.
records.logic: 貸す is the lender’s action: the speaker asks the listener to let them use the pen temporarily.
records.difference: ペン is a writing instrument with ink; 鉛筆（えんぴつ） is a pencil.

records.nuance: おしゃべり can mean chatting or being talkative. Describing the younger sister as とてもおしゃべり means she talks a lot; the tone can be affectionate or mildly critical.
records.logic: The sentence uses おしゃべり as a description of her disposition, rather than saying she is chatting at this moment.
records.difference: おしゃべり describes someone who talks a lot; 静か（しずか） means quiet.

records.nuance: 直す is a transitive verb meaning to fix, repair, or correct something. Here それ is the thing the speaker fixed; its exact nature is not specified.
records.logic: The speaker acts on an object and restores or changes it to a desired state. For illness, 治す is commonly used instead.
records.difference: 直す is used for fixing or correcting an object or work; 治す is used for curing an illness or injury.

records.nuance: メニュー means a menu or list of available dishes or options. メニューをください asks for one.
records.logic: The noun identifies the list the speaker wants to consult; the request does not itself indicate ordering a particular dish.
records.difference: メニュー is the list of choices; 注文（ちゅうもん） is an order placed from it.

records.kanji_breakdown: アイスクリーム = ice cream
records.nuance: アイスクリーム means ice cream. The sentence says the younger brother loves it very much.
records.logic: 大好き expresses strong liking, while アイスクリーム names the food.
records.difference: アイスクリーム is ice cream; アイスキャンディー is a frozen ice pop.

records.kanji_breakdown: 間 = interval / space; 違 = differ (character cues only)
records.nuance: 間違い means a mistake or error. この文には間違いがあります says there is an error in this sentence.
records.logic: Treat 間違い as an established word for an error, not as a literal “space-difference” etymology.
records.difference: 間違い is a mistake or error; 間違える is the verb “to make a mistake.”

records.nuance: おしゃれ describes someone stylish or attentive to appearance. あの子はおしゃれだね comments that the girl looks stylish; “trendy” is possible but can be narrower.
records.logic: It describes a person’s appearance or fashion sense, not necessarily whether a particular style is currently fashionable.
records.difference: おしゃれ describes style and presentation; きれい means beautiful or clean, depending on context.

records.kanji_breakdown: ジュース = juice; soft drink
records.nuance: ジュース means juice and, in everyday Japanese, can also refer broadly to a sweet nonalcoholic drink. This sentence only says the drink is too sweet.
records.logic: 甘すぎる evaluates its sweetness; the sentence does not identify its flavor or ingredients.
records.difference: ジュース is a drink; 水（みず） is water.

records.nuance: ゼロ means zero. 今日の交通事故はゼロです says there are no traffic accidents today.
records.logic: ゼロ states that the count is 0; the sentence concerns today’s accident count.
records.difference: ゼロ is the number zero; 少し（すこし） means a little or a small amount.

records.nuance: ピンク means pink. It describes the color of the dress the daughter is wearing.
records.logic: The phrase ピンクのドレス uses の to connect the color with the dress.
records.difference: ピンク is a color; 赤（あか） is red.

records.nuance: グラス means a drinking glass here: the speaker is admiring a glass vessel. It can also refer to a glass of a drink, depending on context.
records.logic: The sentence’s きれいな makes the object itself sound beautiful; the word is not referring to the glass material.
records.difference: グラス is a drinking vessel; ガラス is glass as a material.

records.kanji_breakdown: 姉 = older sister; さん = respectful / familiar address
records.nuance: 姉さん is a familiar, respectful way to address an older sister, like “sis” here. It can also address a young woman in other contexts, but this sentence is an apology to “sis.”
records.logic: The vocative pause after 姉さん shows direct address, rather than describing a third person.
records.difference: 姉さん addresses an older sister or, in other contexts, a young woman; 姉（あね） usually refers to one’s own older sister when speaking about her.

records.kanji_breakdown: 兄 = older brother; さん = respectful / familiar address
records.nuance: 兄さん is a familiar, respectful way to address an older brother, like “big brother” here. The sentence congratulates him directly.
records.logic: The comma after 兄さん marks direct address; it is not a sentence about someone else’s brother.
records.difference: 兄さん addresses an older brother; 兄（あに） commonly refers to one’s own older brother when speaking about him.

records.nuance: ダンス means dance or dancing. ダンスが大好きです says she loves dancing.
records.logic: The noun ダンス is the activity she likes; 大好き marks strong affection for it.
records.difference: ダンス is the activity of dancing; 踊り（おどり） can refer to a dance or dancing, often with emphasis on the performance or style.

records.kanji_breakdown: 業 = business / work; 者 = person / operator
records.nuance: 業者 means a business operator or service provider. In 引っ越しを業者に頼んだ, it refers to a company hired to handle the move, not necessarily one businessman.
records.logic: 頼む marks the provider as the party entrusted with the moving work; the word itself is broader than “company” or “businessman.”
records.difference: 業者 is the provider hired for a service; 会社（かいしゃ） is a company as an organization.

records.kanji_breakdown: 彼 = he / that person; ら = pluralizing suffix
records.nuance: 彼ら means they or them, often for a group of men or a mixed group. Here it refers to the people who are basketball players.
records.logic: ら makes 彼 plural; the Japanese sentence does not specify the group’s gender composition.
records.difference: 彼ら refers to people as “they”; 彼女たち（かのじょたち） explicitly refers to a group of women.

records.nuance: おじ means an uncle: a parent’s brother or a parent’s sister’s husband. The spoken reading alone does not show whether he is older or younger than the parent; 伯父 and 叔父 distinguish that in writing.
records.logic: The sentence says this uncle works for a bank; it gives no further family-age detail.
records.difference: おじ is an uncle; おば is an aunt.

records.nuance: サッカー means soccer. 彼はサッカーの選手です says he is a soccer player.
records.logic: The の phrase links the sport with 選手, a player.
records.difference: サッカー is soccer; 野球（やきゅう） is baseball.

records.nuance: スープ means soup or broth. コーンスープ is corn soup; the Japanese 作っている describes the mother making it now, while the deck English “made” presents a completed action. “Chowder” is also a narrower English choice than スープ.
records.logic: コーン names the corn variety, while スープ names the dish.
records.difference: スープ is a soup or broth; 汁（しる） is a broader word for liquid or soup in food.

records.nuance: バナナ means banana. 毎朝 places the eating habit every morning.
records.logic: 毎朝 gives the repeated time; the sentence does not specify the number eaten each morning.
records.difference: バナナ is a banana; りんご is an apple.

records.nuance: うるさい describes sound that is loud or bothersome. Here it is the cars’ noise on the street, with an uncomfortable or irritating feel.
records.logic: The sentence attributes the bothersome sound to cars; it is more than a neutral statement that vehicles are present.
records.difference: うるさい often implies that the sound bothers the listener; 大きい音（おおきいおと） simply means a loud sound.

records.kanji_breakdown: パトカー = police car; patrol car
records.nuance: パトカー means a police patrol car. あそこに…いる points out one over there.
records.logic: The sentence locates the vehicle; it does not say that it is moving or responding to an emergency.
records.difference: パトカー is a police patrol car; 救急車（きゅうきゅうしゃ） is an ambulance.

records.nuance: 答え means an answer or solution. Here he does not know the answer to that problem.
records.logic: 分からない expresses not knowing or understanding; その問題の答え identifies what he lacks.
records.difference: 答え is the answer; 質問（しつもん） is a question.

records.nuance: ハンバーガー means hamburger. The Japanese says today’s lunch was a hamburger; the English “I had” supplies a natural but unstated subject.
records.logic: 今日の昼ご飯 marks today’s lunch as the topic, and でした identifies what it was.
records.difference: ハンバーガー is a hamburger; サンドイッチ is a sandwich.

records.nuance: エスカレーター means escalator. The speaker suggests taking it to the third floor.
records.logic: まで marks the destination limit; で marks the means of travel.
records.difference: エスカレーター carries people between floors; 階段（かいだん） is a staircase.

records.nuance: タオル means towel. 顔をふいた says the speaker wiped or dried their face with one.
records.logic: で marks the towel as the instrument used to wipe the face.
records.difference: タオル is used for wiping or drying; ハンカチ is a small handkerchief.

records.nuance: パチンコ is a Japanese machine game in which small steel balls are launched through pins toward winning pockets. パチンコをする is the ordinary expression for playing it.
records.logic: する forms a verb with the game name; the sentence describes a repeated activity.
records.difference: パチンコ is a pinball-like Japanese machine game; ゲーム is a general game.

records.nuance: みかん is a mandarin orange, commonly eaten as a small citrus fruit. 1つください asks for one.
records.logic: The quantity is explicitly one; the noun itself does not encode a plural.
records.difference: みかん is a mandarin orange; レモン is a lemon.

records.kanji_breakdown: 歯 = tooth; ブラシ = brush
records.nuance: 歯ブラシ means toothbrush. The sentence says a new one is needed.
records.logic: 歯 identifies the teeth the brush is for; ブラシ names the brush.
records.difference: 歯ブラシ is for cleaning teeth; くし is used to comb hair.

records.nuance: ケーキ means cake. The sentence says cake was eaten on someone’s birthday; the Japanese leaves the subject unstated.
records.logic: 誕生日に marks the occasion, not necessarily the cake’s flavor or who baked it.
records.difference: ケーキ is cake; クッキー is a cookie or biscuit.

records.nuance: コップ means a drinking cup or tumbler. コップ一杯の水 is a glassful of water, which the speaker drinks every morning.
records.logic: 一杯 measures one containerful; the phrase does not mean a cup made of water.
records.difference: コップ is an everyday drinking vessel; グラス often refers to a glass drinking vessel. Their uses can overlap.

records.nuance: ナイロン means nylon. このジャケットはナイロンでできています says the jacket is made of nylon.
records.logic: でできています identifies the material the jacket is made from.
records.difference: ナイロン is a synthetic material; 綿（めん） is cotton.

records.nuance: スーツ means a suit. そんなに高くない says that suit is not that expensive; “reasonably priced” is an interpretive English rendering.
records.logic: 高い refers to price in this context; そんなに with the negative softens the judgment.
records.difference: スーツ is a coordinated suit; 制服（せいふく） is a uniform.

records.nuance: チケット means ticket. The sentence gives the price for one ticket to this amusement park; Japanese does not mark the noun as plural.
records.logic: 3000円です states the price; the English “tickets” does not establish a plural in Japanese.
records.difference: チケット is an admission or travel ticket; 切符（きっぷ） often means a transport ticket.

records.nuance: チョコレート means chocolate. The sentence says the younger sister loves it very much.
records.logic: 大好き expresses strong liking; the word identifies the food.
records.difference: チョコレート is chocolate; 飴（あめ） is candy or sweets.

records.nuance: チャンネル means a television channel here. 変えてください politely asks someone to change it, without naming the new channel.
records.logic: The TV context selects the broadcast-channel sense; 変える requests a change.
records.difference: チャンネル is a TV channel; 番組（ばんぐみ） is a program or show.

records.nuance: マッチ means a matchstick here. 持っていますか asks whether the listener has one; it does not mean a sports match.
records.logic: Possessing an item fits the question; the context-free noun can have other senses in other settings.
records.difference: マッチ is a matchstick; ライター is a lighter.

records.nuance: いとこ means cousin. The sentence says the cousin and speaker are the same age; it does not specify the cousin’s gender.
records.logic: と私は joins the cousin with the speaker as the two people being compared.
records.difference: いとこ is a cousin; 兄弟（きょうだい） means siblings.

records.kanji_breakdown: ストーブ = room heater; stove
records.nuance: ストーブ usually means an indoor heating appliance in Japanese. Here the family still uses one at home; the sentence does not specify its fuel.
records.logic: うちでは sets the home as the setting; 使っています describes continued use.
records.difference: ストーブ is usually a room heater in Japanese; コンロ is a cooking burner or stove.

records.kanji_breakdown: ガソリンスタンド = gas station
records.nuance: ガソリンスタンド means gas station or filling station. The speaker asks whether one is nearby.
records.logic: この近くに asks about a place in the nearby area; ありますか asks whether it exists there.
records.difference: ガソリンスタンド is a fuel station; 駐車場（ちゅうしゃじょう） is a parking lot.

records.nuance: デート means a date or romantic outing. The sentence says the speaker went to an amusement park on a date; the Japanese does not state the subject explicitly.
records.logic: 遊園地に gives the destination, and デートで frames the outing as a date.
records.difference: デート is a romantic outing; 旅行（りょこう） is a trip and does not imply romance.

records.nuance: 襖 means a Japanese sliding panel used as a room partition or door. The sentence asks someone to close it.
records.logic: This is a specific interior fitting, not a generic hinged door. The reading and example distinguish it from 麩（ふすま）, wheat bran, which is also read ふすま.
records.difference: 襖 is a paper- or cloth-covered sliding partition; 障子（しょうじ） is a different type of sliding screen.

records.nuance: レモン means lemon. The speaker put lemon in tea and drank it.
records.logic: 紅茶に marks the tea as the drink receiving the lemon; 入れて links adding it with drinking.
records.difference: レモン is a lemon; ライム is a lime.

records.nuance: チーズ means cheese. 一切れ specifies one slice or piece.
records.logic: The counter 一切れ supplies the portion; チーズ names the food.
records.difference: チーズ is cheese; バター is butter.

records.kanji_breakdown: ドライブ = drive; car outing
records.nuance: ドライブ means driving or a car outing. Here the speaker went as far as Gunma by car; the Japanese does not make the driver’s identity explicit.
records.logic: まで marks Gunma as the extent or destination of the trip. The English “I drove” is a natural rendering, but ドライブしました can describe taking a drive.
records.difference: ドライブ is a car outing or drive; 旅行（りょこう） is a trip that need not be by car.
records.filipino: nag-drive hanggang Gunma; namasyal sakay ng kotse

records.nuance: ラケット means racket. The sentence says a tennis racket was bought.
records.logic: テニスの specifies the sport the racket is for; 買いました is the purchase.
records.difference: ラケット is used to hit a ball in racket sports; バット is used in baseball.

records.kanji_breakdown: スチュワーデス = stewardess; female flight attendant
records.nuance: スチュワーデス is an older, gender-specific term for a female flight attendant. The sentence says she became one. Current neutral Japanese terms include 客室乗務員 or フライトアテンダント.
records.logic: 彼女 identifies a woman in this sentence; なった marks becoming the occupation.
records.difference: スチュワーデス is specifically female and dated; 客室乗務員 is a gender-neutral term for cabin crew.

records.kanji_breakdown: テープレコーダー = tape recorder
records.nuance: テープレコーダー means tape recorder. The speaker recorded their own voice on it.
records.logic: で marks the recorder as the device used; 自分の声 is the speaker’s own voice.
records.difference: A テープレコーダー records sound on tape; a digital recorder need not use tape.
records.filipino: tape recorder; aparatong pangrekord ng boses

records.nuance: ソース means sauce. ソースはどれですか asks which sauce it is; the Japanese alone does not specify Worcestershire sauce, though that is the deck’s English gloss.
records.logic: どれ selects one item from a visible or known set; the context determines the sauce type.
records.difference: ソース is a broad word for sauce; ウースターソース names Worcestershire sauce specifically.
records.filipino: sarsa; Worcestershire sauce kung iyon ang uri

records.nuance: タイプライター means typewriter. The sentence says the mother owns an old one.
records.logic: 古い describes its age; 持っています expresses possession.
records.difference: タイプライター prints typed characters mechanically; a computer keyboard is used with a computer.

records.nuance: トマト means tomato. The sentence says the speaker loves tomatoes; Japanese does not mark the noun as plural.
records.logic: が marks the thing loved, while 大好き expresses strong liking.
records.difference: トマト is a tomato; きゅうり is a cucumber.

records.nuance: バター means butter. The speaker spread some on bread and ate it.
records.logic: パンに marks where the butter was spread; ぬって connects spreading with eating.
records.difference: バター is butter; チーズ is cheese.

records.nuance: バレーボール means volleyball. 得意です says the younger sister is good at playing it.
records.logic: が marks the activity she is skilled at; 得意 describes ability, not simply liking the sport.
records.difference: バレーボール is volleyball; バスケットボール is basketball.

records.nuance: カレンダー means calendar. The speaker wrote a schedule or plans on it.
records.logic: に marks where the plans were written; 予定 refers to scheduled plans or appointments.
records.difference: カレンダー displays dates and scheduled plans; 時計（とけい） shows the time.

records.nuance: ハンドバッグ means handbag. 忘れました says the speaker forgot it or left it behind; the sentence does not say where.
records.logic: The handbag is the object of 忘れる; the location and circumstances are unstated.
records.difference: ハンドバッグ is a small bag carried by hand; 財布（さいふ） is a wallet.

records.nuance: ベル means bell. 玄関のベルが鳴った says the bell at the entrance rang.
records.logic: 玄関の locates the bell at the entrance; 鳴った describes the sound occurring.
records.difference: ベル is a bell; チャイム is a chime or door chime.

records.kanji_breakdown: 給 = provide / pay; 料 = fee / amount (character cues)
records.nuance: 給料 means salary or wages. The sentence says the salary will rise starting next year.
records.logic: The compound names regular pay for work; 来年から sets when the increase begins.
records.difference: 給料 is pay from employment; 賞金（しょうきん） is prize money.

records.kanji_breakdown: 卒 = complete / finish; 業 = study / work (character cues)
records.nuance: 卒業 means graduating or completing a course of study. The speaker graduated from university last year.
records.logic: 大学を identifies the institution or course completed; 去年 gives the time.
records.difference: 卒業 is completing a school course; 入学（にゅうがく） is entering a school.

records.kanji_breakdown: 就 = take up / enter; 職 = occupation / job
records.nuance: 就職 means entering employment or finding a job. The sentence says young people have recently been finding employment difficult.
records.logic: The subject is young people’s job-seeking/employment situation; 難しくなっています describes a recent growing difficulty.
records.difference: 就職 is starting or obtaining employment; 転職（てんしょく） is changing jobs.

records.kanji_breakdown: 退 = leave / withdraw; 院 = institution / hospital
records.nuance: 退院 means leaving a hospital after treatment or being discharged. The sentence says the speaker’s mother will be discharged today.
records.logic: 今日 sets the discharge day; the word describes leaving hospital care, not leaving a school or other institution in this context.
records.difference: 退院 is discharge from hospital; 入院（にゅういん） is entering or staying in hospital.

records.nuance: インク means ink. The speaker bought ink for a printer.
records.logic: プリンターの identifies what the ink is for; 買った is a completed purchase.
records.difference: インク is printing or writing ink; トナー is printer toner.

records.kanji_breakdown: 契 = pledge / agreement; 約 = agreement / terms (character cues)
records.nuance: 契約 means a contract or agreement. The player made a contract with a new team; the Japanese does not specify the signing procedure.
records.logic: と marks the other party to the agreement; 新しいチーム identifies the team.
records.difference: 契約 is a formal agreement; 約束（やくそく） is a promise and can be less formal.

records.kanji_breakdown: 交 = exchange; 渉 = deal with / interact (character cues)
records.nuance: 交渉 is discussion between parties to arrange terms or resolve an issue. It names the negotiating process, not a guaranteed agreement; negotiations may continue, succeed, or break down.
records.logic: 今 and しています show an ongoing negotiation; 値段を is the matter being discussed.
records.difference: 交渉 is discussion to reach terms; 相談（そうだん） is consultation or asking advice.

records.kanji_breakdown: 事 = matter / event; 件 = case / matter (character cues)
records.nuance: 事件 means an incident or case. Here 犯人 and 捕まっていない show it is a criminal case whose perpetrator has not yet been caught.
records.logic: The rest of the sentence narrows the broad word 事件 to a case involving an offender.
records.difference: 事件 is an incident or case; 事故（じこ） is an accident.

records.kanji_breakdown: 条 = clause / item; 件 = matter / condition (character cues)
records.nuance: 条件 means condition or terms. この条件では厳し過ぎます says these terms are too strict or demanding.
records.logic: では frames the judgment under these conditions; 厳し過ぎる means excessively strict or severe.
records.difference: 条件 are terms or conditions; 結果（けっか） is a result.

records.kanji_breakdown: クーラー = air conditioner; cooler
records.nuance: クーラー commonly means an air conditioner in this hot-weather context. つけました says the speaker turned it on.
records.logic: 暑いので gives the reason for turning on the cooling appliance; the sentence does not describe a temperature setting.
records.difference: クーラー is used for cooling; 暖房（だんぼう） is heating.

records.kanji_breakdown: 参 = join / take part; 加 = add / join
records.nuance: 参加 means participating or taking part. 明日は市民マラソンに参加します says the speaker will take part in the community marathon tomorrow.
records.logic: The verb describes joining an event; 明日 sets it in the future.
records.difference: 参加 is taking part in an event; 観戦（かんせん） is watching a sports event.

records.nuance: 増加 means an increase. The island’s population is increasing year by year.
records.logic: 年々 describes a repeated yearly trend; the population itself is increasing.
records.difference: 増加 is an increase; 減少（げんしょう） is a decrease.

records.nuance: 加える is a transitive verb meaning to add something to something else. Here salt and pepper are to be added.
records.logic: The items being added are marked by を; the target is understood from the cooking context.
records.difference: 加える adds something to a mixture; 入れる（いれる） means to put something in and can overlap in context.

records.kanji_breakdown: 加 = add / apply; 工 = work / craft (character cues)
records.nuance: 加工 means processing or manufacturing material. The sentence says the factory processes fish.
records.logic: The word refers to working material into a processed form; it is an established compound, not a literal historical recipe of its characters.
records.difference: 加工 is processing a material; 調理（ちょうり） is preparing food to eat.

records.nuance: ミルク means milk. The sentence says the speaker gave the baby milk; it may be formula or other milk, as context allows.
records.logic: に marks the baby as recipient and を marks the milk given.
records.difference: ミルク is milk or milk-based feeding; 母乳（ぼにゅう） specifically means breast milk.

records.nuance: 比べる means to compare. The speaker compared this month’s sales with last month’s.
records.logic: 今月と先月 pairs the two periods being compared; 売上 is the item compared.
records.difference: 比べる compares items; 調べる（しらべる） means to examine or investigate.

records.kanji_breakdown: 批 = criticize; 判 = judge / assess (character cues)
records.nuance: 批判 means criticism or criticizing. Here he criticized a colleague; the word can describe evaluation that is negative or disapproving.
records.logic: The object を identifies the colleague as the person criticized; the compound is used as an established word.
records.difference: 批判 is critical judgment; 評価（ひょうか） is a broader evaluation that may be positive, neutral or negative.

records.kanji_breakdown: 評 = assess; 価 = value (character cues)
records.nuance: 評価 means evaluation or assessment. 評価が上がった says his assessment or standing rose recently; it does not literally say he received more recognition.
records.logic: が marks what increased: the evaluation/standing, rather than the man himself.
records.difference: 評価 is an assessment or rating; 批判（ひはん） specifically emphasizes criticism.
records.filipino: pagsusuri; pagtaas ng pagkilala sa kaniya

records.kanji_breakdown: 対 = facing / directed toward; 象 = image / object (character cues)
records.nuance: 対象 means a target or subject. The questionnaire is intended for university students.
records.logic: が対象 identifies university students as the group the questionnaire covers; the whole-word sense is not a literal character-by-character etymology.
records.difference: 対象 is the group or thing a survey concerns; 目的（もくてき） is its purpose.

records.nuance: サラダ means salad. The speaker ate a lot of it.
records.logic: を marks the food eaten; たくさん expresses a large amount.
records.difference: サラダ is a salad; スープ is soup.

records.kanji_breakdown: 故 = fault / cause; 障 = hinder / obstruct (character cues)
records.nuance: 故障 means a malfunction or breakdown. The refrigerator broke down.
records.logic: The appliance is the subject of the malfunction; 故障しました states that it failed.
records.difference: 故障 is a mechanical or equipment failure; 修理（しゅうり） is the repair done afterward.

records.kanji_breakdown: 修 = repair / restore; 理 = put in order (character cues)
records.nuance: 修理 means repairing something. 車を修理に出した says the speaker sent or took the car in for repair.
records.logic: に marks the purpose of sending the car; 出した shows arranging for the repair rather than necessarily fixing it personally.
records.difference: 修理 is fixing a damaged item; 故障（こしょう） is the malfunction that may require repair.

records.kanji_breakdown: 乗 = ride; 換 = change / exchange
records.nuance: 乗り換える means to transfer from one vehicle or route to another. The speaker will transfer to the subway at the next station.
records.logic: 次の駅で marks where the transfer occurs; the subway is the vehicle being changed to.
records.difference: 乗り換える changes transport; 乗り過ごす（のりすごす） means to ride past one’s stop.

records.kanji_breakdown: 乗 = ride; 換 = change / exchange
records.nuance: 乗り換え is a transfer or change of vehicles. 次の駅で乗り換えです says the transfer is at the next station; Japanese leaves the subject unstated.
records.logic: This is the noun form naming the transfer; the deck’s “I’m transferring” supplies a subject and verb not present in this sentence.
records.difference: 乗り換え is a transfer; 乗り換える is the verb “to transfer.”

records.kanji_breakdown: おじさん = uncle; middle-aged man (context-dependent)
records.nuance: おじさん can mean an uncle or, when referring to someone outside the family, a middle-aged man. The deck gloss and this sentence support “my uncle,” but the kana spelling itself does not show the family relationship.
records.logic: 昨日おじさんに会いました says the speaker met him yesterday; the familial reading follows the note’s gloss, not a special kanji distinction.
records.difference: おじさん can refer to an uncle or a middle-aged man; おじいさん usually means grandfather or an elderly man.
records.filipino: tiyuhin; lalaking nasa katanghaliang-gulang (depende sa konteksto)

records.nuance: 換える means to exchange or replace one thing with another. Here the car’s tires were changed.
records.logic: 車のタイヤ is what was replaced; the sentence does not say who did the work.
records.difference: 換える emphasizes exchanging/replacing; 変える（かえる） more broadly means to alter or change something.

records.kanji_breakdown: 着 = wear; 替 = change / replace
records.nuance: 着替える means to change clothes. He changed into clean clothes.
records.logic: に marks the resulting clothing; the verb describes putting on a different outfit.
records.difference: 着替える is changing one’s clothes; 着る（きる） simply means to wear or put on clothing.

records.nuance: 被る（かぶる） means to put on or wear something on the head, especially a hat. Here he went out wearing a hat.
records.logic: 帽子を is the item worn; て-form links wearing it with going out. The reading is fixed by the vocabulary field.
records.meaning: to put on; wear (on the head)
records.difference: 被る（かぶる） is used for hats; 着る（きる） is used for many clothes worn on the upper body.

records.nuance: 破る is transitive: it can mean to tear something or break a rule or promise. 約束を破った means he broke his promise.
records.logic: 約束 selects the figurative “fail to keep” sense, not physically tearing paper.
records.difference: 約束を破る means break a promise; 破れる（やぶれる） often describes something tearing or becoming torn.

records.nuance: ベルト means belt. きつくなりました says it has become tight; the sentence does not explain why.
records.logic: The belt is the subject of the change in fit; avoid inferring a change in the belt or wearer.
records.difference: ベルト is worn around the waist; ネクタイ is worn around the neck.

records.nuance: 破れる is generally intransitive: something tears or becomes torn. Here the shirt is in a torn state.
records.logic: シャツが marks the item affected; the sentence does not state who or what tore it.
records.difference: シャツが破れる describes a shirt tearing; シャツを破る means someone tears a shirt.

records.nuance: 壊す is transitive and means to break or damage something. Here she broke the speaker’s phone.
records.logic: The phone is marked by を as the object affected; the sentence does not establish whether the damage is irreparable.
records.difference: 壊す means someone breaks something; 壊れる（こわれる） means something breaks or stops working.

records.nuance: 壊れる is generally intransitive: something breaks or stops working. Here the company computer broke down.
records.logic: The computer is marked by が as the thing that failed; no person causing it is named.
records.difference: 壊れる describes something breaking; 壊す describes someone breaking it.

records.kanji_breakdown: 救 = rescue; 急 = urgent; 車 = vehicle
records.nuance: 救急車 means ambulance. The speaker asks someone to call one.
records.logic: The word names an emergency vehicle; 呼んでください requests that someone call it.
records.difference: 救急車 is an ambulance; パトカー（ぱとかー） is a police car.

records.nuance: ラーメン means ramen, a noodle dish. The sentence says the speaker ate ramen for supper.
records.logic: 夕食に marks it as the meal; the Japanese does not state a particular broth or topping.
records.difference: ラーメン is a noodle dish; うどん is another Japanese noodle dish, usually thicker.

records.nuance: 助ける means to help or rescue. Here she helped a sick dog.
records.logic: The dog is the object receiving help; the sentence does not specify the kind of help.
records.difference: 助ける is helping someone or something; 手伝う（てつだう） usually means helping with a task.

records.kanji_breakdown: 立 = stand; 派 = group / school (character cues only)
records.nuance: 立派 describes someone as admirable, excellent, or respectable. Here it praises him as a fine person; the whole word is not a literal sum of the character glosses.
records.logic: It evaluates the person positively as an established word; it does not mean “standing group.”
records.difference: 立派な人 is an admirable person; 優しい（やさしい） specifically means kind or gentle.

records.kanji_breakdown: 警 = guard / warn; 察 = observe / inspect (character cues)
records.nuance: 警察 means the police or police authorities. The sentence politely asks someone to call them.
records.logic: The institution responds to the request; 警察 does not name one specific officer.
records.difference: 警察 is the police; 消防署（しょうぼうしょ） is the fire department.

records.kanji_breakdown: 管 = manage / control; 理 = order / reason (character cues)
records.nuance: 管理 means managing or keeping something organized and under control. Here she manages the speaker’s schedule.
records.logic: 私のスケジュール is what she oversees; the sentence does not say whether she created it or only maintains it.
records.difference: 管理 is overseeing and organizing; 予定を立てる（よていをたてる） means making a schedule.

records.nuance: ライター means a lighter in this note. The speaker forgot it at the shop.
records.logic: This katakana word can also represent “writer”; the Vocabulary-English field and shop context identify the fire-starting device.
records.difference: ライター is a lighter here; マッチ is a matchstick.

records.nuance: 盗む means to steal. Someone stole the speaker’s bag.
records.logic: が marks the unknown person as the thief; を marks the bag as the stolen object.
records.difference: 盗む means taking something unlawfully; 拾う（ひろう） means picking something up and does not itself imply theft.

records.nuance: 殺す means to kill. The sentence says the speaker hates killing living things.
records.logic: 生き物を identifies living creatures as the object; 嫌いだ expresses the speaker’s strong dislike of doing this.
records.difference: 殺す means to kill; 傷つける（きずつける） means to hurt or injure, which need not be fatal.

records.nuance: 逮捕 means arrest. Here the criminal who had been fleeing was arrested.
records.logic: 逃げていた describes the criminal’s prior escape; 逮捕されました is passive and formal, focusing on the arrest.
records.difference: 逮捕 is arrest by authorities; 捕まえる（つかまえる） is the broader verb “to catch.”

records.nuance: 逃げる means to escape or get away. Here the bird flew out through the window.
records.logic: から marks the point it escaped from; the sentence does not mean the bird merely ran on foot.
records.difference: 逃げる means to escape; 飛ぶ（とぶ） means to fly and does not itself mean escape.

records.kanji_breakdown: ワイシャツ = dress shirt; business shirt
records.nuance: ワイシャツ is a collared shirt commonly worn with a suit. Although the word comes from “white shirt,” it can refer to colored shirts too; this sentence explicitly says his is white.
records.logic: 白い describes the shirt’s color here; it is not required by the noun ワイシャツ itself.
records.difference: ワイシャツ is a collared shirt often worn under a suit; Tシャツ is a casual T-shirt.

records.nuance: 戦争 means war. The sentence says there was a war in Iraq in 2003.
records.logic: で marks Iraq as the place where the war occurred; the year sets the time.
records.difference: 戦争 is war between organized sides; 競争（きょうそう） is competition.

records.nuance: 競争 means competition. The sentence says the two companies are competing with each other.
records.logic: 互いに makes the reciprocal relation explicit; the competition may be commercial, but the sentence gives no further details.
records.difference: 競争 is competing for advantage; 協力（きょうりょく） is cooperation.

records.nuance: 混む means to be crowded or congested. Here the train is crowded.
records.logic: 電車が marks the train as crowded; it does not necessarily describe a traffic jam.
records.difference: 電車が混む means the train is crowded; 電車が遅れる（おくれる） means the train is delayed.

records.kanji_breakdown: 大 = great / large; 統 = govern / unite; 領 = territory (character cues)
records.nuance: 大統領 means president of a country. The sentence asks who France’s president is; it is asking a question, not asserting an answer.
records.logic: フランスの identifies the country; 誰ですか asks for the person holding the office.
records.difference: 大統領 is a national president; 首相（しゅしょう） is a prime minister.

records.nuance: シャワー means shower. 急いでシャワーを浴びました says the speaker hurried through taking one in the morning.
records.logic: 急いで means in a hurry; it may imply a quick shower but does not give an exact duration.
records.difference: シャワー is a shower; お風呂（おふろ） often refers to bathing in a tub.

records.nuance: 捨てる means to throw away or discard. The sentence politely asks someone to throw out the garbage.
records.logic: ゴミを identifies the item to discard; てください makes it a request.
records.difference: 捨てる means discard; 拾う（ひろう） means pick up.

records.nuance: 拾う means to pick up or find something. Here the speaker picked up a wallet in the street.
records.logic: 道で locates where it was found; the sentence does not say the speaker kept it.
records.difference: 拾う is picking up something found; 盗む（ぬすむ） means stealing something.

records.nuance: 池 means pond. The sentence says there are koi in it.
records.logic: に marks the pond as the place where the fish are; 鯉 names the fish.
records.difference: 池 is a pond; 川（かわ） is a river.

records.kanji_breakdown: 電 = electricity; 池 = pool (character cues only)
records.nuance: 電池 means battery or cell. The sentence suggests putting a new battery in.
records.logic: Learn 電池 as the established word for a power cell; 池 here does not mean that it contains a literal pool of electricity.
records.difference: 電池 stores electrical energy; 電源（でんげん） means a power source or supply.

records.nuance: うどん means thick Japanese wheat noodles. The speaker ate them for lunch.
records.logic: お昼に marks the meal; the sentence does not specify the broth or toppings.
records.difference: うどん are thick wheat noodles; そば are thinner buckwheat noodles.
records.filipino: udon; makakapal na noodles na gawa sa trigo

records.nuance: 深い means deep. It describes the pond’s physical depth here.
records.logic: とても intensifies the adjective; the sentence is about water depth, not emotional or intellectual depth.
records.difference: 深い describes great depth; 浅い（あさい） means shallow.

records.kanji_breakdown: 深 = deep; さ = forms a measure of degree
records.nuance: 深さ means depth. The sentence states that the pool’s depth is two meters.
records.logic: Adding さ to 深い forms a noun measuring how deep something is; 2メートル gives that measure.
records.difference: 深さ is a measured depth; 深い is the adjective “deep.”

records.nuance: 浅い means shallow. The sentence describes the river’s depth.
records.logic: です presents the description politely; the word can be figurative elsewhere, but this river context is physical.
records.difference: 浅い means shallow; 深い（ふかい） means deep.

records.nuance: 落とす means to drop something and, with a wallet, can mean to lose it by letting it fall. The Japanese says 財布 (wallet); the deck English uses “purse.”
records.logic: The speaker dropped or lost the wallet along the way; the Japanese does not imply a deliberate act. The original English wording is preserved separately.
records.difference: 落とす is transitive (“drop/lose something”); 落ちる（おちる） is intransitive (“fall”).

records.nuance: ごみ means garbage or trash. 今日はごみの日 means today is the designated garbage day, usually a collection day.
records.logic: The sentence identifies the day; it does not directly command anyone to throw something out.
records.difference: ごみ is trash; ごみ箱（ばこ） is a trash bin.
records.filipino: basura; araw ng koleksiyon ng basura

records.nuance: 泳ぐ means to swim. Here she swims to lose weight; the Japanese leaves the exact routine unstated.
records.logic: ている can describe an ongoing or repeated activity; ために gives her purpose.
records.difference: 泳ぐ is swimming; 水泳（すいえい） is swimming as a sport or activity.

records.nuance: 水泳 means swimming as an activity or sport. The sentence says the mother swims for her health.
records.logic: する makes the activity into a verb; 健康のために gives the purpose.
records.difference: 水泳 is the activity of swimming; 泳ぐ is the verb “to swim.”

records.nuance: 流れる means to flow or be carried along. With music coming from a radio, it means the music is playing or being broadcast.
records.logic: から marks the radio as the source; the music is the subject, so it is not describing a person playing an instrument.
records.difference: 音楽が流れる means music is playing; 音楽を流す means someone plays or broadcasts music.
records.filipino: tumutugtog sa radyo; ipinapalabas sa radyo

records.kanji_breakdown: 流 = circulate; 行 = go (character cues only)
records.nuance: 流行る means to become popular or fashionable. Sneakers were popular last year.
records.logic: 去年 sets the time; スニーカーが marks what was in fashion. The word can also refer to an illness spreading in other contexts.
records.meaning: to be popular; be in fashion
records.difference: 流行る means to become popular; 売れる（うれる） means to sell well.

records.kanji_breakdown: スーパーマーケット = supermarket
records.nuance: スーパーマーケット means supermarket. The speaker bought carrots there.
records.logic: で marks the place of purchase; 人参（にんじん） is the item bought.
records.difference: スーパーマーケット is a large self-service grocery store; 市場（いちば） is a market.

records.nuance: 洗う means to wash. 早く顔を洗いなさい tells someone to hurry up and wash their face.
records.logic: 顔を marks what to wash; なさい gives a direct instruction, often used by an older or authoritative speaker.
records.difference: 洗う means wash with water; 拭く（ふく） means wipe.

records.kanji_breakdown: 洗 = wash; 面 = face; 所 = place
records.nuance: 洗面所 means a washroom or area with a washbasin. Here she washed her face there; it does not necessarily mean a public restroom.
records.logic: The word names a place for washing up; the sentence’s action fits a sink or vanity area.
records.difference: 洗面所 is a place to wash one’s face; 浴室（よくしつ） is a bathing room.

records.nuance: 油 means oil. 水と油は混ざらない says oil and water do not mix.
records.logic: と pairs the two substances; 混ざらない states their ordinary separation.
records.difference: 油 is oil or grease; 水（みず） is water.

records.nuance: 沈む means to sink or go under. The boat sank in the river.
records.logic: 川に marks where it sank; the sentence describes the boat going below the water’s surface.
records.difference: 沈む means sink; 浮かぶ（うかぶ） means float.

records.nuance: ハンカチ means handkerchief. The speaker wiped their hands with one.
records.logic: で marks the handkerchief as the instrument; 手をふく means wipe or dry the hands.
records.difference: ハンカチ is a small cloth carried for wiping; タオル is usually a larger towel.

records.kanji_breakdown: 久 = long time; しぶり = interval since last occurrence
records.nuance: 久しぶり means after a long time or in a while. The speaker will meet a friend tomorrow after not seeing them for some time.
records.logic: に marks the occasion of meeting after that interval; the word does not specify exactly how long.
records.meaning: after a long time; in a while
records.difference: 久しぶり marks a long gap since the last occasion; すぐ means soon or right away.
records.filipino: matagal na panahon; makalipas ang matagal na panahon

records.nuance: 氷 means ice. The speaker asks someone to put some in a glass.
records.logic: に marks the glass as the destination; 入れてください is a polite request to put it in.
records.difference: 氷 is frozen water; 雪（ゆき） is snow.

records.nuance: 冷える means to become cold or chilled. Here the air conditioner made the speaker’s body feel cold; the Japanese does not necessarily mean they felt fear or had a fever.
records.logic: 体が marks the body as the thing that became cold; クーラーで gives the cause.
records.difference: 冷える describes something becoming cold; 冷やす（ひやす） means to cool something deliberately.
records.filipino: ginaw; nanlamig ang katawan dahil sa aircon

records.nuance: 冷やす means to cool something. In 頭を冷やしなさい, it is an idiom: calm down and think more clearly, rather than literally cooling the head.
records.logic: The phrase uses a physical cooling image for reducing excitement or anger; it is a direct instruction.
records.difference: 頭を冷やす means regain composure; 冷える means to become cold without stating someone cooled it.
records.filipino: kumalma ka muna; palamigin ang ulo

records.nuance: ビデオテープ means videotape. The speaker says they have 30 of them.
records.logic: 30本 counts long cylindrical or tape items; 持っています expresses possession.
records.difference: ビデオテープ stores recorded video on tape; DVD is a different recording medium.

records.nuance: 冷める means to cool down; figuratively, interest or affection can fade. Here the speaker’s feelings for him have died down.
records.logic: 気持ちが marks the feelings as the thing that changed; the sentence is emotional, not about temperature.
records.difference: 気持ちが冷める means feelings fade; 冷える commonly describes becoming physically cold or chilly.
records.filipino: lumamig ang damdamin para sa kaniya

records.nuance: 凍る means to freeze. The sentence says roads freeze on cold mornings.
records.logic: 寒い朝 marks the conditions when the roads freeze; the sentence does not say someone freezes them deliberately.
records.difference: 凍る means turn to ice; 冷える means become cold without necessarily freezing.

records.kanji_breakdown: 冷 = cold; 蔵 = store; 庫 = storage place (character cues)
records.nuance: 冷蔵庫 means refrigerator. The sentence says drinks are in it.
records.logic: に marks the refrigerator as the location; this is the whole-word name for the appliance, not a literal “cold warehouse” description.
records.difference: 冷蔵庫 keeps food and drinks cold; 冷凍庫（れいとうこ） is a freezer.

records.nuance: 涼しい means pleasantly cool or refreshing. The sentence says it will get cooler in the evening.
records.logic: 夕方 sets the time of the change; よ signals an informative or reassuring tone.
records.difference: 涼しい describes comfortably cool weather; 寒い（さむい） usually means cold in an uncomfortable or stronger sense.

records.kanji_breakdown: ぶらぶら = wander about; stroll aimlessly
records.nuance: ぶらぶら describes wandering or strolling around without a fixed task. The speaker wandered around the neighborhood in the morning.
records.logic: 近所を marks the area; した makes the mimetic adverb into a casual activity.
records.difference: ぶらぶら is aimless or relaxed wandering; 散歩（さんぽ） is a walk or stroll, often for exercise.

records.nuance: 汚す is transitive: to make something dirty or soil it. Here he got his clothes dirty.
records.logic: 服を marks the clothing he dirtied; the verb presents him as the cause.
records.difference: 汚す means make something dirty; 汚れる（よごれる） means become dirty.

records.nuance: 汚れ means dirt or a stain. The sentence says the dirt was removed from the shoes.
records.logic: 靴の汚れ is the dirt on the shoes; 落としました means the speaker removed it.
records.difference: 汚れ is the dirt itself; 汚れる（よごれる） means become dirty.

records.nuance: 汚れる is generally intransitive: to become dirty. The sentence warns that clothes will get dirty if no apron is worn.
records.logic: 服が marks the clothes as the affected item; 汚す would say someone dirties them.
records.difference: 汚れる means become dirty; 汚す means make something dirty.

records.kanji_breakdown: 景 = view / scene; 色 = appearance / color (character cues)
records.nuance: 景色 means scenery or a view of the surrounding landscape. Here the speaker says the scenery is beautiful.
records.logic: ここは sets the place being admired; 景色 is the visible surroundings as a whole.
records.difference: 景色 is the view or surrounding landscape; 景色の一部 can include a 山（やま）, mountain.

records.kanji_breakdown: アナウンサー = announcer; broadcaster
records.nuance: アナウンサー means a broadcast announcer or presenter. The speaker wants to become one; the sentence does not restrict the job to reading news.
records.logic: に marks the occupation the speaker wants to become; なりたい expresses that wish.
records.difference: アナウンサー presents or announces on broadcast media; 記者（きしゃ） is a journalist or reporter.
records.filipino: announcer; tagapagbalita sa radyo o telebisyon

records.kanji_breakdown: 影 = shadow; 響 = echo / resound (character cues only)
records.nuance: 影響 means influence or effect. 彼から大きな影響を受けました says the speaker was greatly influenced by him.
records.logic: The phrase 影響を受ける describes another person’s influence reaching and affecting someone; it is not simply physical sound or a shadow.
records.difference: 影響 is a broad effect on someone or something; 感化（かんか） often suggests a personal or moral influence.
records.filipino: malaking impluwensiya; malaki ang naging impluwensiya niya sa akin

records.nuance: 光る means to shine or sparkle. Here the waves were sparkling.
records.logic: きらきら describes the repeated glittering appearance; the waves are the thing shining.
records.difference: 光る is giving off or reflecting light; 照らす（てらす） means to illuminate something.

records.nuance: 太る means to gain weight or become heavier. The sentence says the speaker’s older sister puts on weight easily.
records.logic: すぐ suggests that this happens readily or quickly; it does not specify how much weight.
records.difference: 太る means gain weight; 痩せる（やせる） means lose weight.

records.kanji_breakdown: 太 = great / large; 陽 = sun / sunlight (character cues)
records.nuance: 太陽 means the sun. In this sentence it disappeared behind a cloud.
records.logic: The whole word names the sun; 雲に隠れた describes it becoming obscured from view.
records.difference: 太陽 is the sun; 星（ほし） commonly means the other visible celestial bodies in the night sky.
records.filipino: araw; natakpan ng ulap ang araw

records.nuance: スプーン means spoon. Curry rice is eaten with one.
records.logic: で marks the utensil used to eat the meal.
records.difference: スプーン is used for scooping food; フォーク is a fork.

records.nuance: 星 means a star or, more broadly, a point-like celestial body. 今夜は星がよく見えます says they are clearly visible tonight.
records.logic: よく見える describes visibility; in this night-sky context, 星 refers to lights seen in the sky, not spots or symbols.
records.difference: 星 in the night sky is a celestial light; 惑星（わくせい） specifically means planet.

records.kanji_breakdown: 地 = earth / ground; 球 = sphere
records.nuance: 地球 means Earth, the planet. The sentence says it is round.
records.logic: The established word names our planet; 丸い describes its shape in a simple everyday sense.
records.difference: 地球 is the planet Earth; 世界（せかい） means the world or human society.

records.nuance: 野球 means baseball. The speaker played baseball with a friend.
records.logic: と marks the person they played with; しました is the past form of する with the sport.
records.difference: 野球 is baseball; サッカー is soccer.

records.nuance: 雲 means cloud. Today there are many clouds.
records.logic: が marks clouds as the thing present in abundance; 多い means many.
records.difference: 雲 is a cloud; 霧（きり） is fog.

records.nuance: ブラウス means blouse. The sentence says she is wearing a white blouse.
records.logic: 白い gives the color; 着ている describes what she has on.
records.difference: ブラウス is a blouse; ワイシャツ is a collared shirt commonly worn with a suit.

records.nuance: 曇り means cloudiness or cloudy weather. The sentence says it was overcast all day.
records.logic: 一日 marks the duration; でした describes the day’s weather.
records.difference: 曇り describes an overcast sky; 雨（あめ） means rain.

records.kanji_breakdown: 地 = earth / ground; 震 = shake
records.nuance: 地震 means earthquake. 日本は地震が多いです says Japan has many earthquakes.
records.logic: が多い describes frequent occurrence; the sentence states frequency, not that an earthquake is happening now.
records.difference: 地震 is shaking of the ground; 台風（たいふう） is a typhoon.
records.filipino: lindol; madalas ang lindol sa Japan

records.nuance: 震える means to tremble or shiver. Here he was shivering because he was cold.
records.logic: 寒くて gives the reason for the trembling; the sentence is not about fear.
records.difference: 震える is trembling, often involuntarily; 振る（ふる） is to shake or wave something deliberately.

records.nuance: 振る means to shake or wave something. The dog is wagging its tail.
records.logic: 犬が is the dog doing the action, and しっぽを is the tail being moved.
records.difference: 犬がしっぽを振る is wagging its tail; しっぽが揺れる describes the tail swaying.
records.filipino: iwag; kinakawag ng aso ang buntot

records.nuance: リボン means ribbon. The speaker put one on the present, likely as decoration.
records.logic: に marks the present as the item receiving the ribbon; 付けた means attached or added it.
records.difference: リボン is a decorative strip or bow; 包み紙（つつみがみ） is wrapping paper.
records.filipino: laso; nilagyan ko ng laso ang regalo

records.nuance: 揺れる means to sway or shake. The trees are swaying in the wind.
records.logic: 風で gives the cause; the trees move without the sentence naming anyone moving them.
records.difference: 木が揺れる means a tree sways; 木を揺らす（ゆらす） means someone shakes a tree.
records.filipino: umindayog; umiindayog ang mga puno dahil sa hangin

records.kanji_breakdown: 神 = deity / spirit; 社 = shrine
records.nuance: 神社 means a Shinto shrine. The sentence says Kyoto has many shrines.
records.logic: The word names a place of Shinto worship; には frames Kyoto as the place where they are found.
records.difference: 神社 is a Shinto shrine; 寺（てら） is a Buddhist temple.
records.filipino: santuwaryo ng Shinto; maraming shrine sa Kyoto

records.kanji_breakdown: 秘 = hidden; 密 = close / private (character cues)
records.nuance: 秘密 means a secret. これは秘密です says this is confidential or not to be shared.
records.logic: The sentence assigns secret status to これ; 秘密 is not the same as privacy in general.
records.difference: 秘密 is concealed information; 内緒（ないしょ） is a common conversational word for “secret.”

records.nuance: 厳しい means strict or demanding. Here it describes the speaker’s boss.
records.logic: とても intensifies the judgment; the sentence does not say what specific behavior is strict.
records.difference: 厳しい describes demanding standards; 優しい（やさしい） means kind or gentle.

records.nuance: いかが is a polite way to ask how something is. お加減はいかがですか politely asks how someone is feeling or doing health-wise.
records.logic: お加減 is a considerate expression about someone’s condition; いかが makes the question polite.
records.difference: いかが is polite; どう is the more ordinary conversational “how.”

records.kanji_breakdown: 年 = year / age; 寄 = approach / draw near (character cues only)
records.nuance: 年寄り means an older or elderly person. In the example, お年寄り is the polite form, and many elderly people live in that village.
records.logic: お adds respectful politeness; the sentence talks about residents, not a particular elderly person.
records.difference: 年寄り can sound blunt in some contexts; お年寄り is more respectful, while 高齢者（こうれいしゃ） is neutral or formal.
records.filipino: nakatatanda; maraming nakatatanda ang nakatira sa nayong iyon

records.kanji_breakdown: 歴 = passage / sequence; 史 = history / record (character cues)
records.nuance: 歴史 means history, the events and development of the past. The speaker is interested in history.
records.logic: に marks the topic of interest; the sentence does not specify a particular country or period.
records.difference: 歴史 is the past studied or recorded; 昔（むかし） means long ago or the old days.

records.kanji_breakdown: 世 = world / generation; 紀 = era / record (character cues)
records.nuance: 世紀 means century, a period of one hundred years. The sentence says a new century is beginning.
records.logic: 新しい modifies the upcoming period; 始まりです identifies its start.
records.difference: 世紀 is a 100-year period; 年（ねん） is a year.
records.filipino: siglo; simula na ng bagong siglo

records.kanji_breakdown: 建 = build; 設 = establish / set up
records.nuance: 建設 means construction or building. Construction of a new building has begun.
records.logic: 新しいビルの identifies what is being built; 始まった says the work began.
records.difference: 建設 is building or construction; 建物（たてもの） is the resulting building or structure.

records.kanji_breakdown: ステレオ = stereo; stereo system
records.nuance: ステレオ means stereo equipment or a stereo system. In the Japanese sentence, he listened to music on it; 聞いた is past tense, while the deck English says “is listening.”
records.logic: で marks the stereo as the means or equipment used; the Japanese describes a completed listening event.
records.difference: ステレオ is audio equipment; ラジオ is a radio receiver.
records.filipino: stereo; nakinig siya ng musika gamit ang stereo

records.nuance: 建物 means a building or structure. これは日本一古い建物です calls this the oldest building in Japan.
records.logic: The whole word names a built structure; 日本一古い gives its ranking in Japan.
records.difference: 建物 is a building; 建設（けんせつ） is the activity of constructing one.

records.nuance: 建つ means to be built or stand erected. Here a house will be built here next year; Japanese does not say it will be “our” house.
records.logic: 家が is the thing that will be built; this intransitive verb does not name who builds it.
records.difference: 建つ describes something being built; 建てる（たてる） means someone builds it.
records.filipino: may itatayong bahay dito sa susunod na taon

records.kanji_breakdown: 構 = arrange / structure; 成 = form / become (character cues)
records.nuance: 構成 means composition or arrangement of parts. The speaker tried changing the system’s configuration or organization.
records.logic: システムの identifies what is being reorganized; 変えてみました means tried changing it.
records.difference: 構成 is how components are arranged; 構造（こうぞう） is how something is built or physically structured.

records.kanji_breakdown: 構 = build / structure; 造 = make / construct (character cues)
records.nuance: 構造 means structure or construction. The sentence says this building’s structure is complex.
records.logic: この建物の specifies the structure being described; 複雑です means complex.
records.difference: 構造 concerns how something is built; 構成（こうせい） concerns the arrangement or makeup of its parts.

records.nuance: フォーク means fork. もらえますか politely asks whether the speaker can have or receive one.
records.logic: を marks the requested utensil; もらえますか is a polite way to request it.
records.difference: フォーク is used for spearing food; スプーン is used for scooping.
records.filipino: tinidor; maaari po ba akong makahingi ng tinidor?

records.nuance: 橋 means bridge. The sentence says that bridge is the longest in Japan.
records.logic: あの points to a particular bridge; 日本で一番長い makes a superlative comparison within Japan.
records.difference: 橋 crosses a gap or waterway; 道（みち） is a road or path.

records.nuance: 柱 means pillar or column. Here it describes thick pillars in the house.
records.logic: 家の locates the pillars; 太い describes their thickness.
records.difference: 柱 supports a structure; 壁（かべ） is a wall.
records.filipino: haligi; makakapal ang mga haligi sa bahay

records.kanji_breakdown: 位 = position / rank; 置 = place (character cues)
records.nuance: 位置 means position or location. The sentence says the speaker’s town is located north of Tokyo.
records.logic: 東京の北 specifies the location; 位置します is a formal way to say it is situated there.
records.difference: 位置 is a location; 場所（ばしょ） is a general place or spot.
records.filipino: lokasyon; nasa hilaga ng Tokyo ang bayan ko

records.nuance: 離婚 means divorce. The sentence says the speaker’s friend got divorced.
records.logic: The sentence reports the event without saying who initiated it or when the marriage began.
records.difference: 離婚 is ending a marriage; 結婚（けっこん） is marriage.

records.nuance: おば means aunt. The sentence says the aunt lives in Osaka; the kana reading does not show whether she is older or younger than the parent.
records.logic: In kanji, 伯母/叔母 can distinguish an older or younger aunt, but this note’s kana spelling leaves that unspecified.
records.difference: おば is an aunt; おじ is an uncle.
records.filipino: tiyahin; nakatira sa Osaka ang tiyahin ko

records.nuance: 停車 means a train or vehicle stopping. The announcement says this train will not stop before reaching Tokyo.
records.logic: まで sets Tokyo as the endpoint of the no-stop span; the formal 致しません politely announces that it will not stop en route.
records.difference: 停車 is a vehicle stopping; 発車（はっしゃ） is a vehicle departing.
records.filipino: huminto; hindi hihinto ang tren na ito bago makarating sa Tokyo

records.nuance: バス停 means bus stop. The speaker gets off at the next one.
records.logic: 次の marks the next stop; で identifies where the speaker gets off.
records.difference: バス停 is a bus stop; 駅（えき） is a train station.
records.filipino: hintuan ng bus; bababa ako sa susunod na hintuan ng bus

records.kanji_breakdown: 周 = surrounding; 辺 = area / vicinity
records.nuance: 周辺 means the surrounding area or vicinity. There are many universities in this area.
records.logic: この周辺 points to the area around here; it does not mean only the outskirts.
records.difference: 周辺 means the nearby area; 中心（ちゅうしん） is the center.
records.filipino: paligid; maraming unibersidad sa lugar na ito

records.nuance: 隣 means next door or beside. 隣の家 is the neighboring house, where there is a dog.
records.logic: の links 隣 with 家; this is a spatial neighbor, not the person sitting beside someone.
records.difference: 隣 means directly next to or neighboring; 近く（ちかく） means nearby more generally.

records.nuance: きらきら describes a bright, repeated sparkle. The stars are shining brightly.
records.logic: It modifies 光っている to show how the stars shine; it is vivid but not necessarily a single flash.
records.difference: きらきら is a glittering shine; ぴかぴか can describe a gleaming surface or something brand-new.
