records.nuance: 黄色 means yellow. Here it says the traffic light was yellow.
records.logic: 信号 is the traffic signal; でした places its color in the past.
records.difference: 黄色 is the color yellow; 青（あお） is blue/green, including the Japanese traffic-light term.

records.nuance: 横 means side or width across. 横の長さは1メートル says its side-to-side measurement is one meter.
records.logic: The object is understood from the preceding context; 横 does not itself specify which object is measured.
records.difference: 横 is side-to-side; 縦（たて） is lengthwise or vertical, depending on the object.
records.filipino: lapad; isang metro ang lapad nito

records.kanji_breakdown: 横 = horizontal / sideways; 書 = write
records.nuance: 横書き means horizontal writing, with lines running across the page. The book is printed horizontally.
records.logic: 横 describes the direction of writing; 書き names the writing style, not the book’s physical orientation.
records.difference: 横書き runs horizontally across the page; 縦書き（たてがき） runs vertically.
records.filipino: pahalang na pagkakasulat; pahalang ang pagkakasulat sa aklat na ito

records.kanji_breakdown: 判 = judge; 断 = decide (character cues)
records.nuance: 判断 means judgment or decision. The sentence says his judgment is correct.
records.logic: 正しい evaluates the judgment as right; the sentence does not describe a formal court ruling.
records.difference: 判断 is reaching a judgment; 決定（けってい） is a decision or determination.
records.filipino: pasya; tama ang naging pasya niya

records.kanji_breakdown: どうぞ = please; go ahead; this way
records.nuance: どうぞ is a polite expression used to invite or guide someone. こちらへどうぞ means “this way, please.”
records.logic: こちらへ gives the direction toward the speaker’s side; どうぞ makes the invitation courteous.
records.difference: どうぞ invites or permits someone; お願いします（おねがいします） is a direct “please” request.

records.nuance: 断る means to refuse or turn something down. The speaker rejected his marriage proposal.
records.logic: プロポーズを is the proposal being refused; 私は identifies the speaker as the one refusing.
records.difference: 断る is refusing an offer or request; 受け入れる（うけいれる） means accept.
records.filipino: tanggihan; tinanggihan ko ang alok niyang magpakasal

records.kanji_breakdown: 横 = across; 断 = cross; 歩 = walk; 道 = road / path
records.nuance: 横断歩道 means pedestrian crossing or crosswalk. The sentence says there is one over there.
records.logic: The word names the marked place for walking across a road; あります states that it is present.
records.difference: 横断歩道 is for pedestrians crossing a road; 歩道（ほどう） is a sidewalk.
records.filipino: tawiran ng mga naglalakad; may tawiran doon

records.kanji_breakdown: 大 = large; 幅 = width / extent
records.nuance: 大幅 means on a large scale or substantially. The plan was changed substantially.
records.logic: It modifies the degree of the change; Japanese does not state who made it, though the deck English supplies “we.”
records.difference: 大幅に means substantially; 少し（すこし） means a little.
records.filipino: nang malaki; binago nang malaki ang plano

records.nuance: 訪れる means to visit a person or place. The speaker visited Kyoto in summer.
records.logic: 京都を marks the place visited; 夏に sets when. The verb is somewhat more formal than 行く.
records.difference: 訪れる is visiting a place; 行く（いく） is the general verb “go.”
records.filipino: bisitahin; binisita ko ang Kyoto noong tag-init

records.nuance: ネックレス means necklace. The speaker gave one to their wife as a present.
records.logic: 妻に marks the recipient; プレゼントしました describes giving it as a gift.
records.difference: ネックレス is worn around the neck; イヤリング are earrings.
records.filipino: kuwintas; ibinigay ko sa asawa ko ang kuwintas bilang regalo

records.nuance: 訪ねる means to visit a person or place. He visited his friend in New York; this is 訪ねる, not the homophone 尋ねる “ask/inquire.”
records.logic: ニューヨークの友達 is the friend he visited in New York; the verb describes going to see someone.
records.difference: 訪ねる means go to see a person or place; 尋ねる can mean ask or search for information.
records.filipino: binisita niya ang kaibigan niya sa New York

records.kanji_breakdown: 冷 = cool; 房 = room / compartment (character cues)
records.nuance: 冷房 means air conditioning for cooling. 冷房を入れてください asks someone to turn on the air conditioner.
records.logic: を marks the cooling system as what to switch on; 入れる is commonly used for turning it on.
records.difference: 冷房 cools a room; 暖房（だんぼう） heats it.

records.kanji_breakdown: 暖 = warm; 房 = room / compartment (character cues)
records.nuance: 暖房 means heating or a heating system. The sentence says heating is needed in winter.
records.logic: 冬は gives the season; 必要です says heating is necessary.
records.difference: 暖房 provides heat to a room; 冷房（れいぼう） cools it.
records.filipino: pagpapainit; kailangan ang pampainit sa taglamig

records.kanji_breakdown: 文 = writing; 房 = room; 具 = tool (character cues)
records.nuance: 文房具 means stationery or writing supplies. The speaker bought some new stationery.
records.logic: The established word covers tools used for writing or schoolwork; it does not mean furniture for a writing room.
records.difference: 文房具 includes pens and notebooks; 家具（かぐ） means furniture.
records.filipino: kagamitan sa pagsusulat; mga bagong gamit sa paaralan

records.nuance: パジャマ means pajamas. 着て is a casual instruction to put them on or wear them.
records.logic: この identifies these pajamas; the te-form functions as a request or direction in this context.
records.difference: パジャマ are sleepwear; 服（ふく） is clothing in general.

records.nuance: 諸国 means various countries. Here it refers to countries in Europe that he traveled through or visited.
records.logic: ヨーロッパ specifies the region; the word does not mean every country in Europe necessarily.
records.difference: 諸国 means multiple countries; 一国（いっこく） is one country.

records.nuance: 緑色 means green. It describes the color of the jacket he is wearing.
records.logic: の connects the color with ジャケット; 着ています describes what he has on.
records.difference: 緑色 is green; 青色（あおいろ） is blue.

records.kanji_breakdown: 貿 = trade; 易 = exchange (character cues only)
records.nuance: 貿易 means trade, especially trade between countries. The sentence says the father works in trade.
records.logic: の仕事 describes his line of work; the sentence does not say whether he imports or exports particular goods.
records.difference: 貿易 is trade between regions or countries; 商売（しょうばい） is business or commerce more broadly.

records.nuance: 輸入 means importing goods into a country. These clothes were imported from Italy.
records.logic: イタリアから marks the source country; 服 is the imported item.
records.difference: 輸入 brings goods into a country; 輸出（ゆしゅつ） sends goods out.
records.filipino: angkat; mga damit na inangkat mula sa Italy

records.nuance: ボールペン means ballpoint pen. The sentence politely asks someone to write their name with one.
records.logic: で marks the pen as the writing instrument; 名前を書いてください is the request.
records.difference: ボールペン uses a small rolling ball to dispense ink; 鉛筆（えんぴつ） is a pencil.

records.kanji_breakdown: 輸 = transport; 出 = go out
records.nuance: 輸出 means exporting goods to another country. The sentence says his company exports cars.
records.logic: 車を marks the goods exported; しています describes the company’s ongoing business activity.
records.difference: 輸出 sends goods out of a country; 輸入（ゆにゅう） brings goods in.
records.filipino: export; ini-export ng kumpanya niya ang mga kotse

records.kanji_breakdown: 指 = finger; 輪 = ring / circle
records.nuance: 指輪 means ring worn on a finger. The speaker gave one to her as a gift; the sentence does not say what kind of ring or their relationship.
records.logic: 彼女に is the recipient and 指輪を is the gift; 彼女 can mean “her” or “girlfriend” depending on context.
records.difference: 指輪 is a finger ring; 腕輪（うでわ） is a bracelet.
records.filipino: singsing; ibinigay ko sa kaniya ang singsing bilang regalo

records.nuance: 往復 means going and returning, or a round trip. With 切符, 往復切符 is a round-trip ticket; the speaker asks for one.
records.logic: The compound describes both directions of a journey; 切符 names the ticket.
records.difference: 往復 is a round trip; 片道（かたみち） is one way.
records.filipino: papunta at pabalik; tiket na balikan

records.kanji_breakdown: 復 = repeat / return; 習 = learn / practice
records.nuance: 復習 means reviewing or studying material again. The question asks whether the listener reviewed yesterday’s lesson.
records.logic: 昨日の identifies the material reviewed; しましたか asks whether the review was done.
records.difference: 復習 is review of previously studied material; 予習（よしゅう） is preparation before a lesson.
records.filipino: pag-uulit-aral; nirepaso mo ba ang aralin kahapon?

records.nuance: すいか means watermelon. The sentence says watermelon is delicious in summer.
records.logic: 夏は sets the seasonal topic; 美味しい describes its taste.
records.difference: すいか is watermelon; メロン is melon.
records.filipino: pakwan; masarap ang pakwan tuwing tag-init

records.kanji_breakdown: 繰 = spin / repeat; 返 = return
records.nuance: 繰り返す means to repeat. She repeated the same mistake.
records.logic: 同じ間違いを is the thing repeated; the verb is transitive here.
records.difference: 繰り返す means repeat something; 繰り返し is the noun/adverbial form “repetition.”
records.filipino: ulitin; inulit niya ang parehong pagkakamali

records.nuance: 留学 means going to another place, commonly another country, to study for a period of time. Study is the purpose of the stay, unlike travel alone; the destination and duration come from context.
records.logic: アメリカに marks the destination; 1年間 gives the duration.
records.difference: 留学 is studying in another country; 旅行（りょこう） is travel and does not necessarily involve study.
records.filipino: mag-aral sa ibang bansa; nag-aral sa US sa loob ng isang taon

records.kanji_breakdown: 停 = stop; 留 = stay; 所 = place
records.nuance: 停留所 means a stop or stopping place. The sentence specifies a bus stop where the speaker waited ten minutes.
records.logic: で marks the place of waiting; バスの identifies which kind of stop.
records.difference: 停留所 is a vehicle stop; 駅（えき） is a train station.
records.filipino: hintuan; naghintay ako nang sampung minuto sa hintuan ng bus

records.kanji_breakdown: 書 = write; 留 = keep / retain
records.nuance: 書留 means registered mail, a postal service that records handling and delivery. The speaker wants to send this by registered mail.
records.logic: で marks the mailing method; 送りたい expresses the speaker’s wish to send it.
records.difference: 書留 is registered post; 普通郵便（ふつうゆうびん） is ordinary mail.
records.filipino: registered mail; nais kong ipadala ito sa pamamagitan ng rehistradong koreo

records.nuance: そちら is a polite distal expression for “there” or the addressee’s side/place. 夕方そちらに着きます says the speaker will arrive there in the evening.
records.logic: に marks the destination; the Japanese omits the subject, while the deck English supplies “I.”
records.difference: そちら is polite; そこ is the less formal “there.”
records.filipino: doon sa inyo; darating ako diyan pagsapit ng gabi

records.nuance: 守る means to protect or keep. 約束を守る人 is a person who keeps promises.
records.logic: 約束を selects the “keep/fulfill” sense rather than physical protection; 人 describes that person.
records.difference: 約束を守る means keep a promise; 約束を破る（やぶる） means break one.

records.kanji_breakdown: 留 = stay; 守 = guard (character cues)
records.nuance: 留守 means being away from home or not at home. The sentence says the father is currently out; it does not mean the house is necessarily unattended.
records.logic: 父は is the topic, 今 sets the present time, and 留守です states he is away.
records.difference: 留守 is absence from home; 在宅（ざいたく） means being at home.
records.filipino: wala sa bahay; wala ngayon ang tatay ko

records.nuance: 住宅 means housing or a residence. 住宅地 is a residential area, described here as quiet.
records.logic: 地 adds “area”; 静かな describes the neighborhood, not necessarily one particular house.
records.difference: 住宅 refers to homes or housing; 家（いえ） is a house/home.

records.nuance: 自宅 means one’s own home. 自宅に電話をください asks someone to call the speaker at home; the English shortens this to “call home.”
records.logic: The point of reference is the speaker’s own home; the destination of the call is not a place the caller should travel to.
records.difference: 自宅 is one’s own home; お宅（おたく） is a polite way to refer to another person’s home.
records.filipino: sariling bahay; pakitawagan ako sa bahay

records.nuance: お宅 is a polite way to refer to someone else’s home. The question asks where the teacher’s home is.
records.logic: 先生のお宅 shows respect toward the teacher; どちら politely asks which place.
records.difference: お宅 is respectful for another person’s home; 自宅（じたく） means one’s own home.
records.filipino: tahanan ng guro; saan po ang bahay ng guro?

records.kanji_breakdown: 早 = early; 起 = get up
records.nuance: 早起き means getting up early or being an early riser. The sentence describes the grandfather as someone who gets up early.
records.logic: It names the habit or tendency to rise early; it does not say what time he wakes.
records.difference: 早起き means rising early; 夜更かし（よふかし） means staying up late.
records.filipino: maagang gumising; maagang gumigising ang lolo ko

records.kanji_breakdown: 昼 = noon / daytime; 寝 = sleep
records.nuance: 昼寝 means a daytime nap, usually around midday. The sentence says the child naps every day.
records.logic: 毎日 marks the habit’s frequency; 昼寝 is a short daytime sleep, not sleeping through the night.
records.difference: 昼寝 is a daytime nap; 睡眠（すいみん） is sleep more generally.
records.filipino: idlip sa tanghali; araw-araw umiidlip sa tanghali ang anak ko

records.nuance: 静か means quiet or peaceful. The speaker wants to go somewhere quiet during this year’s summer vacation.
records.logic: な links the adjective to 所; this describes the place’s atmosphere, not necessarily that it is remote.
records.difference: 静か describes low noise or calm; 寂しい（さびしい） means lonely or desolate.
records.filipino: tahimik; gusto kong pumunta sa tahimik na lugar ngayong bakasyon sa tag-init

records.nuance: どっち is a casual way to ask “which one?” Here the speaker asks which color the listener likes.
records.logic: の connects it with 色; the question treats the colors as choices, commonly two alternatives.
records.difference: どっち is casual; どちら is the more polite equivalent.
records.filipino: alin; alin sa mga kulay ang gusto mo?

records.nuance: 暇 means having free time or being available. 明日は暇ですか asks whether the person is free tomorrow.
records.logic: Tomorrow is the time being asked about; the question is about availability, not boredom.
records.difference: 暇 means free time or availability; 忙しい（いそがしい） means busy.
records.filipino: may libreng oras; libre ka ba bukas?

records.kanji_breakdown: 趣 = interest / inclination; 味 = taste (character cues only)
records.nuance: 趣味 means a hobby or personal interest. The speaker lists movies and tennis as hobbies.
records.logic: It refers to activities someone enjoys; do not interpret it literally as “taste” or limit it to one activity.
records.difference: 趣味 is a personal hobby or interest; 仕事（しごと） is work.
records.filipino: libangan; mga hilig ko ang pelikula at tennis

records.kanji_breakdown: 両 = both; 方 = side / direction
records.nuance: 両方 means both. The speaker politely asks for both the chocolate and the cake.
records.logic: 両方 gathers the two named items together; ください makes it a request.
records.difference: 両方 means both items; 片方（かたほう） means one of the two.
records.filipino: kukunin ko po ang pareho: tsokolate at keyk

records.kanji_breakdown: 両 = two / both; 替 = exchange (character cues)
records.nuance: 両替 means exchanging one kind or denomination of money for another. The speaker asks to have 10,000 yen changed; no target currency or denominations are specified.
records.logic: を marks the money to be exchanged; the sentence leaves what it will be exchanged into unstated.
records.difference: 両替 exchanges currency or denominations; 支払う（しはらう） means pay.
records.filipino: pagpapalit ng pera; Pakipalitan po ang 10,000 yen.

records.kanji_breakdown: バスケットボール = basketball
records.nuance: バスケットボール means basketball. The speaker’s older sister is a basketball player.
records.logic: の connects the sport with 選手; the sentence does not say what position she plays.
records.difference: バスケットボール is basketball; バレーボール is volleyball.
records.filipino: basketball; manlalaro ng basketball ang ate ko

records.nuance: 両親 means both parents. The sentence says the speaker’s parents live in Osaka.
records.logic: The word refers to the two parents together; it does not mean relatives more broadly.
records.difference: 両親 is both parents; 祖父母（そふぼ） means grandparents.
records.filipino: mga magulang; nakatira sa Osaka ang mga magulang ko

records.kanji_breakdown: 片 = one side; 道 = way / route
records.nuance: 片道 means one way in a journey. The speaker bought a one-way ticket to Tokyo.
records.logic: 東京まで gives the destination; 片道 specifies that the ticket covers only the outward trip.
records.difference: 片道 is one way; 往復（おうふく） is round trip.
records.filipino: one-way; bumili ako ng one-way ticket papuntang Tokyo

records.nuance: 内側 means the inner side or inside of a boundary. The instruction is to step back to the inside of the white line.
records.logic: 白線の sets the line as the boundary; the exact safe side depends on where the line is placed.
records.difference: 内側 is the inside of a boundary; 外側（そとがわ） is the outside.
records.filipino: panloob na bahagi; umatras po kayo sa loob ng puting guhit

records.kanji_breakdown: 向こう = other side / over there; 側 = side
records.nuance: 向こう側 means the far or other side. The sentence says the speaker’s house is across the river.
records.logic: 川の identifies the river as the boundary; the house is on the far side from the speaker’s viewpoint.
records.difference: 向こう側 is the side beyond a divider; こちら側（こちらがわ） is this side.
records.filipino: kabilang panig; nasa kabilang pampang ng ilog ang bahay ko

records.nuance: サンドイッチ means sandwich. The Japanese says today’s lunch is sandwich; it does not mark the number, while the deck English uses plural “sandwiches.”
records.logic: 今日のお昼は sets today’s lunch as the topic; the sentence identifies what it is.
records.difference: サンドイッチ is a sandwich; ハンバーガー is a hamburger.
records.filipino: sandwich; sandwich ang tanghalian namin ngayon

records.nuance: 外側 means the outside or outer side. The speaker asks someone not to walk beyond the white line.
records.logic: 白線の外側 is the side outside the marked boundary; ないでください makes it a polite prohibition.
records.difference: 外側 is outside a boundary; 内側（うちがわ） is inside.
records.filipino: panlabas na bahagi; huwag kayong maglakad sa labas ng puting guhit

records.nuance: 左側 means the left side. The instruction is to look at the left side of the screen.
records.logic: 画面の identifies which object has the left side; を見てください requests attention to it.
records.difference: 左側 is the left side; 右側（みぎがわ） is the right side.
records.filipino: kaliwang bahagi; pakitingnan ang kaliwang bahagi ng screen

records.nuance: 右側 means the right side. She always walks on the speaker’s right.
records.logic: 私の sets the speaker’s viewpoint; the sentence does not say whether she is in front or behind.
records.difference: 右側 is the right side; 左側（ひだりがわ） is the left side.
records.filipino: kanang bahagi; lagi siyang naglalakad sa kanan ko

records.nuance: 裏 means the back or reverse side. 会社の裏に公園があります says there is a park behind the company premises.
records.logic: 裏 is the side behind or opposite the front; here it is the area at the back of the company location.
records.difference: 裏 is the back side; 前（まえ） is the front.
records.filipino: likuran; may parke sa likod ng opisina

records.nuance: にこにこ describes smiling happily or pleasantly. The sentence says she is always smiling.
records.logic: It describes the expression on her face; it does not by itself prove she feels happy all the time.
records.difference: にこにこ is a smiling expression; 泣く（なく） means cry.

records.kanji_breakdown: 裏 = reverse side; 返 = turn back / over
records.nuance: 裏返す means to turn something over to its reverse side. He turned the paper over.
records.logic: 紙を marks the object deliberately flipped; the sentence does not say he turned it inside out.
records.difference: 裏返す is transitive (“turn something over”); 裏返る（うらがえる） means turn over by itself or be reversed.

records.kanji_breakdown: 週 = week; 刊 = publish / issue; 誌 = magazine
records.nuance: 週刊誌 means weekly magazine. The sentence says that magazine is full of gossip.
records.logic: ばかり emphasizes that it contains little besides gossip; this may be an emphatic criticism.
records.difference: 週刊誌 is issued weekly; 月刊誌（げっかんし） is issued monthly.
records.filipino: lingguhang magasin; puro tsismis ang laman ng magasin na iyon

records.kanji_breakdown: 朝 = morning; 刊 = published edition
records.nuance: 朝刊 means morning newspaper edition. The sentence says there was an interesting article in today’s morning paper.
records.logic: 今日の identifies the edition; 面白い can mean interesting or amusing, and the sentence does not force only the humorous sense.
records.difference: 朝刊 is a morning edition; 夕刊（ゆうかん） is an evening edition.
records.filipino: edisyon sa umaga; may kawili-wiling artikulo sa diyaryo ngayong umaga

records.kanji_breakdown: 夕 = evening; 刊 = published edition
records.nuance: 夕刊 means evening newspaper edition. The speaker saw that news in the evening edition.
records.logic: で marks the edition as the source; 見ました says saw/read, without specifying exactly how the story was consumed.
records.difference: 夕刊 is an evening edition; 朝刊（ちょうかん） is a morning edition.
records.filipino: edisyon sa gabi; nakita ko ang balitang iyon sa diyaryong panggabi

records.nuance: ウール means wool. The sentence says this wool sweater is warm.
records.logic: ウールの identifies the sweater’s material; 暖かい describes its warmth.
records.difference: ウール is wool; 綿（めん） is cotton.
records.filipino: lana; mainit ang sweater na yari sa lana

records.nuance: 詳しい means detailed or knowledgeable. In もっと詳しく説明してください, it becomes 詳しく and asks for a more detailed explanation.
records.logic: もっと increases the requested degree; 詳しく modifies 説明してください, “please explain.”
records.difference: 詳しい can describe detailed information or someone knowledgeable; 細かい（こまかい） means fine-grained or small in detail.
records.filipino: detalyado; ipaliwanag po nang mas detalyado

records.nuance: 細かい describes small or fine parts, detailed information, or close attention to minor distinctions. It can describe careful precision positively or excessive attention to details negatively, depending on context. In 細かいことにうるさい, the criticism is expressed by the complete phrase.
records.logic: 細かい centers on small, fine-grained parts or distinctions. Applied to こと, it points to minor details; with うるさい, it describes being fussy about them.
records.meaning: fine; small; detailed; meticulous; sometimes nitpicky, depending on what is described
records.difference: 細かい describes fineness or attention to detail. 細かいことにうるさい specifically describes being fussy about minor details. The negative judgment comes from the complete expression.
records.filipino: maselan sa maliliit na detalye; mapili sa mga detalye

records.nuance: 細か（こまか） is the na-adjective form meaning fine or detailed. 細かな問題 describes an issue in fine detail or involving small particulars; the deck English “complex issue” is an interpretation, since 細か itself does not necessarily mean difficult or complex.
records.logic: 細か focuses on small particulars. In this sentence it can describe a fine-grained or detailed issue; any sense of complexity comes from context or the deck translation, not automatically from the word itself.
records.difference: 細かな問題 and 細かい問題 have similar meanings; 細かな uses the na-adjective form before a noun.
records.filipino: detalyadong usapin; usaping may maraming maliliit na detalye

records.nuance: 積もる（つもる） describes snow accumulating and lying on a surface. 雪が積もっています describes the resulting state: snow has accumulated/is lying on the ground.
records.logic: Snow builds up layer by layer; the verb presents that accumulation as happening, without naming an agent.
records.difference: 積もる is intransitive: snow accumulates. 積む is transitive: someone piles or loads something.
records.filipino: naipon/nabunton ang niyebe; natabunan ng niyebe

records.nuance: コーラ is the loanword for cola. The sentence says the speaker’s older brother likes cola; it does not specify a particular brand.
records.logic: This is a borrowed beverage name written in katakana, so no kanji breakdown applies.
records.difference: コーラ is cola; ソーダ often means soda water or another carbonated drink in Japanese.

records.nuance: With the confirmed reading やく, 訳 means a translation or rendering. Here it is the translation of that sentence. The same kanji read わけ has separate senses such as reason or meaning, which do not fit this note.
records.logic: The noun names the rendered wording in another language; no extra agent or language is specified.
records.difference: 訳 can refer to the translation itself; 翻訳 often names the act or work of translating more explicitly.
records.filipino: salin; ang salin ng pangungusap na iyon

records.nuance: 訳す（やくす） means to translate or render something. In この文を訳してください, the sentence is the object to be translated.
records.logic: The verb acts on a source text and expresses it in another language; the target language is left unstated here.
records.difference: 訳す and 翻訳する both mean “translate”; 翻訳する is a more explicit/formal compound, while 訳す is compact and common.
records.filipino: isalin; pakisalin ang pangungusap na ito

records.nuance: 検討（けんとう） means examining an issue and thinking it through. The request asks for consideration of the problem by the end of today, not necessarily a final decision.
records.logic: The compound suggests careful examination and deliberation; in this sentence the focus is evaluating the problem.
records.difference: 検討 weighs and evaluates an issue; 調査 focuses more on investigating or collecting facts.
records.filipino: pagsusuri at pag-iisipan; pag-aralan at timbangin ang usapin

records.nuance: 塗る（ぬる） means applying paint or another substance across a surface. Here someone is painting the wall; the progressive form 塗っています describes an action in progress.
records.logic: Paint is spread over the wall’s surface to cover it; the verb takes the surface/object marked by を.
records.difference: 塗る coats a surface with a substance; 貼る attaches a separate flat item, such as a sticker.
records.filipino: pinturahan ang dingding; pahiran ng pintura

records.kanji_breakdown: トイレットペーパー = toilet paper
records.nuance: トイレットペーパー is toilet tissue/paper used in the bathroom. 交換しました says it was replaced; the subject is omitted.
records.logic: This is a katakana loanword, so no kanji breakdown applies.
records.difference: トイレットペーパー is specifically bathroom tissue; ティッシュ often refers to facial tissue.

records.nuance: 付く（つく） means to become attached or remain on something. Here the sentence says mud is on the shoes; the subject “I” in the English is supplied by context.
records.logic: The mud has adhered to the shoes, so 付く presents the resulting state without saying who caused it.
records.meaning: stick to; be attached; get on
records.difference: 付く is intransitive (“mud sticks/is on”); 付ける is transitive (“someone attaches/adds”).
records.filipino: may putik sa sapatos ko; dumikit ang putik sa sapatos

records.nuance: 付ける（つける） means to attach or add something. おまけを付けました says a free bonus item was included/added.
records.logic: The subject adds an extra item to something; を marks おまけ as what is added.
records.difference: 付ける is transitive: someone adds something. 付く is intransitive: something becomes attached or included.
records.filipino: nagdagdag ng libreng bonus na item; may kasamang libreng dagdag

records.nuance: 受け付ける（うけつける） means to accept and process submissions or items. Here mail is accepted until five o’clock.
records.logic: The organization receives mail as submissions/items and handles it; the sentence gives the closing time for acceptance.
records.difference: 受け付ける means accept/process an item or request; 受け取る focuses on receiving or taking possession of it.
records.filipino: tumatanggap ng mga liham at iba pang koreo hanggang alas singko

records.kanji_breakdown: 片 = one side; 付 = attach/settle
records.nuance: 片付ける（かたづける） means to tidy, put away, or clean up. 早く and なさい make this a firm instruction to hurry and clean the room.
records.logic: The transitive verb describes someone putting scattered things in order; the room is what is being tidied.
records.meaning: to tidy; put away; clean up
records.difference: 片付ける is transitive (“tidy something”); 片付く describes something becoming tidy or getting settled.
records.filipino: ligpitin at ayusin ang kuwarto mo

records.nuance: どなた is a respectful way to ask who someone is. 失礼ですが softens the question; the deck English “Who are you?” sounds more direct than the Japanese phrasing.
records.logic: The word asks for a person’s identity while using respectful language; the sentence does not name the person.
records.difference: どなた is respectful; 誰（だれ） is the plain, less formal equivalent.

records.nuance: 受付（うけつけ） means reception/registration or the desk where it is handled. In 受付は9時からです, the reception or registration service begins at nine.
records.logic: The noun refers to the reception function or place where requests/visitors are received; the sentence gives its start time.
records.difference: 受付 is a noun for the reception/registration function or desk; 受け付ける is the verb “to accept/process.”
records.filipino: mula alas nuwebe ang serbisyo sa resepsyon; magsisimula ang pagtanggap sa tanggapan sa alas nuwebe

records.nuance: 近付く（ちかづく） means to move nearer or approach. 近付いてきました presents a woman coming closer toward the speaker or scene’s reference point.
records.logic: The subject’s distance from the reference point decreases; くる adds the viewpoint of movement toward that point.
records.difference: 近付く is intransitive (“approach”); 近付ける is transitive (“bring something closer”).
records.filipino: lumapit sa akin ang isang babae

records.kanji_breakdown: 片 = one side; 付 = settle
records.nuance: 片付く（かたづく） means to get tidied, dealt with, or completed. Here a considerable amount of work has been taken care of; Japanese does not state who completed it.
records.logic: The work reaches a more settled/done state. This is intransitive, so the sentence foregrounds the result rather than an actor.
records.meaning: be tidied; be settled; get taken care of
records.difference: 片付く describes work getting done; 片付ける means someone tidies or finishes something.
records.filipino: malaking bahagi ng trabaho ang natapos na; marami nang naasikaso sa trabaho

records.nuance: 気を付ける（きをつける） means to be careful or take care. 体に気を付けてください is a polite wish to take care of one’s health.
records.logic: It asks someone to direct attention toward their condition and act carefully; 体 identifies health/body as the concern.
records.difference: 気を付ける is a broad “take care/be careful”; 注意する often points more directly to paying attention to a specific matter.
records.filipino: mag-ingat po kayo at alagaan ang inyong kalusugan

records.nuance: ハイキング is an outdoor recreational walk, often in the countryside or hills. The sentence says the speaker went hiking with a friend yesterday.
records.logic: This is a katakana loanword; the sentence supplies a past outing and companion, not a technical climb.
records.difference: ハイキング is generally a recreational walk; 登山（とざん） specifically means mountain climbing/ascent.
records.filipino: pag-hike; paglalakad sa kalikasan kasama ang kaibigan kahapon

records.nuance: 貼る（はる） means to stick or paste a flat item onto a surface. Here a sticker was put on the desk; the past form is 貼った.
records.logic: The sticker adheres to the desk’s surface; the verb is transitive and the attached item is marked by を.
records.difference: 貼る attaches a separate item such as a sticker; 塗る spreads paint or another substance over a surface.

records.kanji_breakdown: 記 = record; 念 = remember; 日 = day
records.nuance: 記念日（きねんび） is a day marking a memorable event. Here it is the speaker’s parents’ wedding anniversary.
records.logic: The characters provide cues for remembering/marking a day; this is a learning aid, not a historical etymology.
records.difference: 記念日 is the date/day itself; 記念 can mean commemoration or remembrance more generally.
records.filipino: anibersaryo; anibersaryo ng kasal ng mga magulang ko

records.nuance: 残念（ざんねん） describes disappointment or regret when an outcome falls short. The game result was disappointing; the sentence does not identify a particular person’s feelings.
records.logic: The word conveys an unsatisfied or regretful feeling left by the outcome; the character cues are mnemonic, not a literal derivation.
records.difference: 残念 is a broad reaction to an unsatisfying outcome; 悔しい more strongly conveys personal frustration or chagrin.
records.filipino: nakapanghihinayang; nakadidismaya ang naging resulta ng laro

records.nuance: 例えば（たとえば） introduces a concrete example of a broader point. Here the software is one example of a way to study Japanese.
records.logic: It signals that the following case illustrates the preceding/general statement; no literal kanji etymology is needed.
records.difference: No useful distinction is needed here; 例えば simply introduces an example.
records.filipino: halimbawa, maaaring mag-aral ng Japanese gamit ang software na ito

records.nuance: ハム is ham, a processed meat product. In ハムサンド the word identifies the sandwich filling; the Japanese sentence is a request for a ham sandwich.
records.logic: This is a katakana loanword, so no kanji breakdown applies.
records.difference: Ham is distinct from ベーコン (bacon), though both are processed meat; the sentence only specifies ham.
records.filipino: ham; sandwich na may palamang ham

records.nuance: 例文（れいぶん） means an example sentence. The request is to make three such sentences.
records.logic: 例 marks an illustrative example and 文 refers to a sentence/text; together they name a sentence used as a model.
records.difference: 例 is any example or case; 例文 is specifically a sentence offered as an example.
records.filipino: pangungusap na halimbawa; gumawa ng tatlong pangungusap na halimbawa

records.nuance: 例（れい） means an example or case. 一つ例をあげてください asks someone to give one example.
records.logic: 例 names a case offered to illustrate or support a point; 一つ counts one example.
records.difference: 例 is a general example/case; 例文（れいぶん） is specifically an example sentence.
records.filipino: magbigay po kayo ng isang halimbawa

records.nuance: 余る（あまる） means there is more than needed, leaving a surplus. Here a lot of the dinner food was left over after the meal.
records.logic: 余る focuses on an amount exceeding what was used or needed; it does not say why the food was not eaten.
records.meaning: be left over; remain in excess
records.difference: 余る suggests excess beyond what was needed; 残る simply means something remains, without that surplus implication.
records.filipino: maraming pagkaing natira mula sa hapunan

records.nuance: 除く（のぞく） means to exclude or leave out. 部長を除く全員 says everyone except the department manager; 部長 is a role such as department head, not necessarily a company director.
records.logic: The department manager is removed from the group being described; the other employees worked on Saturday too.
records.difference: 除く is the verb “exclude”; 以外 means “other than/except” as a noun-like expression.
records.filipino: maliban sa hepe ng departamento, nagtrabaho rin ang lahat noong Sabado

records.nuance: ボーイフレンド is a boyfriend/romantic male partner. ハンサムな方でした says he was handsome or “on the handsome side”; the past tense does not by itself mean he is an ex-boyfriend.
records.logic: The loanword names the relationship. 方 here softens the evaluation to “rather/on the … side”; the sentence gives no relationship timeline beyond past tense.
records.difference: 彼氏（かれし） is a common Japanese alternative for “boyfriend”; ボーイフレンド is the direct loanword.
records.filipino: noong panahong iyon, gwapo ang boyfriend ko

records.nuance: 削る（けずる） can mean to cut away a part or reduce an amount. He reduced his working hours for his family’s sake; the sentence does not mean he physically shaved anything.
records.logic: The amount of work time is cut back, with his family given as the reason; the verb takes 時間 as its object.
records.meaning: to reduce; cut down; shave off
records.difference: 削る suggests cutting away part of an amount; 減らす more generally means to decrease something.
records.filipino: binawasan niya ang oras niya sa trabaho para sa pamilya niya

records.nuance: 遅刻（ちこく） means being late for a set time or appointment. 遅刻しないでください is a polite request not to arrive late.
records.logic: The issue is arriving after the required time, not moving slowly in general.
records.difference: 遅刻 means lateness for a scheduled time; 遅れる can describe any delay or falling behind.
records.filipino: huwag po kayong mahuli sa takdang oras

records.nuance: 緩い（ゆるい） means loose when describing these trousers: they do not fit snugly. The sentence does not say they are too long or too large in every dimension.
records.logic: The fit leaves extra room rather than holding tightly to the body.
records.difference: 緩い describes a loose fit; 大きい means large in size and does not necessarily mean loose-fitting.

records.nuance: 苦しい（くるしい） can describe physical discomfort as well as hardship. After eating too much, the speaker’s stomach feels uncomfortably full/tight; the deck English “hurts” is a rough translation, not necessarily sharp pain.
records.logic: The sentence connects overeating with an uncomfortable, pressured feeling in the abdomen. 苦しい here is broader than a specific painful spot.
records.difference: 苦しい describes general discomfort or distress; 痛い（いたい） more directly describes pain in a particular place.
records.filipino: sumisikip at hindi komportable ang tiyan ko dahil naparami ang kain ko

records.nuance: アイロン is a household iron; アイロンをかける means to iron clothing. The sentence says she ironed the shirt, not that she placed an iron on it.
records.logic: The word is in katakana and has no kanji breakdown. In this collocation, the iron is used to press the shirt smooth.
records.difference: アイロンをかける is ironing; シャツを洗う means washing a shirt.

records.nuance: 苦い（にがい） means bitter-tasting. The speaker likes coffee with a bitter taste; no figurative “painful experience” sense is intended.
records.logic: The sentence applies the taste adjective to coffee, so it describes flavor rather than emotional bitterness.
records.difference: 苦い describes a bitter taste; 酸っぱい（すっぱい） means sour.
records.filipino: mahilig ako sa mapait na kape

records.nuance: 苦手（にがて） means something one is not good at or feels uncomfortable doing. Here the speaker is not good at cooking; it does not necessarily mean they dislike cooking.
records.logic: The word identifies a weak or difficult area for the person. Its meaning is lexical, not literally “bitter hand.”
records.meaning: not good at; weak at; uncomfortable with
records.difference: 苦手 can include lack of confidence or ability; 下手（へた） states poor skill more directly.

records.nuance: 困る（こまる） means to be troubled or not know how to handle a situation. Losing the cell phone leaves the speaker in difficulty; 困っています describes the current predicament.
records.logic: The problem is the situation caused by losing the phone, rather than a physical feeling. The subject “I” is supplied by context and the English.
records.meaning: be troubled; be in a jam; have difficulty
records.difference: 困る describes being in a troublesome situation; 迷う emphasizes being unsure which choice or direction to take.
records.filipino: naproblema ako nang mawala ang cellphone ko

records.nuance: 貧乏（びんぼう） means having little money or resources and living in hardship. The sentence places that state in the past; Japanese だった alone does not establish that he is no longer poor.
records.logic: It describes limited means in the relevant past period, without giving a cause or saying what his present finances are.
records.difference: 貧乏 describes economic hardship; 貧しい（まずしい） can also describe something lacking or meager beyond a person’s finances.
records.filipino: mahirap siya noon; hindi sinasabi ng pangungusap kung nagbago na ang kalagayan niya

records.kanji_breakdown: カレーライス = curry and rice
records.nuance: カレーライス is the Japanese dish of curry served with rice. The sentence says children like curry rice; it does not specify a particular recipe or type of curry.
records.logic: This is a conventional katakana compound, so no kanji breakdown applies.
records.meaning: curry and rice; Japanese curry rice
records.difference: カレーライス explicitly names the curry-and-rice dish; カレー alone may refer to curry more broadly or the curry portion.
records.filipino: gusto ng mga bata ang kanin na may curry

records.kanji_breakdown: 不 = not; 幸 = good fortune/happiness
records.nuance: 不幸（ふこう） means misfortune or unhappiness. Here a misfortune occurred in her family; the sentence does not say what happened or imply a death.
records.logic: The compound names an unfortunate state or event. The context reports that something unfortunate happened without identifying the event.
records.difference: 不幸 can describe a misfortune/event or an unhappy state; 不運（ふうん） more specifically emphasizes bad luck.
records.filipino: may kasawiang-palad na nangyari sa pamilya niya

records.nuance: 幸せ（しあわせ） means happiness or being happy. The speaker says having good friends makes them happy.
records.logic: The sentence links the speaker’s happiness to having good friends; いて is the existence/having construction, not a literal possession.
records.difference: 幸せ describes a state of happiness; 楽しい（たのしい） means enjoyable or fun, often about an experience/activity.
records.filipino: masaya ako dahil may mabubuti akong kaibigan

records.nuance: 塩（しお） is salt. もうちょっと adds the nuance “a little more,” and 入れて asks someone to put it in.
records.logic: Salt is the ingredient to be added; the request leaves the dish or container understood from context.
records.difference: 塩 is the ingredient; 塩分（えんぶん） refers to salt content in food or a substance.

records.kanji_breakdown: 塩 = salt; 辛 = spicy; harsh
records.nuance: 塩辛い（しおからい） means strongly salty. 海の水は塩辛い describes seawater’s salty taste; it does not mean spicy-hot.
records.logic: This established adjective means strongly salty; do not read 辛 here as saying the sea water is spicy. The sentence selects the salt-taste sense.
records.difference: 塩辛い and しょっぱい both mean salty; しょっぱい is more conversational.

records.kanji_breakdown: キャッシュカード = bank cash/ATM card
records.nuance: キャッシュカード is a bank card used at an ATM to access an account, including withdrawing cash. It is not automatically a credit card or a payment card for purchases.
records.logic: The sentence says cash was withdrawn using the card; it does not specify which bank or amount.
records.difference: A Japanese キャッシュカード primarily accesses a bank account at ATMs; a credit card borrows against a credit line and is a different product.
records.filipino: nag-withdraw ako ng pera gamit ang ATM card ko

records.nuance: 砂糖（さとう） is the ordinary word for sugar. Here the question asks whether the listener adds sugar to coffee, typically about their usual preference.
records.logic: Learn this as the established whole-word reading and meaning; the characters are cues and should not be read as a literal “sand sugar” explanation.
records.difference: 砂糖 is sugar; 甘味料（かんみりょう） is the broader category of sweeteners, including non-sugar products.
records.filipino: naglalagay ka ba ng asukal sa kape?

records.nuance: 規模（きぼ） is the overall scale or size of something. この動物園は日本一の規模です says this zoo is Japan’s largest in scale; the sentence does not specify whether that means land area, number of animals, or another measure.
records.logic: 規模 treats the zoo as an undertaking/organization with an overall scale. The English “largest zoo” is a concise rendering that leaves the measurement unspecified too.
records.difference: 規模 refers to overall scale or scope; 大きさ（おおきさ） is general size and need not imply an organized operation or scope.
records.filipino: ito ang zoo na pinakamalaki ang kabuuang saklaw sa Japan

records.nuance: 農業（のうぎょう） is agriculture, including growing crops and raising livestock. The sentence says the speaker is studying agriculture, not necessarily working as a farmer.
records.logic: The compound names the agricultural field/industry; 勉強しています expresses study in progress or an ongoing course of study.
records.difference: 農業 is the practical field/industry; 農学（のうがく） is the academic discipline that studies agriculture.

records.nuance: 濃い（こい） can describe a strong or intense taste. 濃い味 means strongly flavored or heavily seasoned; it does not tell us whether the flavor is salty, rich, or another type.
records.logic: The adjective describes flavor intensity/concentration, not simply whether the speaker likes food.
records.difference: 濃い味 describes a concentrated/intense flavor; 強い味 is a broader phrase for a strong flavor or taste.
records.filipino: gusto ko ng pagkaing matapang ang timpla

records.nuance: イヤリング means an earring/ear ornament. In current Japanese, it often contrasts with ピアス for non-pierced vs. pierced styles, though the broader word “earring” can cover either; the sentence does not identify how these are fastened.
records.logic: This is a katakana loanword, so no kanji breakdown applies. している means she is wearing them.
records.difference: イヤリング often means clip-on/screw-back earrings in everyday Japanese contrast with pierced ピアス; actual usage is not an absolute rule.

records.nuance: 薄い（うすい） means physically thin here: the electronic dictionary has little thickness. It does not mean its screen or color is faint.
records.logic: The adjective describes thickness of the device as an object; とても intensifies it as “very.”
records.difference: 薄い means thin in thickness; 細い（ほそい） means narrow or slender in width/shape.

records.nuance: 厚い（あつい） describes the dictionary’s physical thickness in this sentence. The same adjective has other context-dependent senses, including deep or heavy, but it does not mean hot here.
records.logic: The sentence applies a thickness adjective directly to the dictionary; とても makes the degree strong.
records.difference: 薄い（うすい） means thin; 厚い means thick.

records.kanji_breakdown: 厚 = thick; さ = degree-forming suffix
records.nuance: 厚さ（あつさ） is the measurable thickness of the board. The suffix さ turns 厚い into a noun naming its quality or degree.
records.logic: 測った (measured) and 板 (board) show a physical dimension, not figurative depth.
records.difference: 厚い（あつい） describes something as thick; 厚さ names its thickness.

records.nuance: 迫る（せまる） means the deadline is drawing near, creating a sense of time pressure. It can also mean physically approaching or pressing someone, depending on context.
records.logic: The subject 締め切り (deadline) and progressive ています indicate that the due time is nearing. Here it is intransitive.
records.meaning: to draw near; to be approaching (a deadline)
records.difference: 迫る describes a deadline or event drawing near, often with urgency; 近づく（ちかづく） is a more general “come closer/approach.”

records.nuance: ガールフレンド means a female romantic partner. In 昔は彼女のことをガールフレンドと言っていました, the speaker says that people used to call a girlfriend a “girl friend”; the sentence does not establish that the word is obsolete today.
records.logic: 彼女のことを…と言う means to refer to a girlfriend as …; 昔は sets this as a past naming practice. The deck’s “garufurendo” is a romanization cue, not the Japanese word’s meaning.
records.difference: ガールフレンド is a loanword. 彼女 can mean “she” or “girlfriend”; context decides.

records.nuance: 伸びる（のびる） describes hair becoming longer. It is an intransitive change; だいぶ means considerably, and ね invites shared recognition.
records.logic: The hair is the subject of a change in length. The sentence says it has grown/lengthened, not that someone deliberately grew it.
records.difference: 伸びる is intransitive (“grow/lengthen”); 伸ばす（のばす） is transitive (“grow/let something grow/extend something”).
records.filipino: humaba; humaba na nang husto ang buhok mo

records.kanji_breakdown: 引 = pull; 越 = cross over
records.nuance: 引っ越す（ひっこす） means to move one’s residence. 来月 makes the move a future plan; the sentence does not say why the speaker is moving.
records.logic: The compound is conventionally used for changing residence; 大阪に marks the destination. Its meaning should be learned as a whole, not inferred as a literal sum of the characters.
records.difference: 引っ越す is the verb; 引っ越し（ひっこし） is the noun “a move/relocation.”

records.nuance: 越える（こえる） means to cross over the mountain in this sentence. It can also mean to go beyond a limit, but the mountain makes the physical crossing sense clear.
records.logic: The mountain is the obstacle or terrain crossed; 高い describes its height.
records.difference: 越える commonly describes crossing terrain or boundaries; 超える often emphasizes exceeding a numerical amount or limit, though usage overlaps.

records.kanji_breakdown: 引 = pull; 越 = cross over
records.nuance: 引っ越し（ひっこし） is a move or change of residence. 去年 places it in the past; the Japanese omits the subject, which the deck renders as “I.”
records.logic: 引っ越し is the noun for the conventional act of moving home; する makes it an action.
records.difference: 引っ越し is the noun; 引っ越す（ひっこす） is the verb “to move house.”

records.kanji_breakdown: カセットテープ = cassette tape
records.nuance: カセットテープ is magnetic recording tape housed in a cassette. 昔は…使っていました describes past habitual use; 昔 does not specify exactly how long ago.
records.logic: The word names the cassette medium as a whole; 使っていました is a past continuing/habitual use.
records.difference: カセットテープ names the medium; テープ alone can mean tape more broadly.

records.kanji_breakdown: 追 = follow; 越 = pass over
records.nuance: 追い越す（おいこす） means to pass a vehicle or person ahead and move in front. Here the truck passes “us.”
records.logic: The truck is the subject, and 私たちを marks those overtaken, so the verb is transitive in this sentence.
records.difference: 追い越す means to overtake and get ahead; 追いつく（おいつく） means to catch up.

records.nuance: 上昇（じょうしょう） means an upward increase. In this sentence, it describes Earth’s temperature rising; it does not state a cause or a rate.
records.logic: The compound is used for movement or change upward in level or amount; 気温 (temperature) selects the increase sense.
records.difference: 上昇 is a relatively formal noun; 上がる（あがる） is a common everyday verb meaning “go up/rise.”
records.filipino: pagtaas; pag-init ng temperatura ng daigdig

records.kanji_breakdown: 改 = check; 札 = ticket; 口 = opening
records.nuance: 改札口（かいさつぐち） is the ticket gate or gate area where tickets are checked at a station. It is not the station entrance in general.
records.logic: The word refers to the passage/gate associated with ticket inspection; で marks it as the meeting place.
records.difference: 改札口 is the ticket-checking gate; 駅の入口（えきのいりぐち） is a station entrance.
records.filipino: lagusan sa istasyon kung saan sinusuri ang mga tiket

records.nuance: 失礼（しつれい） literally suggests a lapse of courtesy, but 失礼します is a polite set phrase used when taking one’s leave. Here it means the speaker is excusing themself to go.
records.logic: ではそろそろ frames a polite departure; します is part of the conventional expression, not a claim that the speaker is being rude.
records.meaning: excuse me; I’ll be leaving (polite set phrase)
records.difference: 失礼します is used when departing; 失礼しました often apologizes for a discourtesy already made.

records.nuance: かゆい describes an irritating itchy sensation on the skin. The sentence locates it on the speaker’s back; the word itself does not mean pain.
records.logic: 背中が is the body part that feels itchy, a common pattern with this adjective.
records.difference: かゆい is an itch; 痛い（いたい） is pain or soreness.

records.nuance: お礼（おれい） means thanks or an expression of gratitude. In this sentence it is a thank-you letter written to her; it does not imply a payment or reward.
records.logic: 手紙 (letter) specifies how gratitude is expressed. お is the conventional polite prefix in this noun.
records.difference: お礼 is gratitude/thanks; お詫び（おわび） is an apology.

records.nuance: 謝る（あやまる） means to apologize or ask forgiveness for a wrong. 直ぐに means immediately; the sentence gives no recipient or details of the offense.
records.logic: The verb describes the act of apologizing; the reading あやまる distinguishes this vocabulary item from other readings/uses of 謝.
records.difference: 謝る is apologize; 叱る（しかる） is to scold someone.

records.kanji_breakdown: 注 = pour; 射 = shoot; inject
records.nuance: 注射（ちゅうしゃ） means an injection or shot. The sentence says he is not very fond of injections, not necessarily that he is afraid of them.
records.logic: The established compound refers to injecting medicine or another liquid into the body with a syringe; 好きではありません expresses dislike.
records.difference: 注射 refers to an injection; 薬（くすり） is medicine generally and need not be injected.

records.nuance: 程度（ていど） means level, degree, or extent. この程度の怪我なら means “if it is an injury of this degree”; the Japanese does not identify whose condition is fine or specify a gender.
records.logic: この points to the present degree/extent, and なら sets a condition. The deck’s “small extent” and “she” are translation choices not explicit in Japanese.
records.difference: 程度 names a degree or extent; 少し（すこし） directly means “a little.”
records.filipino: kung ganito lang kalubha ang pinsala, ayos lang

records.nuance: ぐらぐら describes something swaying or shaking without stability. With 揺れた and a house shaken by an earthquake, it conveys pronounced wobbling; it can describe other kinds of instability in other contexts.
records.logic: 地震で gives the cause and 家が marks the thing shaken. ぐらぐらと modifies 揺れた.
records.difference: ぐらぐら suggests unstable, repeated movement; ゆらゆら often suggests a gentler, swaying motion.
records.filipino: umuga nang malakas ang bahay dahil sa lindol

records.nuance: 誘う（さそう） means to invite or encourage someone to join an activity. デートに makes the activity a date here; it does not imply that this was a first date.
records.logic: 彼女を is the person invited, and デートに marks what she was invited to do. The verb takes a direct object here.
records.meaning: to invite; to ask someone to join
records.difference: 誘う is to invite/encourage someone; 招待する（しょうたいする） is more specifically to invite as a guest, often formally.

records.nuance: 導入（どうにゅう） means introducing, bringing in, or adopting something for use. Here a company adopted a new system; the sentence does not say how it was implemented.
records.logic: 新しいシステムを is the object, and 会社で gives the setting. The word is a conventional compound, not a claim that a system is literally guided inside.
records.difference: 導入 is used for bringing a system or method into use; 紹介（しょうかい） is introducing or presenting a person/thing to someone.
records.filipino: pagpapakilala at paggamit ng bagong sistema

records.nuance: 努力（どりょく） means sustained effort toward a goal. もっと努力しよう is an invitation to make more effort or work harder together.
records.logic: The compound names exerting effort toward an aim; しよう is the volitional form “let’s do.”
records.difference: 努力 focuses on exertion toward a goal; 練習（れんしゅう） specifically means practice.

records.nuance: 怒る（おこる） means to become or be angry in this sentence. A second reading, いかる, also exists; preserve the note’s exact reading おこる. The cause is her lie; Japanese does not say whom she lied to, although the deck English adds “to him.” 怒った means he became angry; it does not say he scolded her.
records.logic: The reason clause 彼女が嘘をついたので explains why he got angry; 怒った is the past form of おこる.
records.meaning: to get angry; to be angry
records.difference: 怒る（おこる） means become/be angry and can sometimes mean scold; 叱る（しかる） specifically means to scold or reprimand.
records.filipino: nagalit ang lalaki dahil nagsinungaling ang babae

records.nuance: ジャム means fruit preserve/jam. このイチゴで means strawberries are the ingredient or material used to make it.
records.logic: で marks the material, while 作りましょう is “let’s make.” No special kanji breakdown applies because the word is written in katakana.
records.difference: ジャム is fruit preserve; ゼリー is jelly/gel dessert and may be made from juice.

records.nuance: 独身（どくしん） means unmarried or without a spouse. まだ means “still”; it does not say the speaker’s brother lives alone or whether he is dating someone.
records.logic: The compound is conventionally used for marital status; learn its established meaning rather than treating it as a literal description of being physically alone.
records.difference: 独身 describes not having a spouse; 一人暮らし（ひとりぐらし） means living alone.
records.filipino: wala pang asawa ang kuya ko

records.nuance: 占める（しめる） means to make up or account for a share of a whole here. The Japanese says junk mail makes up 70 percent of the mail that reaches the speaker.
records.logic: 迷惑メールが is the subject and 7割を占めている states its proportion within the incoming email.
records.meaning: to account for; to make up (a proportion)
records.difference: 占める can mean to occupy a place or position; with a proportion such as 7割, it means to constitute that share.

records.nuance: 処理（しょり） means handling or processing something to deal with it. 事務的な処理 is administrative processing; the sentence says it takes one week.
records.logic: に1週間かかります means “takes one week for”; no person doing the processing or reason for its duration is specified.
records.difference: 処理 is handling work or matter to completion; 手続き（てつづき） focuses on the procedure or required formal steps.

records.nuance: 紹介（しょうかい） means introducing or presenting someone to another person. 両親に彼女を紹介した says the speaker introduced a girlfriend/partner to their parents; 彼女 can mean “she” or “girlfriend,” and this context supports girlfriend.
records.logic: 彼女を is the person introduced; 両親に marks who she was introduced to.
records.difference: 紹介する is to introduce someone or something; 招待する（しょうたいする） is to invite someone to an event or place.
records.filipino: ipinakilala ko ang kasintahan ko sa mga magulang ko

records.nuance: スリッパ means slippers, especially the open indoor footwear commonly worn in Japanese homes. はいてください is a polite request to put them on.
records.logic: The verb 履く（はく） is used for footwear worn on the feet; the katakana word is a loanword and has no kanji breakdown.
records.difference: スリッパ are typically indoor slippers; 靴（くつ） is general footwear, especially shoes worn outdoors.

records.nuance: 招く（まねく） means to invite someone as a guest. 両親を食事に招いた means the speaker invited their parents to a meal; the verb can have other senses such as causing an outcome, but not here.
records.logic: 両親を is the invited person and 食事に gives the occasion. The past form 招いた describes the invitation.
records.difference: 招く is a verb meaning invite/ask someone to come; 招待（しょうたい） is the noun “invitation” or the act of inviting a guest.
records.filipino: inanyayahan ko ang mga magulang ko sa kainan

records.nuance: 招待（しょうたい） means inviting someone as a guest, often to an event. Here the speaker invited a former high-school teacher to a wedding.
records.logic: 結婚式に marks the event; 招待した is the past form of 招待する, “invite as a guest.”
records.meaning: invitation; to invite as a guest
records.difference: 招待 emphasizes inviting a guest to an event; 紹介（しょうかい） means introducing someone to another person.
records.filipino: inanyayahan ko sa kasal ang dati kong guro noong high school

records.nuance: 夫婦（ふうふ） means a married couple, husband and wife. 仲がいい says the two get along very well; it does not say how long they have been married.
records.logic: その夫婦 refers to that married pair; とても仲がいい describes their good relationship.
records.difference: 夫婦 means a married couple; カップル may refer to a couple without specifying that they are married.

records.nuance: 奥（おく） means the inner or far part of a place. With a desk, 机の奥 is the back/farther-in part of the desk, not necessarily a drawer or the underside.
records.logic: 机の奥に marks a location within the desk’s depth; あった says the scissors were there.
records.difference: 奥 is the inner or far part; 前（まえ） is the front.

records.nuance: トランプ means playing cards in Japanese. トランプをして遊びました means the speaker played a card game with a friend; the exact game is not specified.
records.logic: 友達と marks the companion; をして遊ぶ is a common way to say that someone played a game/activity.
records.difference: トランプ refers to playing cards or a card game; カード can mean cards more broadly, including non-playing cards.
records.filipino: naglalaro ako ng baraha kasama ang isang kaibigan

records.kanji_breakdown: 奥 = inner part; さん = respectful title
records.nuance: 奥さん（おくさん） is a polite, familiar way to refer to another person’s wife. In this sentence it means his wife; the word is not normally used to refer to one’s own wife when speaking to others.
records.logic: 彼の identifies whose wife; きれいな方 is a polite way to describe her as beautiful.
records.difference: 奥さん refers respectfully to another person’s wife; 妻（つま） is the ordinary word for one’s own wife.

records.kanji_breakdown: 皆 = everyone; さん = respectful address
records.nuance: 皆さん（みなさん） means everyone or all of you, in a polite but fairly everyday form. 皆さんにお話があります means the speaker has something to say to everyone addressed.
records.logic: に marks the people being addressed; 皆さん is the audience, not the speaker.
records.difference: 皆さん is a polite everyday address to a group; 皆様（みなさま） is more formal and more deferential.
records.filipino: may sasabihin ako sa inyong lahat

records.kanji_breakdown: 皆 = everyone; 様 = respectful title
records.nuance: 皆様（みなさま） is a respectful, formal way to address everyone present or involved. It is commonly used in greetings and public announcements.
records.logic: The word addresses the audience directly; こんにちは is a greeting.
records.difference: 皆様 is more formal/deferential than 皆さん（みなさん）.
records.filipino: magandang araw po sa inyong lahat

records.nuance: 誰か（だれか） means someone or somebody. In a request, 誰かに聞いてみてください means “please try asking someone”; it does not identify who.
records.logic: 誰か is the person to ask, marked by に; 聞いてみる means try asking/checking with them.
records.difference: 誰か means an unspecified person; 誰（だれ） alone asks “who?”

records.nuance: よろしい（宜しい） is a polite form of よい, often meaning acceptable, suitable, or all right. In this question, the speaker asks whether the report is acceptable as it is.
records.logic: これで asks whether this version/state will do; ですか makes it a polite question.
records.difference: よろしい is polite/formal; いい is the everyday casual equivalent.
records.filipino: ayos na po ba ito bilang ulat?

records.nuance: 国籍（こくせき） means nationality or citizenship as a person’s legal affiliation with a country. 私は日本国籍です says “I have Japanese nationality”; “I’m a Japanese citizen” is a natural English rendering.
records.logic: 日本国籍 is the nationality/status; the Japanese sentence does not tell how the speaker acquired it or where they live.
records.difference: 国籍 is legal nationality/citizenship; 国民（こくみん） means a country’s people/citizens collectively or an individual citizen.

records.nuance: 愛（あい） is love or deep affection. 愛をこめて手紙を書いた means she wrote the letter with love/affection; this sentence does not specify that the love is romantic.
records.logic: 愛をこめて describes the feeling or care put into the act of writing; it does not necessarily describe the letter’s topic.
records.difference: 愛 is love/affection broadly; 恋（こい） often emphasizes romantic longing or being in love.
records.filipino: sumulat siya ng liham nang may pagmamahal

records.kanji_breakdown: 可 = can/acceptable (character cue); 愛 = love (character cue)
records.nuance: 可愛い（かわいい） means cute or endearing. Here it describes the speaker’s girlfriend/partner’s baby as cute; 可愛い is commonly written with these kanji, but the spelling is ateji and should not be read as a literal kanji formula.
records.logic: 彼女の赤ちゃん is the baby; 可愛いです expresses an affectionate positive judgment.
records.difference: 可愛い describes something as cute/endearing; 美しい（うつくしい） means beautiful, often emphasizing beauty rather than cuteness.

records.kanji_breakdown: 恋 = romantic longing; 人 = person
records.nuance: 恋人（こいびと） is a romantic partner or someone one loves. In this sentence he lost a romantic partner; Japanese does not specify that the person was female.
records.logic: 恋人 is the object of 失った; the past verb means he lost that person or relationship.
records.difference: 恋人 is gender-neutral; 彼女（かのじょ） can mean girlfriend but specifically identifies a female partner in that context.

records.kanji_breakdown: ラッシュアワー = rush hour
records.nuance: ラッシュアワー means rush hour, the busy commuting period when many people travel. The speaker dislikes trains during that period; the Japanese does not say they dislike all trains.
records.logic: ラッシュアワーの電車 means trains associated with rush hour; 嫌いです expresses dislike.
records.difference: ラッシュアワー is the commuting period; 通勤時間（つうきんじかん） can mean commuting time more broadly.
records.filipino: ayoko ng mga tren kapag rush hour

records.nuance: 誕生日（たんじょうび） is a person’s birthday—the calendar date of their birth. The sentence gives her birthday as July 16.
records.logic: 彼女の誕生日は…です identifies her birthday and states the date; the word does not itself mean a birthday party.
records.difference: 誕生日 is the birthday/date; 誕生日会（たんじょうびかい） is a birthday party.
records.filipino: ika-16 ng Hulyo ang kaarawan niya

records.nuance: 祝日（しゅくじつ） means a public holiday or holiday designated for celebration. The sentence simply states that May 3 is a holiday; it does not name the holiday in the vocabulary sentence.
records.logic: The date is the topic and 祝日だ predicates that it is a holiday.
records.difference: 祝日 is a holiday; 休日（きゅうじつ） is a day off more generally and need not be an official public holiday.

records.kanji_breakdown: 祝 = celebrate; お = polite prefix
records.nuance: お祝い（おいわい） means a celebration, congratulations, or a congratulatory observance. 就職のお祝い is celebrating someone’s getting a job; it can also refer to a congratulatory gift depending on context.
records.logic: 彼の就職の… marks the occasion, and しよう is “let’s”; the sentence proposes celebrating his new employment.
records.difference: お祝い can mean celebrating/congratulating or a gift for an occasion; お祭り（おまつり） is a festival.
records.filipino: ipagdiwang natin ang pagkakakuha niya ng trabaho

records.nuance: 夢（ゆめ） means a dream during sleep in 昨夜恐ろしい夢を見た. It can also mean a future hope in other contexts, but 昨夜 and 見た establish the sleep-dream sense.
records.logic: 夢を見る is the ordinary expression for having/experiencing a dream; 恐ろしい describes it as frightening.
records.difference: 夢 can mean a sleeping dream or an aspiration; 希望（きぼう） is hope/aspiration and does not mean a sleeping dream.

records.nuance: カップ means a cup or cup measure. In a water/ingredient instruction, 1カップ is one cup of liquid measure; the exact standard volume depends on the recipe convention and is not specified here.
records.logic: 水を1カップ入れてください asks the listener to add one cup of water; the word is written in katakana and has no kanji breakdown.
records.difference: カップ can mean a drinking cup or a measuring amount; コップ usually refers to a drinking glass/cup.

records.nuance: 泣く（なく） means to cry, often with tears or a crying voice. 妹はすぐに泣く says the younger sister cries quickly/soon; the deck’s “cries easily” is a natural interpretation but slightly broadens すぐに.
records.logic: すぐに means soon/quickly and describes how promptly she cries; it does not alone explain her reason or emotional sensitivity.
records.difference: 泣く（なく） is crying; 鳴く（なく）, a homophone, is used for animal or bird calls.
records.filipino: umiiyak agad ang nakababata kong kapatid na babae

records.nuance: 涙（なみだ） means tears. 彼女の目から涙がこぼれた describes tears spilling from her eyes; it does not state why she is crying.
records.logic: 目から marks where they came from, and こぼれる describes tears spilling or falling out.
records.difference: 涙 are tears; 泣く（なく） is the act of crying.
records.filipino: tumulo ang mga luha mula sa kanyang mga mata

records.nuance: 喜ぶ（よろこぶ） means to feel glad or delighted. The sentence says she was very happy, but does not specify what caused her happiness.
records.logic: とても intensifies the degree; the past form 喜びました reports her reaction.
records.difference: 喜ぶ describes feeling glad; 嬉しい（うれしい） is an adjective meaning happy/glad.

records.nuance: 恥ずかしい（はずかしい） describes feeling embarrassed, ashamed, or self-conscious. The sentence only says the feeling was strong; it does not say what caused it.
records.logic: とても marks the intensity and かった makes the adjective past tense.
records.difference: 恥ずかしい is the feeling of embarrassment; 恥（はじ） is shame or disgrace, often naming the concept rather than the feeling.

records.nuance: スケート means skating; in a sentence about doing it on a lake, it naturally suggests ice skating on a frozen lake. The sentence does not explicitly describe the ice or type of skating.
records.logic: 湖で marks where the activity took place; スケートをした means went skating.
records.difference: スケート here is skating on a lake; スキー（skiing） is sliding on snow with skis.

records.kanji_breakdown:
弁 = speech; distinguish
当 = hit; appropriate
records.nuance: 弁当（べんとう） is a prepared meal packed to take along, commonly a lunch box. In this sentence the speaker says they brought a bento today; it does not explicitly say when they will eat it.
records.logic: 弁当（べんとう） is a conventional word for a meal packed to take along. The character cues here are not a literal explanation of the modern compound; learn the established word as a whole.
records.difference: 弁当 is a packed meal; 食事（しょくじ） means a meal generally and need not be packed.
records.filipino: may dala akong baon ngayong araw

records.kanji_breakdown: 看 = watch; 護 = care/protect; 師 = professional
records.nuance: 看護師（かんごし） is a nurse who provides nursing care. The word does not specify gender; the sentence says the speaker’s mother has this occupation.
records.logic: The established compound names a nursing professional; 母は identifies the speaker’s mother as the topic.
records.difference: 看護師 is a nurse; 医師（いし） is a physician/doctor.

records.nuance: 患者（かんじゃ） means a patient receiving medical care. The sentence says the patient is asleep; it gives no information about the illness or treatment.
records.logic: 患者は is the topic and 眠っています describes the current state of sleeping.
records.difference: 患者 is someone receiving treatment; 医師（いし） is the doctor providing it.

records.nuance: 述べる（のべる） means to state or express an opinion, usually in a relatively formal or organized way. The sentence says the supervisor stated an opinion; it does not reveal what it was.
records.logic: 上司が is the speaker of the opinion, and 意見を is what was expressed.
records.difference: 述べる is often more formal or deliberate than 言う（いう）, the general verb “say.”
records.filipino: inilahad ng boss ang kanyang opinyon

records.kanji_breakdown: たくさん = many; much; a lot
records.nuance: たくさん means a lot or plenty. 昨日はたくさん泳ぎました says the speaker swam a lot yesterday; it does not specify distance or time.
records.logic: 昨日 sets the action in the past; たくさん indicates a large amount of swimming.
records.difference: たくさん is a general “a lot”; 少し（すこし） means a little.

records.nuance: 訴える（うったえる） means to sue in court in this sentence. 彼女は会社を訴えた says she sued the company; other contexts can mean to complain or appeal, but 会社を as the object fits the legal sense.
records.logic: 会社を is the defendant/object of the lawsuit; 訴えた is the past form.
records.meaning: to sue; to bring a case against
records.difference: 訴える can mean sue or appeal/complain; 告訴する（こくそする） is a more specific/formal word for filing a criminal complaint.

records.kanji_breakdown: 迷 = lose one’s way; be uncertain
records.nuance: 迷う（まよう） means to lose one’s way here. 道に迷いました is a common expression for getting lost; it does not say where or for how long.
records.logic: 道に identifies the path/route where the speaker became lost; 迷いました is polite past tense.
records.meaning: to get lost; to lose one’s way
records.difference: 道に迷う means get lost; 迷子（まいご） is a lost child/person.

records.kanji_breakdown: 迷 = bewildered; 惑 = confused (character cues)
records.nuance: 迷惑（めいわく） means trouble or inconvenience caused to another person. 人に迷惑をかけてはいけません means you must not cause trouble for others.
records.logic: 人に marks who is affected; 迷惑をかける is the fixed expression “cause trouble/inconvenience.”
records.difference: 迷惑 is trouble caused to or felt by someone; 困る（こまる） means to be troubled or not know what to do.
records.filipino: huwag magdulot ng abala sa ibang tao

records.nuance: 地域（ちいき） means an area or region. この地域は雨が多い says this area gets a lot of rain; it does not define the area’s boundaries or explain the rainfall.
records.logic: この地域 is the place being discussed; 雨が多い describes its climate/weather pattern.
records.difference: 地域 is an area/region; 地方（ちほう） often means a broader locality or part of a country.

records.nuance: ピクニック means a picnic—an outing that typically includes eating outdoors. The sentence invites the listener to go on one today; it does not say where or what food they will bring.
records.logic: に行きましょう is “let’s go to/for”; 今日は sets the proposed day.
records.difference: ピクニック is an outing often involving food outdoors; 散歩（さんぽ） is a walk and need not be an outing or meal.

records.nuance: 政権（せいけん） means political power or the government/administration exercising it. 政権が交代した means power changed hands; it does not identify which party or leader took over.
records.logic: 政権 is the topic, and 交代した reports a change or transfer.
records.difference: 政権 refers to governing power/administration; 政府（せいふ） more directly means the government as an organization.

records.nuance: 贈る（おくる） means to give something as a gift, often with gratitude or celebration in mind. The speaker gave flowers to their mother; it does not say why or for what occasion.
records.logic: 母に marks the recipient and 花を the gift; the verb is transitive.
records.meaning: to give as a gift; to present
records.difference: 贈る means give as a gift; 送る（おくる） means send or see someone off, though the pronunciations are the same.
records.filipino: binigyan ko ng mga bulaklak ang nanay ko

records.kanji_breakdown: 贈 = give as a gift; 物 = thing
records.nuance: 贈り物（おくりもの） means a gift or present. The speaker thanks someone for a lovely gift; neither its giver nor occasion is specified.
records.logic: すてきな describes the gift positively; どうもありがとう expresses thanks.
records.difference: 贈り物 is a gift; お土産（おみやげ） is a souvenir or gift brought from a trip/place.

records.nuance: 与える（あたえる） means to give or cause an effect. Here the news gave him a major shock; it is the news’ impact, not a physical object being handed over.
records.logic: そのニュースは is the cause/topic, 彼に marks the affected person, and 大きなショックを is what it caused.
records.meaning: to give; to cause; to have an effect on
records.difference: 与える can describe giving or causing an effect; 受ける（うける） describes receiving/experiencing that effect.
records.filipino: labis siyang nagulat sa balitang iyon

records.kanji_breakdown: あちら = over there; that direction
records.nuance: あちら is a polite or less direct way to say “over there” or “that way.” In this suggestion, it means going in that direction to take a look.
records.logic: あちらに marks the destination/direction; 行ってみよう means “let’s try going.”
records.difference: あちら is more polite/distant than そこ（そこ）, “there” near the listener.

records.nuance: 貯金（ちょきん） means money saved by setting it aside, or the act of saving money. 貯金は十分にあります says there are enough savings; it does not specify an account or amount.
records.logic: 十分にあります describes the savings as sufficient; the sentence’s topic is the saved money.
records.difference: 貯金 means savings or saving money; 収入（しゅうにゅう） is income received.

records.nuance: 預ける（あずける） means to entrust or leave something in someone else’s care. Here the speaker entrusted a key to him; this does not say that he owns or may keep it permanently.
records.logic: 鍵を is the thing entrusted and 彼に is the person receiving it temporarily.
records.meaning: to entrust; to leave in someone’s care
records.difference: 預ける is to entrust something; 預かる（あずかる） is to take and keep something in one’s care.
records.filipino: ipinagkatiwala ko sa kanya ang susi

records.kanji_breakdown: 預 = keep in custody; take charge
records.nuance: 預かる（あずかる） means to take charge of or keep something entrusted to you. 荷物を預かってください asks someone to look after the luggage; it does not say for how long.
records.logic: 荷物を is the object to be kept; ください makes a polite request.
records.meaning: to keep; to look after; to take custody of
records.difference: 預かる is to receive and keep in one’s care; 預ける（あずける） is to entrust something to someone else.

records.kanji_breakdown: 得 = acquire; 意 = intention/skill (character cues)
records.nuance: 得意（とくい） means being good at or confident in an activity. 歌が得意です says he is good at singing; it does not say he is a professional singer.
records.logic: 歌が marks the skill, and 得意です describes his aptitude/confidence in it.
records.difference: 得意 means good at something; 好き（すき） means liking it, which does not necessarily mean being skilled.

records.nuance: どきどき describes a pounding heartbeat, often from nervousness, excitement, or anticipation. The sentence says meeting her brings on that feeling but does not specify which emotion or the relationship.
records.logic: 彼女に会うと sets the trigger (“when [I] meet her”); どきどきします describes the resulting heartbeat/feeling.
records.meaning: heart pounding; to feel one’s heart race
records.difference: どきどき often describes a pounding heart from excitement or nerves; わくわく emphasizes eager anticipation.
records.filipino: kinakabahan o nasasabik ako kapag nakikita ko siya

records.nuance: 燃える（もえる） means to burn or be on fire. 山が燃えています says the mountain is burning now; it does not specify the cause or scale of the fire.
records.logic: 山が is the thing burning, so this is the intransitive verb; ています describes an ongoing state/activity.
records.meaning: to burn; to be on fire
records.difference: 燃える is intransitive (“burn/be on fire”); 燃やす（もやす） is transitive (“burn something”).

records.nuance: 焼ける is intransitive: the meat becomes cooked/done. In this sentence, 焼けました reports the result; it need not mean the meat was burned.
records.logic: The meat is the thing undergoing the change: it has reached a cooked state.
records.meaning: be cooked; be done; burn (in other contexts)
records.difference: 焼ける describes something becoming cooked; 焼く（やく） means someone cooks or grills it.

records.kanji_breakdown: すき焼き = sukiyaki, a Japanese hot-pot dish
records.nuance: すき焼き is a dish, commonly made with beef and vegetables cooked in a sweet-savory sauce. The sentence only says the speaker ate sukiyaki last night.
records.logic: Treat すき焼き as the established name of the dish; do not infer its history from the kanji spelling.
